What are valid and invalid reasons for filing a dispute?

SoundCloud sees many reasons given as the basis for disputes but a lot of these reasons are not legally valid. Below are some of the common reasons for filing a dispute, along with an explanation of why it is valid or is not valid. Please note that any dispute filed based on an invalid reason as listed below will be rejected by SoundCloud’s Copyright Team. #### Valid reasons for filing a dispute ##### My original content was blocked If you are signed to a label that is distributed by a digital distributor, that digital distributor may have delivered that content to our content ID system for protection.  We will need to work with them to resolve the situation.  If your upload is blocked for matching your own content, we encourage you to file a dispute so that the issue can be resolved.  There are also steps that can be taken when resolving a dispute to avoid the situation from happening in the future.  Our team can advise on this when filing a dispute. ##### I have permission from the copyright owner If you used someone else’s work but you have explicit permission from the rightsholder to upload that content, you are encouraged to file a dispute so that the issue can be resolved.  When filing a dispute, please provide adequate details about your rights and/or permissions for our Copyright Team to review. ##### My track was misidentified and blocked for matching something else Our content ID system uses multiple layers of audio fingerprinting technology, but no technology is perfect.  Sometimes tracks are blocked for matching something entirely different from your upload.  If this happens, we encourage you to file a dispute to let us know that a mistake has been made.  Please be sure to provide enough detail about your rights that our Copyright Team can properly process your dispute. ##### Your use falls under fair use or a copyright exception If you believe that your use of someone else’s work falls under fair use or a copyright exception, we would encourage you to let us know.  Please keep in mind that such a determination is case-specific, so please be sure to provide plenty of details as to why you feel your work is allowable to help our Copyright Team review. #### Invalid reasons for filing a dispute ##### I bought the track online and/or own the CD or vinyl Buying a digital or physical copy of a track does not include the right to share that track on SoundCloud. Online distribution is a right that belongs to the copyright owner and is not automatically transferred to you with your digital or physical purchase. ##### I only used a small part of the copyrighted work Generally, you always need permission to post someone else’s work on SoundCloud, whether it’s the entire work or just a small part (e.g. a sample).   We have heard from some of our users that they believed they could legally sample someone else’s work if they used less than 30 seconds or some other small amount.  This is not always true.  Using this content without permission may still be infringing. ##### I’m not earning any money from it As mentioned above, you always need permission to use someone else’s work, regardless of whether you are making money from it. ##### Other tracks on SoundCloud contain the same copyrighted content Permission to use or publish copyright-protected material is generally granted on a case-by-case basis by the copyright owner(s). The fact that someone else may have permission to use the same content does not mean that it is freely available for everyone to use. A separate license has to be obtained for each use and user. ##### I got it as a free download and want to share it Some creators may give away their album or track as a free download.  Generally that gives you the right to download and listen to it only. That doesn’t mean you can post it on SoundCloud.  You still need permission from all copyright owner(s) even if they have made the track available for free elsewhere. Additionally, if you have received a promotional copy from a label, we would encourage you to ensure that the rights granted include the right to share on SoundCloud.  If your permissions with a promotional copy do not explicitly state that the content can be shared on SoundCloud, then unfortunately that track can’t be shared here and your dispute will be rejected. ##### I credited the original creator Crediting the original creator is not a substitute for the permission required to upload their content. You still need permission, usually granted in the form of a license, from the copyright owner(s) even if you give them credit. ##### I’m a big fan of the artist and want everyone to hear their music We all love to share the music that we enjoy.  Our community is part of what makes SoundCloud unique.  However, most creators want control over where and how their content appears.  Their label or distributor may also have a say in how the content is shared.  If the content is already on SoundCloud, you can share with your audience by “reposting” instead of uploading on your own.  If you don’t have permission from all copyright owners, including the label and/or distributor if relevant, to post the track then you should not be uploading their content.

What is a dispute?

Whenever a track is taken down for copyright infringement, you have the possibility to contest the takedown via our online dispute process. 

A dispute is your opportunity to let us know if you have rights and permissions in place for a track that has been blocked for copyright infringement. You can file a dispute against a copyright takedown if you believe that your track has been removed incorrectly.

To file a dispute, you can fill in our form, where you’ll be asked to describe your rights to the track that has been blocked, and our Copyright Team will review your claim. #### What would you like to learn more about? Please note: The Copyright team does not respond to questions or enquiries submitted in the dispute process. The information you provide is solely used for assessing your claim.

Copyright for SoundCloud Creators: Reporting Copyright Infringement

How do I report content on SoundCloud that infringes my copyright?

If you identify any tracks on SoundCloud that you believe infringe your copyright, you can let us know using any of the methods explained here.  Before making a report concerning any possible copyright infringement, please consider the following: - These infringement reporting methods should be used for copyright infringement only. If you wish to make a report concerning trademark infringement or any other rights, please email us at legal@soundcloud.com. - Please only report infringement of your own copyright, or the copyright of someone you are authorized to represent. Reporting content that does not belong to you may result in the suspension or termination of your account. You may also be liable for damages (including costs and legal fees) incurred by SoundCloud, the person whose sounds you report, or any copyright owner or authorized licensee as a result of sounds being removed.  If you believe that someone else’s copyright is being infringed, you are encouraged to tell them and direct them to this page. - Please do not report copyright infringement unless you have a genuine claim. If you make groundless or malicious reports of copyright infringement, you risk having your account suspended or terminated. You may also be liable for damages (including costs and legal fees) incurred by SoundCloud, the person whose tracks you report, and/or any copyright owner or authorized licensee, as a result of tracks being removed in reliance on your notice. - Please provide details. The more information we have regarding your claim, the quicker we can process your notice.

How you can report to us:

Report form

You can file a report using our Report Form.  Please note that you will need to be logged in to your SoundCloud account to use this feature. ##### Using the report button Each track page has a button entitled “Report,” which you can use to report the track on that page.  The button is located on the left side of the track page, under the name of the user uploading. ##### By writing to us The report button and the report form are the most efficient ways to report copyright infringement.  However, if you would prefer to send your own notification, you may do so in writing, making sure that you include the following information: - a statement that you have identified tracks on SoundCloud which infringe your copyright or the copyright of a third party on whose behalf you are entitled to act; - a description of the copyright work(s) that you claim have been infringed; - a description of the sound(s) that you claim are infringing and the specific track URL(s) where such tracks can be located; - your full name, address, and telephone number, a valid email address at which you can be contacted, and your SoundCloud username if you have one; - a statement that you have a good faith belief that the disputed use of the material is not authorized by the copyright owner, its agent, or the law; - a statement that the information in your notice is accurate and that you are the owner of the exclusive right that is allegedly infringed or authorized to act on their behalf;

In addition, if you wish for your notice to be considered as a notice pursuant to the United States Digital Millennium Copyright Act 17 U.S.C. §512(c), please also include the following: - with respect to your statement that you are the owner of the exclusive right that is allegedly infringed (or authorized to act on their behalf), confirmation that such statement is made under penalty of perjury; and - your electronic or physical signature (which may be a scanned copy).

Your notice should be sent to us by email to** **copyright@soundcloud.com and/or by mail to the following address:

SoundCloud Global Limited & Co. KG Karl Marx Str. 101 12043 Berlin Germany  Attn: Copyright Team

If you wish for your notice to be considered as a notice pursuant to the United States Digital Millennium Copyright Act 17 U.S.C. §512(c), your notice should be sent to SoundCloud’s designated copyright agent by email to copyrightagent@soundcloud.com and/or by mail to the following address:

SoundCloud Operations, Inc. 71 5th Avenue, 3rd Floor New York, NY 10003 USA Attn: Copyright Agent

Reporting infringement of someone else’s content

The short answer to this question is no.  There are a variety of reasons that you should not report content that you do not own. First, reporting content that does not belong to you is a violation of our Terms of Use.  We view reports of content that you do not own as abusive and there may be penalties on your account, including having your account frozen or suspended. Second, if the reported content is incorrectly removed, you can be liable for damages (including costs and legal fees) incurred by SoundCloud, the person whose sounds you reported, or any copyright owner or authorized licensee as a result of sounds being removed. Third, music licensing is complicated.  It may not always be clear what is infringing and what is not without being the rightsholder and knowing who has obtained the required licenses and/or permissions.  Your report may be for legitimately licensed content. We understand that these reports usually aren’t malicious and you’re only trying to help, but this is a matter for the rightsholder to resolve.  If you see content that you do not own that you believe is infringing, you may get in touch with the rightsholder(s) who can enforce their rights as necessary.

Reporting infringement of your images

If you would like to report infringement of your image’s use on SoundCloud, please email our Copyright Team through the contact button at the bottom of this article, and fill out the information below. 1. The full playback URL of the page(s) concerned where the image is located 2. Your full name, address, email and telephone number 3. Explain how the image(s) infringe(s) your copyright 4. Include the following statement: “I have a good faith belief that use of the copyrighted work described above is not authorized by the copyright owner (or by a third party who is legally entitled to do so on behalf of the copyright owner) and is not otherwise permitted by law. I hereby confirm that I believe the image(s) identified in this email infringe(s) my copyright.” 5. Scanned copy of your physical signature

In accordance with the Digital Millennium Copyright Act (DMCA), we only accept copyright complaints from content owners or someone officially authorized to act on their behalf.

By submitting a takedown request, you consent to having your information revealed to parties involved in the case.

Reporting infringement of your tracks

I have a SoundCloud account, and I’d like to report infringement of my tracks

If you’d like content that infringes your copyright to be removed from SoundCloud, please sign into your SoundCloud account and fill in the relevant information in our takedown request form here.

You can also reach this form by clicking the ‘Report’ button below any track’s waveform. #### I don’t have a SoundCloud account, but I’d like to report infringement of my tracks If you do not have a SoundCloud account, please email our Copyright Team through the contact form at the bottom of this article with the information below filled out: 1. The full playback URL of the track(s) concerned 2. Your full name, address, email and telephone number 3. Explain how the track(s) infringe(s) your copyright 4. Include the following statement: “I have a good faith belief that use of the copyrighted work described above is not authorized by the copyright owner (or by a third party who is legally entitled to do so on behalf of the copyright owner) and is not otherwise permitted by law. I hereby confirm that I believe the track(s) identified in this email infringe(s) my copyright.” 5. Scanned copy of your physical signature

In accordance with the Digital Millennium Copyright Act (DMCA), we only accept copyright complaints from content owners or someone officially authorized to act on their behalf.

By submitting this takedown form, you consent to having your information revealed to parties involved in the case.

Copyright for SoundCloud Creators: Takedowns by Content Type

My own content was flagged for copyright infringement and blocked

It can be frustrating when your original content is blocked on SoundCloud because the system mistakenly flags it as copyrighted, even if you own the rights. Though it may seem like an error, this system protects your work from unauthorized uploads and helps prevent others from uploading your music without permission.’ #### Why your own content may be blocked There are a few common reasons your original content may be identified and blocked: 1. Your label or digital distributor submitted your content for protection

If you are signed to a label or work with a digital distributor, they may have delivered your tracks to SoundCloud’s content identification system to protect them. 2. If your artist or band name appears in the takedown notice, it likely means your label or distributor submitted it. In this case, your content is protected from unauthorized uploads, but your upload may be blocked until your rights are verified. 3. Your content was misidentified

Although our content identification system is advanced, it isn’t perfect. In some cases, original content may be misidentified and incorrectly flagged. 4. If you think your content was wrongly flagged, file a dispute with clear proof of ownership for our Copyright Team to review. 5. Your content was reported for infringement

If your track was reported directly by a rights holder, you may need to contact the reporting party to resolve the issue. 6. In such cases, SoundCloud cannot take sides, and the content will remain blocked to comply with copyright law. Contact us via our AI agent for more information about the infringement report.

How to get your track reinstated

If you are the rights holder and your content was blocked, the quickest way to resolve the issue is to file a dispute. When you submit a dispute, be sure to include:  1. Your artist or band name 2. Any relevant label or distributor information 3. Proof of ownership or permission, if available

After submission, our Copyright Team reviews the track’s metadata. If your profile clearly matches the rights holder, your track is usually reinstated quickly. If not, providing detailed info helps prove your authorization to upload. #### How to prevent this from happening again If your content is repeatedly blocked and you are working with a label or digital distributor, we recommend contacting them directly. They can authorize your SoundCloud account and ensure you’re able to upload your own music without being blocked in the future. In general, filing a dispute and coordinating with your label or distributor are usually the fastest ways to resolve the issue and prevent it from happening again.

A track in the public domain was taken down for copyright infringement

The vast majority of the material that is publicly available on the internet for free is NOT in the public domain. If you want to create something new based on publicly available material, it is your responsibility to find out whether the material you want to use falls in the public domain before making use of it. It is absolutely essential that you verify this, even if you are using someone else’s material for promotional purposes only or if you are not making any profit from its use.

Works that are in the public domain either fell out of copyright protection or are not eligible for copyright protection - such as federal government works in the US territory - or were gifted to the public domain by their creators. This type of works can be used without requesting permission from their creators. For any other work that does not fall in the public domain, you will certainly need the permission from the copyright holder(s) to do so.

What’s important to bear in mind is that copyright protection can vary from country to country and that when a track is uploaded to your account, it is available everywhere in the world. You should therefore make sure that the material you want to use has fallen in the public domain globally. #### For more information and guidance, here are two websites worth checking out: Public Domain Sherpa - General information about public domain, also from a US perspective

Out of Copyright - Provides a useful public domain calculator

If you are able to provide proof that the work you have uploaded on SoundCloud is globally available in the public domain, our Copyright Team is happy to manually review these permissions and reinstate the track onto your profile. Please sign into your account and fill out the disputes form here.

A track you bought was taken down for copyright infringement

In accordance with current copyright legislation, you can only upload content that you own the  appropriate licenses for with regard to that purpose. Purchasing a track does not transfer rights to publicly publish the track - either in original or in an edited way - without explicit permission. In order to be able to upload the track to SoundCloud, you would need to get in touch with the original’s copyright holder.

If you are able to provide proof that you do have permission from the original’s rights holders to publish their content on SoundCloud, our Copyright Team is happy to manually review these permissions and reinstate the track onto your profile. Please sign into your account and fill out the disputes form here. #### I uploaded the track as private, isn’t that okay? Even if it is for your own personal use, you won’t be allowed to upload a purchased track to your SoundCloud profile as a private track. Purchasing a track does not necessarily give you the right to upload it to an online platform or to make it available to a wider audience. As you may know it is still possible to share private tracks with other listeners. 

Remember to only upload content, both publicly and privately, that you own the copyright to or that you have the necessary rights holder permission to make a copy of and publish online. SoundCloud is using an automated content identification system that recognizes copyright protected content. If the system detects copyright protected material in a private upload, that content will be blocked.

A track you composed with someone else was taken down for copyright infringement

Everyone who has worked on a track owns parts of the copyright of that track, and you’ll need everyone’s approval before you can upload them to SoundCloud. 

For example, if you wrote the lyrics for the track, you own the copyright to them. However, if you did not create the beat or instrumental backing, then someone else owns the copyright for that and they can request that its publication be blocked if you do not have their permission. 

If you are able to provide proof that you do have permission from the original’s rights holders for their part of the track to publish their content on SoundCloud, our Copyright Team is happy to manually review these permissions and reinstate the track onto your profile. Please sign into your account and fill out the disputes form here.

You uploaded someone else’s track and it was taken down for copyright infringement

In accordance with current copyright legislation, you can only upload content for which you own the appropriate licenses or for which you obtained the permission from the copyright owner(s) for that purpose. Purchasing or downloading a track does not transfer rights to publicly publish the track - either in original or in an edited way - without explicit permission. In order to be able to upload the track to SoundCloud, you would need to get in touch with the original copyright holder(s).

If you are able to provide proof that you do have permission from the original rights holders to publish their track on SoundCloud, our Copyright Team is happy to manually review these permissions and reinstate the track onto your profile. Please sign into your account and fill out the disputes form here. #### I uploaded the track as private, isn’t that okay? Even if it is for your own personal use, you won’t necessarily be allowed to upload a track you don’t own the copyrights to to your SoundCloud profile as a private track. Buying or downloading a track does not necessarily give you the right to upload it to an online platform or to make it available to a wider audience. As you may know it is still possible to share private tracks with other listeners.

Remember to only upload content, both publicly and privately, that you own the copyright to or that you have the necessary rights holder permission to make a copy of and publish online. SoundCloud is using an automated content identification system that recognizes copyright protected content. If the system detects copyright protected material in a private upload, that content will be blocked.

Your cover version was taken down for copyright infringement

Based on current copyright legislation, you always need permissions or the appropriate licenses if you would like to cover a copyrighted song in public , as is the case when publishing a track on SoundCloud. Permissions or licenses may be needed for both the composition rights and the sound recording rights, depending on whether you’re using a part of an original sound recording or have provided the vocals and played all the instruments.

While some producers and publishers are fine with third parties using their material, some others are not and do not want their works used or altered without explicit consent.

 If you are able to provide proof that you do have permission from the relevant rights holders or that you obtained all necessary licenses to publish your cover version on SoundCloud, our Copyright Team is happy to manually review these permissions and reinstate the track onto your profile. Please sign into your account and fill out the disputes form here. #### I uploaded my cover under Creative Commons, why was it still taken down? Creative Commons is a non-profit organization that has drafted a set of copyright licenses that may be used by any creator for any of their content. With Creative Commons licenses, creators have the choice to give up certain exclusive rights normally associated with copyright, while retaining others.  

Although you, as the creator of the cover have chosen to give up certain of these exclusive rights associated with copyright, the original creator of the track you used still owns the copyright for the original track, and you will need their explicit permission to publish your cover version on SoundCloud. #### I uploaded my cover for non-commercial purposes, doesn’t this qualify as fair use? Fair use is a legal doctrine that primarily exists in the copyright law of the United States. Fair use limits the exclusive rights granted by copyright and allows the use of copyrighted material  for certain limited purposes only, without requiring permission from the rights holder and depending on the exact use of the original work to be determined on a case by case basis.  Purposes recognized under fair use may be such as criticism, comment, news reporting, teaching and similar activities.    ​

However, uploading a cover version of a track for non-commercial and promotional purposes to SoundCloud does not fall within the fair use exemption.

Your DJ mix was taken down for copyright infringement

If you use parts of a track in a DJ set, please bear in mind that the original creator owns the copyright for that part in your track and, based on current copyright legislation, you will need their explicit permission to upload your DJ mix on SoundCloud.

Some producers and publishers are fine with others using their material in DJ sets, but some are not and do not want their works altered or distributed without their explicit consent.

If you are able to provide proof that you do have permission from the original rights holders to publish their material in your DJ mix on SoundCloud, our Copyright Team is happy to manually review these permissions and reinstate the track onto your profile. Please bear in mind that you should have permission to use all tracks that you have included in your DJ mix, and not just the one that has been detected by our content identification system. If you do not clearly specify and prove that all these permissions have been granted by their respective copyright holders (usually record labels and publishers), your dispute will be rejected.    

If you have all permissions in place, then sign into your account and fill out the dispute form here. Please link any available screenshots or images of permissions into the dispute form via a linking service. #### I uploaded my DJ mix under Creative Commons, why was it still taken down? Creative Commons is a non-profit organization that has drafted a set of copyright licenses that may be used by any creator for any of their content. With Creative Commons licenses, creators have the choice to give up certain exclusive rights normally associated with copyright, while retaining others.     Although you, as the creator of the DJ mix have chosen to give up certain of these exclusive rights associated with copyright, the original creator of the track you used still owns the copyright for that part in your mix, and you will need their explicit permission to publish your track on SoundCloud and to license your DJ mix, which includes the original creator’s track, under the Creative Commons License. #### I uploaded my DJ mix for non-commercial purposes, doesn’t this qualify as fair use? Fair use is a legal doctrine that primarily exists in the copyright law of the United States. Fair use limits the exclusive rights granted by copyright and allows the use of copyrighted material  for certain limited purposes only, without requiring permission from the rights holder and depending on the exact use of the original work to be determined on a case by case basis.  Purposes recognized under fair use may be such as criticism, comment, news reporting, teaching and similar activities.      ​

However, uploading a DJ mix for non-commercial and promotional purposes to SoundCloud does not fall within the fair use exemption.

Your entry for a remix competition or contest was taken down for copyright infringement

There are a couple of reasons why your remix entry may have been removed from SoundCloud. #### The competition or contest was not based on SoundCloud The first reason that your track was removed could be that the competition was not being run on the SoundCloud Platform. If that’s the case, then you wouldn’t necessarily have the right to upload your remix to SoundCloud if the organizers of the competition has not acquired the correct permissions for that purpose. #### The competition or contest has finished It’s possible that the rules of the competition state that entries must be removed from accounts once a competition finishes. So, if you didn’t remove your remix in time, it may have been reported for copyright infringement.

Always be sure to read the rules of the contest before you submit your entry, and bear in mind that SoundCloud does not run any remix competitions on SoundCloud platform - we don’t make the rules! #### The competition or contest is based on SoundCloud, and it hasn’t finished yet. What do I do? If you are able to provide proof that you do have permission from the competition/contest to publish their material in your remix on SoundCloud, our Copyright Team is happy to manually review these permissions and reinstate the track onto your profile. Please sign into your account and fill out the disputes form here.

Your mashup was taken down for copyright infringement

Since a mashup is based on other creators’ tracks, you’ll need to make sure that the copyright owners of the works you included in your mashup are fine with you using them in your upload to SoundCloud, even in their edited form. If you created your mashup based on tracks you have downloaded or found from other online sources, you will still need the content creator’s permission to upload it to your account - crediting the original creator does not count as permission.

If you are able to provide proof that you do have permission from the originals’ rights holders to publish their material in your mashup on SoundCloud, our Copyright Team is happy to manually review these permissions and reinstate the track onto your profile. Please sign into your account and fill out the disputes form here. #### I uploaded my mashup under Creative Commons, why was it still taken down? Creative Commons is a non-profit organization that has drafted a set of copyright licenses that may be used by any creator for any of their content. With Creative Commons licenses, creators have the choice to give up certain exclusive rights normally associated with copyright, while retaining others.  

Although you, as the creator of the mashup have chosen to give up certain of these exclusive rights associated with copyright, the original creator of the track you used still owns the copyright for that part in your mashup, and you will need their explicit permission to publish your track on SoundCloud. #### I uploaded my mashup for non-commercial purposes, doesn’t this qualify as fair use? Fair use is a legal doctrine that primarily exists in the copyright law of the United States. Fair use limits the exclusive rights granted by copyright and allows the use of copyrighted material  for certain limited purposes only, without requiring permission from the rights holder and depending on the exact use of the original work to be determined on a case by case basis.  Purposes recognized under fair use may be such as criticism, comment, news reporting, teaching and similar activities.      

​However, uploading a mashup for non-commercial and promotional purposes to SoundCloud does not fall within the fair use exemption.

Your radio show was taken down for copyright infringement

If your radio station has its own SoundCloud account and all necessary licenses covering master recordings rights and publishing rights for the specific use of their SoundCloud account, you might be able to upload your show to the radio station’s account.

When you would like to use SoundCloud to upload and stream a radio show that includes copyright protected music, there are a number of rights that need to be cleared before uploading your tracks to SoundCloud.

The following rights will need to be cleared: - master recording rights for all the tracks that are used in your upload - publishing rights for all the tracks that are used in your upload

Please be aware that in some cases multiple rights holders are involved in copyright ownership.

If you are able to provide proof that you do have permission from the original rights holders to use their material in your radio show on SoundCloud, our Copyright Team is happy to manually review these permissions and reinstate the track onto your profile. Please sign into your account and fill out the disputes form here.

Your remix was taken down for copyright infringement

Since your remix is based on another creator’s track, you’ll need permission from the original creator and any other relevant rights holders before you can upload and publish your remix online.

While some producers and publishers are fine with SoundCloud members using their material, some others are not and do not want their works used or altered without explicit consent.

 If you are able to provide proof that you do have permission from the original’s rights holders to publish your cover version on SoundCloud, our Copyright Team is happy to manually review these permissions and reinstate the track onto your profile. Please sign into your account and fill out the disputes form here. #### I uploaded my remix under Creative Commons, why was it still taken down? Creative Commons is a non-profit organization that has drafted a set of  copyright licenses that may be used by any creator for any of their content. With Creative Commons licenses, creators have the choice to give up certain exclusive rights normally associated with copyright, while retaining others.  

Although you, as the creator of the remix have chosen to give up certain of these exclusive rights associated with copyright, the original creator of the track you used still owns the copyright for the original track, and you will need their explicit permission to publish your cover version on SoundCloud. #### I uploaded my remix for non-commercial purposes, doesn’t this qualify as fair use? Fair use is a legal doctrine that primarily exists in the copyright law of the United States. Fair use limits the exclusive rights granted by copyright and allows the use of copyrighted material  for certain limited purposes only, without requiring permission from the rights holder and depending on the exact use of the original work to be determined on a case by case basis.  Purposes recognized under fair use may be such as criticism, comment, news reporting, teaching and similar activities.     

​However, uploading a remix for non-commercial and promotional purposes to SoundCloud does not fall within the fair use exemption.

Your spoken word podcast was taken down for copyright infringement

If you’re using music in your podcast, please be sure that it’s fully cleared and not infringing on anyone’s rights.

In accordance with current copyright legislation, you can only upload tracks for which you own the necessary licenses for. Purchasing a track to use it in your podcast does not automatically transfer rights to you to publicly publish the track in your podcast - neither in original nor in an edited way - without explicit permission. In order to be able to upload your podcast with the music in question to SoundCloud, you would need to get in touch with the original copyright holder. If you clear all content you use beforehand, you will avoid running into copyright infringement problems on the platform. Please also keep in mind that the SoundCloud Platform is available globally and that your licenses need to take account of that.

If you are able to provide proof that you do have permission from the original rights holders to use their material in your podcast on SoundCloud, our Copyright Team is happy to manually review these permissions and reinstate the track onto your profile. Please sign in to your account and fill out the disputes form here. #### Where can I find music to use in my future podcasts, so I don’t infringe on anyone’s copyright? ##### Online sound libraries You can find royalty-free and podsafe tracks from online sound libraries. These sound libraries offer tracks that may be used for different purposes depending on the specific license. Whereas some may be only made available for private download, others may be used in published projects, and they would be a great choice for you to use as a podcast introduction or transition music. If you find sounds you want to use from such libraries, please read their license terms to ensure that you can publish them on SoundCloud as part of your podcast. Please ensure the master recording as well as the publishing rights are covered in the license terms. ##### SoundCloud creators and Creative Commons You can get permission directly from the creator(s) in the case that they retain all rights to their music. Since you’re already on SoundCloud, feel free to search for tracks you like from creators on the platform. Using the Creative Commons search filters can help find available tracks, but we still recommend getting direct permission from the creator. You can reach out to creators directly via the messaging function and ask for their permission. If they aren’t the sole creator of the track or have assigned their rights to a recording company and/or to a publisher, please ensure that you get all the other rights holders’ permissions before using the content.

(image: fulllogo_transparent_nobuffer - Ari Salzberg.png) DataMind Audio is a pioneering company that operates at the intersection of professional music software and generative artificial intelligence (AI). Created by musicians for musicians, our mission is to produce innovative electronic instruments that leverage the power of generative AI to expand and augment human creativity and capability in sound design and music production. #### SoundCloud Exclusive Offer Enjoy 1 month free of all DataMind Audio instruments and models, Plus 20% off all products (Save $100–$245). *This free trial is only available through SoundCloud—you won’t find it anywhere else. #### DataMind Audio Product ##### Combobulator Our flagship product, Combobulator, is the first commercial plugin to bring neural audio synthesis to the DAW, using Audio Variational Auto-Encoders to synthesize an audio “style-transfer” in real-time from neural networks. #### Highlights: - Using AI models trained on the audio from world-class music producers, our plugin transforms a live audio signal to sound like the selected music producer’s stylistic palette. - All our data sets are ethically-sourced directly from the artists, sound designers, and music producers we work with. With your purchase of each model, artists make 50% of the gross profit from each sale. - Our newest Combobulator AI models are trained on foley sound libraries in collaboration with legendary sound effects studio Sound Ideas, perfect for sound in TV, Film, and Games. - Our latest plugin, Concatenator, uses AI to re-create an audio signal with a folder of samples, representing a major breakthrough in audio mosaic technology.

  2. Click on Sign in with Soundcloud
  3. The benefit will unlock for checkout.
How to use tools:

Combobulator: The Combobulator resynthesises an audio input signal by performing a timbral “style-transfer” on it. It uses a revolutionary new synthesis method, neural synthesis, to reinterpret real-time audio through a selected model (AKA “Artist Brain”, AKA Neural Network). Neural synthesis does not use samples. The neural synthesis engine synthesizes the output from scratch, based on what each model has “learned” about sound during model training. While the Combobulator functions like an audio effect, it is designed to be played as a neural synthesis instrument. Each model is like a “black box” that contains a universe of timbres that can only be explored by altering the input signal and modulating the latents, a neural synthesis concept we will clarify in section 2. Each model can be used to create drums, bass, textures, melodies, and harmonies, all together or individually. To use, simply load the Combobulator onto any audio track in your DAW as an audio effect. Select your model to hear your audio re-created with neural audio synthesis on playback. Tweak the controls, use the modulation controls on the right, and scroll through the presets to explore and modulate the neural network. Concatenator: Concatenator is a real-time “audio mosaicing” plugin that reconstructs a real-time audio signal using segments of a user-defined library of samples. It applies a machine learning algorithm to analyze pitch, amplitude, and spectral features of the input, then dynamically arranges matching fragments in real time. Through its blend of cutting-edge algorithms and a real-time engine, Concatenator streamlines the creation of audio mosaics, transforming extensive sample libraries into dynamic instruments or spontaneous collages. Unlike traditional granular synthesis, which often relies on randomness, Concatenator adopts a data-driven approach. This enables precise, automatic matching of the input signal with the loaded corpus (the “library” of sounds) while minimizing the need for manual editing. Key parameters such as polyphony, “particles,” and “variation” allow users to fine-tune how precisely Concatenator imitates the source audio. Familiar synthesis modulation features open up further creative possibilities. Concatenator’s low-latency processing— under 50 milliseconds—makes it suitable for live performance, interactive sound design, and studio production. ##### More About Combobulator and DataMind: DataMind Audio has just launched its innovative virtual instrument, the Combobulator v1.0, out of beta—introducing twice as many “Artist Brains” (audio worlds based on specific artists and producers) and powerful new audio sculpting features. This isn’t just another AI music tool; it’s a first-of-its-kind “neural audio synthesis” instrument that allows artists to explore and interact with the creative essence of a musician’s sonic mind. The Combobulator’s unique capabilities offer a new way for artists to engage with AI. It empowers creators to sculpt and shape sounds using features like Freeze, Encoder, Bend, and Dilation—unlocking radical sonic possibilities that blur the lines between human creativity and AI. Their sonic essence is captured as a massive map that can be explored, mined, and manipulated as far as the user’s creativity will take them. This is the first in a series of products aimed at creating a sustainable, artist-centered ecosystem supported by ethical AI. DataMind Audio’s mission is clear: to innovate the future of music and creativity by offering tools that support artists, rather than just recreating existing works. Artists who contribute to creating their “Artist Brains” receive 50% of the profits, ensuring a fair and sustainable model. ##### Press on DataMaind Audiocipher, DataMind Audio Combobulator: An Ethically Trained AI Plugin (and on Linkedin) Music Ally, UK startup DataMind Audio unveils ‘Combobulator’ AI instrument Kill the DJ, DataMind Audio Offers Artists an Ethical & Lucrative Way to Use AI in Its VST Plugin Music Connection, DATAMIND AUDIO LAUNCHES VIRTUAL A.I. Creators on SoundCloud: Audience Growth & Promotion

Amplify tracks to reach 100+ listeners

Zero plays on a track you’ve worked hard on is tough. Our audio algorithm, exclusive to SoundCloud, will recommend your newly uploaded tracks to listeners who are most likely to love them. The goal is to give your music the best chance by making sure new uploads are heard by real people during that critical post-release period. This feature is available now for all Artist and Artist Pro subscribers. Learn more** here. #### Quick Navigation: Which uploads are eligible? How do I get my eligible tracks heard by more fans? How many people are you going to be surfacing these new uploads to? Who are my tracks being surfaced to? Are these plays coming from bots? How does the “autoplay” algorithm work? What if I don’t want my track to be heard by lots of new fans? Who will be able to see these tracks? How will this impact my listening experience on SoundCloud? Can you turn this on or off as a listener? #### Which uploads are eligible?** - A public track - A music track (no podcasts, ASMR, or spoken word) - Under 10 minutes in length, but over 1 minute - Uploaded or made public within the last 14 days

We recommend up to 30 tracks per day per subscriber. If you upload more, only the first 30 will be considered. If your track is available to Go+ subscribers only, meaning your rightsholder has only made it available to these subscribers, it will not be eligible for our algorithm. Additionally, while our goal is to amplify and recommend every track uploaded by a subscriber, we do take into account things like track quality when surfacing to new fans. Please note: If your track was uploaded to SoundCloud through a distributor, please be aware that we cannot guarantee its eligibility for Amplify. #### How do I get my eligible tracks heard by more fans? To opt in to this feature, view any track page for a track that is eligible based on the criteria above. Below the track’s banner and waveform, you’ll see the option to enable here: #### How many people are you going to be surfacing these new uploads to? This update was designed to give your music the best chance possible. We start by recommending your tracks to around 100 people with listener profiles that align with your sound. Note that while we can amplify your track to people, we can’t force them to listen all the way through. So this does not mean every track is guaranteed 100 listens. #### Who are my tracks being surfaced to? Are these plays coming from bots? We’re not showing tracks to random accounts - we’re matching them up to listeners who are likely to love them based on their use of autoplay, user activity, and listening history. This naturally weeds out bots, which typically don’t have this type of data available. Creators are limited to a total of 30 uploads for recommendations per day. #### How does the “autoplay” algorithm work? Our autoplay algorithm helps connect fans with similar tastes based on indicators from their user activity and listening history. So, for example, if a user is a huge fan of Digicore, your Digicore tracks could show up in their autoplay. Find out more about autoplay here. #### What if I don’t want my track to be heard by lots of new fans? If you don’t want your track to be discoverable, you can always upload a private link and share directly with fans and collaborators. Publicly uploaded tracks have always been and will continue to be eligible for inclusion in SoundCloud’s autoplay and recommendation algorithms. #### Who will be able to see these tracks? Publicly available tracks on SoundCloud are available to everyone and can be seen by anyone. This change just means that your track will be amplified and suggested to more listeners (and more potential fans) through autoplay. #### How will this impact my listening experience on SoundCloud? Making sure that autoplay remains a fun and valuable way to discover new music will always be a top priority. As we test this initiative, we will be making adjustments based on listener behavior to make sure we’re amplifying and recommending the right tracks to listeners who will resonate with. #### Can you turn this on or off as a listener? Our recommendations are tailored to your listening behavior and can help surface tracks you might be interested in. If you don’t want to listen to autoplay recommendations, you can always hit the skip button, queue up songs, create a playlist, or actively choose what tracks to listen to. You can learn more about autoplay here. #### To get started, sign up for Artist Pro** today!**

How the Feed on SoundCloud Works

About the Feed 

The SoundCloud Feed helps listeners discover new tracks and keeps them up to date with the artists they already follow. As an artist, using the Feed is a great way to be discovered by new fans and to strengthen your relationship with your existing community. We have just released a major update to the Feed on mobile (iOS and Android), splitting your algorithm into two tabs: Discover and Following. On the web, your Following algorithm can be found under the Feed section. Keep an eye out for more improvements to the Feed in the future, with a particular focus on giving creators more ways to express themselves, grow, and connect with their fans. ##### Discover Tab: Your public tracks will be recommended on the Discover tab for listeners, based on their similarity to songs listeners already listen to and like. Every recommendation is personalized for the listener and includes an explanation of why it was selected. ##### Following Tab: The Following tab shows new releases and reposts from the profiles that you follow. All your public tracks and reposts will appear on the Following tab for all users who follow you. Encourage your fans to follow your profile so they know when you drop new tracks. Users who unfollow you will no longer see your posts in their Following tab. You can make your track stand out on the Following tab by adding a caption. This is a great way to share a personal message with your followers, such as how excited you are to release the track or a story from the creative process. #### Getting tracks on the Feed  Your tracks, if made public, will automatically appear on the Feed for followers and future fans. A 30-second preview of your track will be recommended to users via their personalized feed. This preview will link to your full track. All your existing public tracks and reposts will appear on the Feed tab for all users who follow you in chronological order. If you don’t want your track to appear in the Feed, you can always set your track to private. ##### How to select a Track preview When you upload a track to SoundCloud, you can choose the previewthat appears in the Feed. Click the “Advanced” button during upload to select your preview. This same clip will also be used for social sharing, like Instagram previews. If you don’t select a preview, our AI will automatically choose a 30-second snippet of your track for the Feed. ##### Uploading artwork for Feed  The artwork you choose when uploading your track will automatically appear on the Feed. If you don’t upload an artwork, we’ll show your profile picture.

How to grow your audience on SoundCloud

Standing out on SoundCloud takes more than great music. To grow your audience, you need to combine your talent with smart promotion, consistent engagement, and the platform’s built-in tools to reach the right listeners. #### Create a profile that stands out First impressions matter. Your profile picture, header, bio, and track descriptions are often the first things listeners notice when they discover your music. A well-crafted profile helps you make a lasting impression and encourages fans to engage with your music. Tips for a memorable artist profile: - Tell your story: Use your bio andtrack descriptions to introduce yourself, share your creative journey, and encourage listeners to repost or engage with your tracks. - Use recognizable visuals: Keep your profile image and header simple and memorable so they scale well in Streams and feeds. - Reinforce your brand: Include your artist name consistently across your profile and artwork. - Be consistent and professional: A polished, cohesive profile signals credibility and helps listeners remember you.

A thoughtful profile not only grabs attention but also invites listeners to explore your music and become long-term fans. #### Promote your music on SoundCloud SoundCloud offers tools to help your music reach more listeners directly on the platform. - Amplify introduces your new music to listeners who are most likely to enjoy it. When enabled, SoundCloud recommends your track to a group of listeners whose past behavior aligns with your sound. - Buzzing Playlists are weekly, fan-powered playlists highlighting tracks gaining strong engagement from listeners. They feature up-and-coming Artist Pro creators across Pop, Hip Hop, R&B, and Electronic. - Share your profile and tracks on social networks, blogs, and other platforms.

The more places your music is discoverable, the more opportunities you have to grow your audience. #### Improve your discoverability with search optimization Making your profile easier to find online helps bring more listeners to your music: - Use a clear display name (e.g., User 123 instead of User123). - Keep your artist name consistent across your profile, URL, and other platforms. - Link to your social profiles or websites in your SoundCloud profile.

Consistency across platforms improves your search visibility and helps fans find you. #### Use Insights to guide your strategy SoundCloud Insights shows who is listening to your music and where your plays are coming from: - Top cities: see where your music is popular to plan tours or promotions. - Listener engagement: identify potential collaborators and active fans. - Plays by app: understand where your audience is listening. - Plays by website: discover which blogs and sites are driving traffic.

Insights help you make smarter decisions about promotion, touring, and networking. #### Build a network Networking and collaboration are key to growing on SoundCloud: - Use Search** and Charts to discover creators with similar styles. - Follow artists whose music you enjoy. - Leave thoughtful feedback and comments** on tracks you like.

Focus on quality interactions—genuine engagement often leads to stronger relationships and opportunities. #### Stay consistent Even the best profiles lose momentum without regular activity: - Upload new music regularly. - Engage with your audience consistently. - Maintain visibility in Streams and playlists.

Consistency helps build your reputation, keeps fans engaged, and increases your chances of being discovered.

Share music from SoundCloud on social media

Share your favorite tracks, profiles, albums, or playlists directly from the SoundCloud app or browser to Instagram Stories, Facebook Stories, Snapchat, Twitter, WhatsApp, and more. #### How to Share ##### iOS & Android 1. Open the latest SoundCloud app and find the track, profile, album, or playlist to share. 2. Tap the share icon. 3. Select the social media app where you want to share it. 4. Edit your story by adding text or a SoundCloud Giphy sticker if you like. 5. When finished, share it with your fans, followers, or friends.

Web
  1. Click the ‘Share’ button underneath the track’s waveform.
  2. Select the icon of the social media app where you would like to share it.
  3. Edit your post and share it with all your fans, followers, or friends.

Audio Snippets

From now on, you can share audio snippets of your favorite tracks via Instagram stories. Available on both iOS and Android apps. ##### How to share 1. Open the latest SoundCloud app and find the track to share. 2. Look for a speaker badge indicating Audio Snippets are allowed. 3. Tap the Instagram Stories icon. 4. Edit your story on Instagram with text or SoundCloud Giphy stickers. 5. Share your edited story with your fans, followers, or friends.

Please note that not all tracks in our catalog have audio snippets available, as this decision is made by the rightsholders and cannot be changed by us.

SoundCloud’s Buzzing Playlists

What is Buzzing?

Buzzing Playlists are a new set of fan-powered, genre-specific playlists, featuring songs based on genuine fan engagement. Updated weekly, these new playlists are sourced from Artist Pro artists who have opted in to have their tracks analyzed by Amplify, and are meant to expose artists to even more listeners, allowing them to get heard by potential new fans. Buzzing Playlists will showcase fresh tracks from the best up-and-coming Artist Pro artists in Pop, Hip Hop, R&B, and Electronic. For Artist Pro artists, it’s a chance to show off their best new music and find future fans. For listeners, it’s a way to discover the tracks and artists other fans in their scene are connecting with. You can listen to this week’s Buzzing Playlists here. #### How can I be featured on a Buzzing playlist? #####  Here’s how Buzzing works: 1. SoundCloud Artist Pro artists upload a fresh track and can opt in to have it analyzed by Amplify, our recommendation algorithm. 2. Amplify then analyzes these uploads and recommends them to up to 100 listeners (real listeners, not bots) most likely to love it, based on their past listening behavior. 3. From there, top tracks are recommended to even more listeners, now up to 1000. 4. The highest performing tracks of those recommended – the ones that listeners engage with the most (engagement, plays, replays, and playlist adds) earn a spot on a coveted, fan-powered, Buzzing playlist.

For details on eligible tracks for Amplify and Buzzing playlists and how to opt in, click here. #### Are all tracks I opt into Amplify featured on a Buzzing playlist? No, only the top-performing tracks from Artist Pro artists that have opted in to have their tracks analyzed by Amplify have the opportunity to make it to a Buzzing Playlist.

Creators on SoundCloud: Creator Insights

Advanced SoundCloud Insights

Play Counts & Top Listeners

  • Your total plays for a selected time period appear in yourInsights Overview page.
  • Self-plays are not counted—plays from your own account will not increase your total.
  • Logged-in listeners’ plays update in real-time; others update within 24 hours.
  • Top Listeners: See the top 50 fans who played your tracks, for any time period you choose. Only signed-in listeners are included. (Exclusive to Artist Pro subscribers)

Country & City Insights

  • View the top 50 countries and** cities** for any time period. (Exclusive to Artist Pro subscribers)

Use this data to:

Plan tours and shows - Strategize your next release - Connect with your fanbase more effectively

Likes, Comments, Reposts & Downloads

  • View engagement data for a selected time period on the top bar of your Insights Overview page.
  • Artist Pro subscriberscan see:

Which tracks received likes, reposts, comments, or downloads - Additional details about the listeners behind these actions

Play Counts from Offline Listening

  • Plays from SoundCloud Go subscribers listening offline count toward your track’s total once the listener reconnects online.
  • Downloads are recorded at the moment the listener presses play offline.
  • Note: Plays may appear in your stats up to 30 days later, as SoundCloud Go allows offline listening for a maximum of 30 days without reconnecting to the internet.

Websites & Apps

  • Artist Pro subscribers can see where their tracks are being played outside of SoundCloud.

Insights include plays on SoundCloud pages and other websites or apps. - Each list shows a maximum of 50 items.

Help with SoundCloud Insights

Jump To:

Insights aren’t updating Unable to see advanced insights What to do if you suspect suspicious or fake activity on your tracks? Can I view Insights for a deleted track or account? Can I export my SoundCloud Insights? #### Insights aren’t updating If it seems like your Insights are stuck on your track’s individual page or your profile, this is due to caching. You can get around this by refreshing your cache. 

To check your Insights in the most accurate spots on the site, it’s best to look at your track’s stats through your Insights Overview page. 

Please note: Our Insights do not count self-plays. Playing your own track while signed in won’t be recorded. To verify if your Insights update, try playing the track while signed out, then sign back in to check the play count. #### Unable to see advanced Insights #### What to do if you suspect suspicious or fake activity on your tracks? If you see a sudden spike in activity on your track or account, it might be due to fake accounts. These accounts mimic real users by following, playing, liking, and reposting sounds. Our Trust and Safety team works to detect and remove them, but some actions may occur before removal. When removed, their interactions are also deleted. Note: We cannot adjust or revert play counts. We recommend blocking and reporting any suspected fake accounts using our block feature . This must be done on a computer, not a mobile device. #### Can I view Insights for a deleted track or account? If you delete your account, your stats will be removed from SoundCloud. #### Can I export my SoundCloud Insights? We do not currently have an exporting feature available for our Insights.

Individual Track Insights

On a desktop browser, your track’s page shows an overview of how many times your track has been recommended and how many fans have listened to your track more than once. The Insights module is only visible on your own tracks, meaning other users cannot see this information. #### Recommended plays Total plays from the SoundCloud algorithm, which includes plays from stations and the autoplay queue. Artist and Artist Pro subscribers can opt into Amplify to boost recommendations to the right fans. When using Amplify, the Recommended plays section turns purple, showing active promotion to new fans via the Amplify algorithm. #### Repeat listeners  Fans who played your track multiple times likely love your music. Consider messaging them on SoundCloud to thank them or ask for feedback. Insights are updated every 24 hours, so they may not always show the most up-to-date information. You can view advanced insights, such as source of plays and top listeners, on your Insights page.

Insights on SoundCloud

SoundCloud Insights gives you the data you need to understand who is listening, how they’re interacting, and where your music is gaining momentum. Whether you’re planning a tour or your next release, these metrics help you turn listeners into fans. Note: The Insights Overview page operates on GMT (Greenwich Mean Time). #### How to Access Your Insights You can check your stats from your desk or on the go: - On Desktop: Click your profile avatar in the top right and select Your Insights. - On Mobile: Head to your Artist Home, Library, or SoundCloud Channel and tap Your Insights.

The default view shows your activity from the past 30 days, but you can use the dropdown menu to toggle between Day, Week, Month, or Year. #### Understanding Your Metrics Every artist on SoundCloud has access to these core engagement stats: - Plays: The total number of times your track has been played (note: your own plays are excluded). - Likes: How many listeners have saved your track to their Library. - Comments: Real-time feedback and fan engagement directly on your waveform. - Reposts: Shares that push your track to other listeners’ Streams. - Downloads: If enabled, the number of times fans have saved your file to their device.

Artist Pro: Advanced Insights

If you’re looking to scale, Artist Pro unlocks the deep-dive data you need to turn plays into a career: - Top Fans: Identify your most dedicated listeners so you can reward them or engage with them directly. - Locations: See exactly which countries and cities are playing your music—essential for planning tour stops or ad spend. - Sources: Find out if your plays are coming from the SoundCloud app, a specific playlist, or an external website embed.

Reading the Activity Graph

The Activity Graph is your visual map of growth. - The Breakdown: The graph highlights your Top 5 tracks individually. All other tracks are grouped under “Others” to keep your view clean. - Interactive Data: On Desktop, hover over any point on the graph to see the daily total. On Mobile, simply tap the graph to see that day’s specific numbers.

Want to dive deeper into a specific release? Check out our guides onIndividual Track Insights or see the SoundCloud Newsrooom for any data reporting updates.

Top & First Fans

The Fans module showcases a track’s most dedicated supporters. When you listen to, like, and follow a particular track, you increase your chances of earning a spot on the artist’s Top & First fan leaderboard. Those who have played a track the most appear in the Top Fans tab, and those who were first to listen appear in the First Fans tab. This module is visible to all users on web and iOS as a way for artists to publicly celebrate their biggest fans and those who were there as soon as a track dropped. If you are on the leaderboard for First or Top Fans, you will see an option to share your rank on social media. Note, users will only qualify for the leaderboard when they Like and Follow the Artist, and have a profile picture. Artist Pro subscribers can see a full list of their Top Fans in the Top listeners section of Insights. #### Removing yourself from a Fans list If you appear in a Top or First Fans list, you can remove yourself by hovering over your name, pressing the X button, and confirming your removal. Please note: this cannot be undone. This will remove you from the particular list but will not remove you from any other Fans lists. If you want to ensure you don’t show up in any Fans lists, you can opt out of the feature entirely by visiting the Privacy tab on your Settings page and disabling “Show when I’m a First or Top Fan”. #### Removing Fans from my tracks Artists can remove specific users from the Fans lists on their track pages by hovering over the user in the list, pressing the X button, and confirming the removal. Please note: this cannot be undone. This will remove the user from the particular list, but will not remove the user from your other Fans lists. Artists can still block specific fans to remove them from all their Fans lists, or can choose to disable the Fans module entirely. If you want to disable this feature on your own tracks, you can do so by visiting the Privacy tab on your Settings page and disabling “Show First and Top Fans for my tracks”.

Refer a Friend**** Program Details The SoundCloud Refer a Friend Program allows paid Artist Pro creators to earn cash by referring friends. When someone signs up for Artist Pro using your unique referral link, they get a free month, and you earn a $15 cash reward after their first paid month. #### How It Works: 1. Share Your Code:** Share your unique referral link with friends. 2. Your Friend Signs Up: They get a free month of Artist Pro when they subscribe. 3. Earn Rewards: After your friend’s first paid month, you’ll earn $15 which you may redeem as a digital gift card or PayPal payout.

Rewards and Limits:

  • Reward Amount: $15 per successful referral.
  • Annual Cap: Maximum of $150 per year (up to 10 referrals).
  • Payout Timing: Rewards are paid 30 days after your friend’s first payment.

Program Qualifications

Referring user must:

  • Be an existing Artist Pro subscriber in the United States.
  • Be age nineteen (19) or older
  • Remain a paid subscriber to qualify for payouts.
Friend:
  • Must be a new Artist Pro customer in the United States.
  • Be age nineteen (19) or older
  • Must pay for a subscription after their trial period.
  • Must pass quality/fraud checks in the program.

Frequently Asked Questions Q: How do I refer my friend? A: After logging into your Artist Pro account, you can visit our program page here: https://invite.soundcloud.com/ Q: How do I find my referral link? A: Your unique referral link is available in your Artist Pro account, by clicking the link at the top of the page or you can visit our program page here: https://invite.soundcloud.com/ Q: How will I know if my friend signed up? A: You’ll receive an email when your friend subscribes and another when you earn a payout. Q: I referred my friend. When will I get my reward? A: Ask your friend when they signed up. If the 31-day pending period hasn’t passed yet, your reward will be sent after that period. If it has passed and you still haven’t received the reward, please contact referral program support (details below). Q: How do I get paid? A: You’ll receive an email with payout instructions after earning a reward. You can choose to redeem rewards as a gift card or via PayPal. Q: Can I refer friends outside the US? A: No, both the referrer and friend must be located in the US. Q: Can I refer someone who previously had an Artist Pro (or Next Pro) subscription? A: No, only new subscribers are eligible. Q: What if my friend cancels before their first paid month? A: If your friend doesn’t complete their first paid month, you won’t receive the referral payout. Q: Do I need to keep my subscription active to get paid? A: Yes, you must remain a paid Artist Pro subscriber to qualify for payouts. Q: Will I be paid immediately once my friend starts their free trial? A: No, your friend must finish their free trial and convert to a paying subscription in order to be eligible. Once your friend begins their paid subscription, it may take up to 31 days to receive your payout. Q: Are all subscriptions eligible for payouts? A: Only Artist pro plans are eligible. Go, Go+ and Artist plans are not eligible for the referral program. Q: Why haven’t I received my reward? A: A few things can affect referral payouts. Here are the most common ones: - Your friend may have canceled during their free trial and didn’t move to a paid subscription. - Referrals aren’t eligible if your friend previously had an Artist Pro subscription. - Your friend needs to sign up using your unique referral link for the referral to track. - Your Artist Pro subscription must stay active through the payout period. - Both you and your friend must be located in the United States. - Payouts can take up to 31 days after your friend finishes their free trial and starts paying. - Your friend may have subscribed to the Artist plan instead of Artist Pro. - You may have reached the reward maximum ($150 or 10 referrals per calendar year) - Referrals may be disqualified if there’s evidence of fraudulent activity.

Q: What is Extole? A: Extole makes software to manage referral programs. They are the service provider we partner with to help us manage SoundCloud’s referral program.
