Subscription Management

Managing your SoundCloud subscription should be straightforward, so you can get back to the music. Here is everything you need to know about upgrading, billing, and updating your details. #### Upgrades & Changes Ready to level up? Whether you’re moving to more creator tools or a deeper listening experience, here is how to upgrade: To upgrade from Artist to Artist Pro: 1. Visit your Subscription Settings from the top-right corner of your SoundCloud dashboard. 2. Select Edit on the subscription you wish to upgrade. 3. Select Upgrade on the Artist Pro plan. 4. Confirm your payment details, and you’re all set.

To upgrade from Go to Go+: 1. Visit your Subscription Settings. 2. Select Edit on the subscription you wish to upgrade. 3. Select Upgrade on the Go+ plan. 4. Confirm your details, and you’re all set.

The lower price you’re seeing is the monthly equivalent of the yearly plan. If you’re paying monthly, you’re on the flexible plan—which is slightly more expensive over the course of a year. To switch and save: 1. Cancel your current monthly plan from the** **Subscriptions tab (on desktop or mobile browser). 2. After it expires, go back and re-subscribe using the yearly option.

Billing & Payments

We offer two billing cycles to fit your needs: - Monthly: Pay as you go, cancel anytime. - Yearly: Pay once for the year at a lower overall cost.

The yearly plan is our best value. While it may be shown as a “per month” price on the pricing page to show you the savings, the full yearly amount is charged at checkout. Both monthly and yearly plans automatically renew. You can view your current plan and opt out of any automatic renewals by visiting your Subscriptions page and clicking on the Edit icon. Keeping your billing info current ensures your music and your listening stay uninterrupted. If you pay by credit or debit card: 1. Log in to SoundCloud on the web or open the app. 2. Go to your Subscriptions page. 3. Click Edit, then select Manage your billing. 4. Enter your new details and save your changes.

If you use PayPal or want to switch to it: To update your PayPal info—or to switch from a card to PayPal—you’ll need to let your current plan expire and then start a fresh one. Because of how PayPal works, these changes are handled as a new subscription. 1. Cancel your current plan at soundcloud.com/you/subscriptions. 2. Wait for your current plan to reach its expiration date. 3. Once it expires, visit your Subscriptions page and choose your desired plan. 4. Enter your updated details and select your preferred payment method.

Note for Artist Pro creators: If your plan expires before you renew, don’t sweat it. Your tracks stay exactly where they are—nothing is deleted. If you go over the free upload limit, your older tracks will simply be hidden from the public, but you can still see them on your Tracks page. They’ll reappear as soon as your new plan is active. Note on already canceled plans: If you have already canceled any upcoming billing, the option to edit your info won’t be available. You’ll simply need to purchase a new plan after your current subscription expires. #### Manage Your Subscription There isn’t a way to change the date your monthly payment is taken at the moment. If it’s more convenient to have payment taken on another date, please opt out of automatic renewals in your account’s Subscriptions page or via Apple by clicking on the Edit icon. Your subscription will continue for the remainder of the 30-day period, and then you will be downgraded to the Basic plan. You can then choose to subscribe again through your Subscriptions page. It is not possible to pause a subscription. However, you can opt out of automatic renewals by going to your account Subscriptions page** and clicking on the Edit** icon. Follow the prompt “Don’t want to renew your plan?” to confirm that you would like to stop your recurring payment. When you cancel your subscription, please note that previous pricing will not apply to your new purchase. #### Still have questions? What happens if I downgrade from Artist Pro to a Basic plan? What happens if I downgrade from Go+ to a Basic plan? Cancel your subscription Chat with our AI agent for quick answers, or connect with a support specialist.

Creators on SoundCloud: Customize your RSS Feed

Add a category for your Podcast RSS Feed

Selecting the right category is essential for making your podcast easy to find on Apple Podcasts and other platforms. By selecting a category that accurately represents your podcast’s content, you improve its searchability and increase the likelihood of reaching your target audience. #### How can I choose a category for my podcast’s RSS feed? To submit your RSS feed to Apple Podcasts and make your podcast more discoverable, you need to choose a category that best reflects the content of your podcast. Here’s how you can do it: 1. Go to your Content Settings page on SoundCloud. 2. Select a category that aligns with your podcast’s subject matter.

Can I choose a subcategory for my podcast on SoundCloud?

Currently, SoundCloud does not allow you to choose a subcategory or a second category for your podcast. You can only select one primary category for your RSS feed. #### Popular podcast categories and their impact on searchability Examples of popular podcast categories include: - Technology: Ideal for podcasts about the latest in tech, gadgets, and innovation. - Health & Wellness: Best suited for content focusing on fitness, mental health, and lifestyle. - True Crime: For podcasts covering criminal cases, investigations, and legal discussions.

Add a stats service URL prefix to your RSS feed

Podtrac and Blubrry provide advanced statistics that help you understand your podcast’s audience better, including detailed listener and subscriber data. This information is valuable for tailoring your content and improving your podcast’s reach. Here’s how you can set it up: 1. Go to the Stats Service URL Prefix section of your Content Settings page on SoundCloud. 2. If you are a Podtrac user, enter the following URL: http://www.podtrac.com/pts/redirect.mp3/. 3. If you are using Blubrry, copy-paste your custom redirect URL from Powerpress, found under the “Services and Stats” section.

​Please note: This section is only for Podtrac or Blubrry users. You should not fill in this section with anything but http://www.podtrac.com/pts/redirect.mp3/. If you’re using Blubrry, copy-paste your custom redirect URL displayed in PowerPress under the “Services and Stats” section. Putting anything else in this section (such as a FeedBurner link or website address) will break your RSS feed.

Add an email address to your RSS feed

Some podcast apps, like Spotify, require a valid email address to use their service. You can choose to show or hide your email on your Content Settings page and update it anytime. #### How to add an Email Address in your SoundCloud RSS Feed: 1. Use your credentials to log in to your SoundCloud account. 2. Access your content settings by clicking the three dots at your profile’s top right and selecting “Settings.” Then, go to the “Content” tab. 3. Decide Whether to Display Your Email Address

Display Your Email Address: If you want your email address to be shown in your RSS feed (recommended for avoiding rejections from podcast apps like Spotify): Check the option to display your email address. 4. Hide Your Email Address: If you prefer not to show your email address (default option): Uncheck the option to display your email address. SoundCloud will instead display the email “feeds@soundcloud.com” in your RSS feed. 5. Regularly check if your podcast is being accepted by all platforms.

What happens if I hide my email address in the RSS feed?

If you hide your email address, SoundCloud will display “feeds@soundcloud.com” in your RSS feed. However, this might cause some podcast apps, like Spotify, to reject your RSS feed because they require a valid, personal email address to be listed. This ensures that the app can contact you if necessary and helps verify the authenticity of your content. Please note: While you can choose not to display your personal email address, be aware that this might prevent some podcast apps from accepting your RSS feed. If you encounter issues, consider allowing your email address to be shown in the feed. #### What should I do if my RSS feed is rejected by an app due to email issues? If your RSS feed is rejected by an app because it does not display a valid email address, you should: 1. Go to your Content Settings page. 2. Choose to display your personal email address in the RSS feed. 3. Resubmit your RSS feed to the podcast app.

Add Episode Descriptions and Artwork to Your Podcast RSS Feed

To optimize your content for podcast platforms like Apple Podcasts, consider adding well-crafted descriptions and high-quality artwork for each episode. Descriptions should be concise yet informative, and the artwork should meet the pixel requirement to ensure it displays correctly on all platforms. #### How can I add individual artwork to each podcast episode? To add individual artwork for each episode, follow these steps: 1. Go to the episode’s edit page on SoundCloud. 2. Upload an image for the episode. 3. Ensure that the image is 1400x1400 pixels; otherwise, Apple Podcasts will not populate the image.

What happens if I don’t add an image to my podcast’s episode?

If you don’t add an image to your podcast’s episode, Apple Podcasts will automatically use your SoundCloud profile image as the default image for that episode.

Add your podcast’s website for Apple Podcasts

If you do not have any websites featured in your profile’s Your links section, SoundCloud will automatically share your SoundCloud Profile URL to Apple Podcasts as your website link.

If you would like to have a different website appear on SoundCloud, add a link to your ‘You on the Web’ section of your profile’s edit page. You can access your profile’s edit page through the Edit button below the header image: Please note: Social networks such as Facebook or Twitter do not count as websites on Apple Podcasts.

Set the Audio Language and Content Rating

Audio Language

Setting the language tag for your podcast helps listeners know what language your content is in, improving their experience. It also ensures your podcast is correctly categorized and distributed on platforms like iTunes, making it easier for local audiences to find. You can update the language anytime on your Content Settings page. #### Content Rating If your podcast has explicit content, check the ‘Contains explicit content’ box on your Content Settings page on SoundCloud. This ensures proper labeling for platforms like Apple Podcasts. Not marking explicit content may cause Apple Podcasts to reject your RSS feed. Explicit content includes strong language, sexual material, or anything unsuitable for all audiences. Properly categorizing your podcast helps meet platform standards like Apple Podcasts.

Set the Title and Author Name for Your Podcast’s RSS Feed

Customizing your RSS feed title and author name allows your podcast to be more easily found and recognized in podcast directories like Apple Podcasts. If your SoundCloud Display Name does not accurately represent your podcast’s brand or content, changing these details can improve your podcast’s discoverability. #### How do I customize the title and author in my podcast’s RSS feed? Your RSS feed title and author name will automatically reflect your SoundCloud account’s Display Name. However, if your Display Name is not what you want your podcast to be searched as in Apple Podcasts or other podcasting platforms, you can customize it by following these steps: 1. Go to your Content Settings page on SoundCloud. 2. Choose a new title and author name that better represent your podcast. 3. Once updated, your RSS information will be changed and reflected in Apple Podcasts and other podcast platforms.

What should I consider when choosing an RSS feed title and author name?

When choosing an RSS feed title and author name, ensure they clearly represent your podcast’s content and brand. This helps listeners find your podcast easily and ensures consistency across different podcast platforms. Here’s an example template of an effective RSS feed title and author name - RSS Feed Title: Tech Talk Weekly - Author Name: Jane Doe, Tech Enthusiast

Creators on SoundCloud: DJ Integrations

Denon DJ / Numark Integration

SoundCloud is integrated as a music streaming service with standalone DJ hardware from Denon DJ and Numark. Please find a full list of compatible products here. In order to access content from SoundCloud through these DJ products, users need a SoundCloud Go+ subscription. New users to SoundCloud Go+ are eligible for a free 30-day trial. Denon / Numark is not compatible with subscriptions via the Apple Store. Go+ subscriptions via SoundCloud only. We are sorry for the inconvenience, and we are working on a solution.  #### Connect the DJ hardware with SoundCloud To connect your Denon or Numark DJ hardware with SoundCloud, follow these steps: 1. Ensure Stable Wi-Fi and Firmware Updates:

Make sure your DJ hardware is connected to a stable Wi-Fi network. 2. Update your device to the latest firmware version. 3. Activate SoundCloud as a Service:

On your DJ hardware, go to Settings/Services. To access Settings, pull the handle from the top of the screen. 4. Activate SoundCloud as an available service. 5. Pairing the Device:

Press the source button on your DJ hardware and select SoundCloud from the bottom of the screen. 6. A six-digit pairing code will appear along with instructions on how to activate the device. 7. Activate via Browser:

On your laptop or mobile device, open a browser and go to eitherdenondj.soundcloud.com** ornumark.soundcloud.com. 8. Log in with your SoundCloud credentials (if not already logged in). 9. If you’re not already subscribed, check out the Go+ trial. 10. Enter the six-digit pairing code displayed on your DJ hardware. 11. Confirm the pairing on the corresponding dialog box. 12. Browse and Play Music:**

Once paired, you can browse your SoundCloud library or search for any track directly from your DJ hardware. 13. Please note that Waveform, Cue, and Loop data will only be stored permanently on the device if a corresponding drive or SD card has been attached.

Disconnect DJ hardware from SoundCloud

If you want to log out of SoundCloud, press the Settings icon on the lower left of the screen when browsing the SoundCloud library. Then press the Log Out button in the dialog.

Rekordbox Integration

Rekordbox seamlessly connects with SoundCloud, giving DJs access to millions of tracks for streaming or offline playback. You can use: - SoundCloud Go+ – Stream tracks online - SoundCloud DJ – Download tracks for offline use

New users may be eligible for a 30-day free trial of SoundCloud Go+. #### Connecting Your SoundCloud Account 1. Open Rekordbox and switch to Performance Mode

  1. In the browser panel, select the SoundCloud node

  2. Click “Log in” or “Start Trial.”

  3. Sign in with your SoundCloud account

Once connected, you can browse and stream SoundCloud’s catalog directly in Rekordbox. Note: Rekordbox 5.6.1 or later is required. SoundCloud is not supported in Export Mode. #### Streaming & Offline Playback #### Streaming with Go+ - Access the full SoundCloud library directly in Rekordbox. - Cue points, loops, and flips are saved automatically for future sessions.

Offline with SoundCloud DJ

  • Select tracks or playlists, open the context menu, and choose “Store Offline.”
  • Requires Rekordbox version 6.6.0 or later. You can update your version here.
  • Offline mode is only available with a SoundCloud DJ subscription.

Tip: Use a stable internet connection when downloading tracks for offline use. #### Features & Playback - Tracks are analyzed for BPM, key, and waveform once loaded. - Search SoundCloud tracks directly in the Rekordbox library (identified by the SoundCloud icon). - Your most recent 1000 SoundCloud Likes are available in-app. - Playlists appear in the “Playlists and Albums” section. - Cue points, loops, and flips persist across sessions.

Audio Quality & Limitations

  • Streaming quality is up to 256 kbps AAC or higher if the original upload allows. Lossless or high-bitrate tracks stream in high quality.
  • Recording DJ sets with streamed SoundCloud tracks is not supported.
  • Playlists cannot be created or edited in Rekordbox; they must be managed in SoundCloud.

Compatibility

  • SoundCloud integration is supported on compatible CDJ setups with proper configuration.
  • Ensure Rekordbox is updated to the latest version to access all features, including offline mode.

Learn more about SoundCloud DJ integrations here.

Serato Integration

Serato integrates with SoundCloud, allowing DJs to stream millions of tracks directly in Serato DJ Pro and Serato DJ Lite. To use SoundCloud in Serato, you need: - SoundCloud Go+(for streaming access) - Serato DJ Pro or Serato DJ Lite (supported versions listed below)

New users may be eligible for a 30-day free trial of SoundCloud Go+. #### Supported Serato Versions To access SoundCloud in Serato, you must use one of the following versions: - Serato DJ Pro 2.1 or later - Serato DJ Lite 1.1 or later

Connecting Your SoundCloud Account

To access SoundCloud content in Serato: 1. Open Serato DJ Pro or Lite 2. Locate the SoundCloud icon in the left library panel

  1. Click the icon and select “Start Trial” or “Sign In”
  2. Log in with your SoundCloud account

If the SoundCloud icon is not visible: 1. Go to Settings (gear icon) 2. Open Library + Display 3. Enable “Show Streaming Services.” 4. Select SoundCloud

Streaming & Search

  • SoundCloud Go+ is required to stream tracks in Serato
  • Use the search bar to find SoundCloud tracks
  • Click the SoundCloud icon next to the search bar to enable SoundCloud search
  • Local results appear first, followed by SoundCloud results (marked with the SoundCloud icon)

Playback Features

When using SoundCloud in Serato: - Tracks are analyzed for BPM, key, and waveform when loaded onto a deck - Analysis data is saved to your library for future use - Cue points, loops, and flips are saved and restored when reloading tracks

Audio Quality

  • Streams are delivered in up to 256 kbps AAC
  • High-bitrate uploads are prioritized when available
  • SoundCloud aims to provide the highest possible quality for Go+ users

Playlists & Library Behavior

  • Your SoundCloud playlists appear under “Playlists and Albums” in the library
  • Playlist creation and editing must be done in SoundCloud (not Serato). Learn how to create a playlist on SoundCloud here.
  • SoundCloud Likes are not currently supported in Serato
  • Adding SoundCloud tracks to Serato crates is not supported

Offline Playback

  • Offline streaming of SoundCloud tracks is not supported in Serato
  • An active internet connection is required to stream

Recording & Performance Limitations

  • Recording DJ sets that include SoundCloud-streamed tracks is not supported

Additional Notes

  • You may not be offered a Go+ trial in Serato if you were previously subscribed
  • Ensure Serato DJ Pro/Lite is updated to the latest supported version for best compatibility

Tune My Music Integration

Tune My Music provides a complete DJ software for all DJs. The DJ software seamlessly integrates with your SoundCloud Go+music library, giving you instant access to millions of tracks. Offline capabilities as part of the SoundCloud DJ subscription are not currently enabled. #### How do I migrate my Spotify collection to SoundCloud? If you’d like to migrate your music collection to SoundCloud directly within the platform, learn how to here. To move your music through our partner, Tune My Music, follow these steps: 1. Connect with your Spotify account 2. Load playlists from your Spotify account 3. Select playlists to move 4. Connect with your SoundCloud account 5. Sign in to SoundCloud

You will need a Go+ subscription to use Tune My Music. Your “Liked Songs” will move to the “Likes” section on SoundCloud. Other playlists will be created as new public playlists by default, allowing others to find and like them. To keep a playlist private, edit its privacy settings. For help rearranging playlists, click here for more info. #### Why are some tracks missing and did not get moved? Tune My Music has a high match rate when trying to find tracks on SoundCloud. However, sometimes tracks cannot be found due to inconsistent metadata or content not being available on SoundCloud. For missing tracks, it’s still worth performing a manual search on SoundCloud. #### Why can I not mix tracks in Tune My Music?  To use Tune My Music with SoundCloud, you must have an active SoundCloud Go+ subscription. Learn more about the benefits of Go+ and to start your free trial here. #### Tune My Music is not working properly. What should I do? Check out the Tune My Music help centre for getting started or technical support.

VirtualDJ Integration

VirtualDJ seamlessly integrates with your music library, giving you instant access to millions of tracks. It can be used online with a Go+ subscription or offline with a SoundCloud DJ subscription. #### How to connect VirtualDJ to SoundCloud 1. SoundCloud is located in the Online Music folder of the Folder List. Right-clicking on the folder will give you the option to sign in to the SoundCloud Catalog. (image: soundcloudlogin.png) 2. A browser window will open, and the login screen will appear. Use your SoundCloud user account credentials to log in, or click on the other options at the top to log in with Facebook or Google.

  1. Once completed, a confirmation window will appear advising that you can close the window as you are successfully logged in.

  2. You can now use the root SoundCloud folder to search their catalog directly from the VirtualDJ search bar. Expanding the SoundCloud folder using the button will also display your liked tracks, playlists, and albums, as well as provide different genre lists of what is currently trending.

  3. Drag and drop any of the songs from the File List to a deck to begin streaming, or right-click and select “Load on” and choose the deck you want the song loaded on.

How do I access Offline play?

To use Virtual DJ offline with SoundCloud, you will need to be subscribed to a SoundCloud DJ subscription. To access Offline Play: 1. Ensure your SoundCloud account is connected. 2. Then find your playlists or tracks on the left tab, and right-click “Download to Cache”. 3. You will then see your tracks move to the next column and start to download. 4. After you have downloaded your tracks to cache (offline), you can use your tracks wherever you like without an internet connection.

VirtualDJ has a bug. What should I do?

Check out the VirtualDJ help center or technical support here .

Creators on SoundCloud: Fan & Community Tools

Fan Support

Fan Support allows your most dedicated listeners to contribute financially to your career, moving beyond plays and likes. Artists receive 100% of every contribution (after third-party payment processing fees). #### Quick Navigation - How to Set Up (Artists) - How to Contribute (Fans) - Tracking & Payouts - Availability & Eligibility

Artist Setup

When you become eligible, a “Get Started” prompt will appear on your profile. 1. Follow the link to create an account with Adyen, our secure third-party payment provider. 2. Once your Adyen account is confirmed, a Support button will automatically appear on your SoundCloud profile for your fans to see. 3. You can manage your account details or update your information at any time via the Fan Support Dashboard.

Information for Supporters

Supporting your favorite artist is direct and secure: - Amounts: Contribute any amount from $1 to $1,000 USD. - Payment Methods: We support Credit Cards, PayPal, Apple Pay, and Google Pay. - Recognition: If your contribution qualifies, you will be featured in the Top Supporters leaderboard on the artist’s profile. - Refund Policy: Fan Support contributions are non-refundable to ensure fairness and clarity for creators.

Tracking & Payouts

You will receive a push notification and an email for every new contribution. You can track your funds in the Fan Support Dashboard: - Pending Balance: Support that has been pledged but hasn’t yet transferred to your Adyen account. - Available Balance: Funds that have cleared and are ready for the next payout. - Payout Schedule: Payments are sent monthly, provided your available balance has reached the $10 minimum threshold.

Availability

We are currently rolling this feature out in stages: For Artists: Currently available exclusively to artists based in the United States. We are working to expand this to more regions soon. For Fans: Supporters can contribute from the following regions: - North America: USA, Canada, Mexico. - Europe: UK, Ireland, France, Germany, Italy, Spain, Netherlands, Belgium, Austria, Denmark, Norway, Sweden, Switzerland, Portugal. - Oceania: Australia, New Zealand.

Want to learn more about your supporters? Check out the Fans Tool to see who is engaging most with your music.

Privacy and Safety in the Fans Tool

Can listeners control who can message them? Yes, they can control who can message them on SoundCloud via the Privacy tab within Settings. Disabling “Receive messages from anyone” ensures only people they follow will be able to send them messages. Make sure to encourage fans to follow you so you’re able to connect with them in meaningful ways! Can fans and artists disable email notifications for new messages? Yes, from within the Notifications tab within Settings. Can fans and artists report abusive messages? Yes, fans and artists can report abusive messages and block the user responsible. This will prevent the sender from being able to continue to contact, and the sender’s account will be reviewed by our team. Can anyone send messages? Only those with a registered SoundCloud account.

Selling vinyl and earning Fan Support with the Artist Support Tab

Making music is the easy part, but earning from it is where things can get complicated. The Artist Support Tab is here to help. It’s a section on your profile where you can showcase your vinyl releases and let fans back you directly. Fans browse, buy, and support without ever leaving your profile. The Artist Support Tab is currently available on Desktop Web only. Stay tuned for updates. #### Setting up your Support tab Every artist has a Support tab. Any live vinyl releases shows up there automatically, each with its tracklist and album art pulled in for you. #### Managing your releases The Support tab is yours to shape. You can: - Add or edit a description for any release, so fans know what they’re picking up. - Hide an item whenever you want, then bring it back later. - Add something new as your catalog grows.

Any changes you make show up right away. Your fans only see the Support tab once there’s at least one visible item on it. If you don’t have any visible items, the tab disappears from your profile until you add something back. #### How fans support you Fans who visit your profile can back you in two ways: - Buy your vinyl straight from the Support tab. - Send a one-time payment through Fan Support if they want to go a step further.

For fans: browsing and buying

When an artist has vinyl to show, you’ll see a Support tab on their profile. From there you can browse all their vinyl in one place, with tracklists, descriptions, and album art, and buy whatever you love. Want to do more than pick up a record? Use Fan Support to send the artist a one-time payment directly from their profile. It’s a simple way to back the artists you care about. #### A few things to know - The Artist Support Tab is on Desktop Web only for now. It isn’t available in the mobile apps yet. - Right now you can sell vinyl releases. We’ll be adding more over time. - Fan Support is a one-time payment fans send you directly, separate from buying a release.

Using the Fans Tool

At SoundCloud, we value fans as the key to an artist’s success. Using Fan Powered Royalties and fan engagement data, Fans identifies an artist’s top fans and helps build meaningful connections with them and their community. More on Fan-Powered Royalties here. #### Who can access the Fans tool? Currently, this tool is in beta and available to Artist Pro subscribers. Because we use Fan-Powered Royalties (FPR) data to identify your top listeners, your tracks must be monetized on SoundCloud. - Independent Artists: Once you monetize your tracks, you’ll be eligible the following month. - Label Artists: If your music is licensed through a label or distributor, check with them to ensure your music is on the Fan-Powered Royalties model. - Basic Artists: To get started, upgrade to Artist Pro.

How many fans can I message at once?

We’re here to help you build authentic 1:1 relationships, not send mass blasts. To keep conversations meaningful and prevent spam, the tool is designed for individual messaging with a limit of 50 messages per day. If you hit the limit, just wait 24 hours to pick the conversation back up. #### When is my fan data updated, and why might it be missing? Your fan list refreshes during the first week of every month. If you’re monetizing but don’t see stats yet, hang tight—we are rolling this out to more Artist Pro subscribers over the next few months. In the meantime, keep promoting your tracks to generate the listener signals we need to build your list. #### How does the Fans tool differ from standard Insights? Think of Insights as your “performance report” (how your music is doing) and Fans as your “action plan” (who to talk to). While Insights shows trends, the Fans tool combines listener signals—like repeat plays, comments, and shares—with Fan-Powered Royalty data to give you a prioritized list of real people to connect with. #### Are more features coming? Definitely. We’re just getting started, and our mission is to make connecting with fans effortless. This is a beta version of the tool, so your input is vital. Feel free to share your thoughts with our AI Agent—they’ll pass your feedback directly to our product team to help shape what we build next.

Creators on SoundCloud: Get Started with Distribution

Distribution Best Practices

Platforms, like Spotify and Apple Music, have strict guidelines for metadata, audio, and artwork. If you don’t follow these rules, your release may be rejected and delayed. To speed up approval, avoid these common mistakes: #### Artwork - Use Original Artwork: Only use artwork you own or have rights to. If using copyrighted images, provide documentation. - Keep Artwork Appropriate: Don’t submit artwork with nudity, excessive violence, or blurry images. - Avoid Generic Artwork: Generic images (like plain or single-color covers) may be rejected. Personalize your artwork. - Match Text to Metadata: Any text on your cover art needs to exactly match your release title and artist name in the metadata. Even small differences, such as extra words, symbols, or a different artist’s name, can lead to rejection. - Don’t Be Misleading: Avoid artwork that imitates famous covers or pop culture, which could confuse listeners.

For more details, see our artwork guidelines here. #### Audio - Distribute Only What You Own: Only submit content you have full rights to (no unofficial remixes or uncleared samples). - Provide Licensing: Even royalty-free samples or third-party beats need proper documentation. - If your release contains covers or music you don’t exclusively own, it may not be eligible for services like YouTube Content ID, TikTok, or Meta. Learn more about Digital Rights Management here.

We can only approve content if you verify you own or control all parts of your track or have the proper rights. If your track includes elements like beats, stems, or samples you didn’t create, upload the relevant licenses. Our content-matching system may flag original tracks if they resemble existing music, even in their melody or beat. This automated process doesn’t imply copying. You can dispute the flag by resubmitting your submission with supporting documentation, such as project files or timestamps. Pro Tip: Providing these documents upfront helps speed up the review. #### Metadata Title: Only list contributors in the proper field, not in track or release titles. Additionally, don’t use popular artist/song names or generic SEO terms in your metadata. Version Information: Only include a version title if a previous version has been distributed. For first-time releases, no version title is needed. Content Rating: Mark tracks as explicit if they contain profanity or drug references. Only use Clean if an Explicit version has already been distributed; use Non-Explicit. Original, Remix, or Cover: Avoid using terms like remix, cover, version, or another artist’s name in the title unless accurate. If it is a remix or cover, be ready to provide proof of rights; if not, label it as original. Contributors: Match your artist name exactly as it appears on Spotify/Apple (case sensitive) to avoid misplacement. Also, make sure you are listing each artist separately. NO social media handles. Songwriters: Platforms require full legal names (no initials) for composer information. Lyrics: If your track contains vocals, provide accurate audio language. For instrumental tracks with no vocals, answer “No” to “Does this track have lyrics?”.

Distribution with SoundCloud for Artists

Ready to share your music? Sign up for Artist Proand start distributing today! #### Quick Navigation: What does it mean to “distribute” or “release” my music? Why should I distribute through SoundCloud? Why do I need a distributor to distribute my music? Can I distribute if I work with a Publisher/PRO? Does SoundCloud for Artists distribute podcasts? Can I distribute a cover song? Distribution Platforms Delivery Timing How do I get paid? #### What does it mean to “distribute” or “release” my music? Distributing your music to platforms like Spotify and Apple Music lets you reach a global audience and earn streaming royalties. This involves creating an account with a digital distributor like SoundCloud, uploading your content with metadata (title, artist name, album artwork, etc.), and choosing platforms for release. Once approved, your music is available for millions to stream on demand. #### Why should I distribute through SoundCloud? SoundCloud for Artists allows you to map all of your Main Artists, Featured Artists, and Remixers to their profiles on Spotify and Apple Music, as well as exclusive member benefits to save you money. In addition to getting your music on other platforms like Spotify, Apple Music, YouTube, TikTok, and others, SoundCloud doesn’t ask for additional payment for features like: - YouTube Content ID - Split pay to pay your collaborators - Mastering your tracks - Custom label names - Unlimited number of Artists on your releases - Sending releases to over 60+ platforms - Advanced fan insights

Why do I need a distributor to distribute my music?

A distributor takes care of licensing, accurately uploading your tracks and the metadata (see below), and payouts to you when fans stream your music on streaming platforms. Platforms like SoundCloud and Bandcamp allow you to upload your music directly. However, for most other streaming platforms, you need to use a distributor. For more information on how SoundCloud can help you make money on SoundCloud and all other streaming platforms, click here. #### Can I distribute if I work with a Publisher/PRO?  Yes! Publishers and performing rights organizations (PROs) are responsible for representing your composition rights, ensuring that you receive royalties and proper credit for the underlying musical works you have created. On the other hand, SoundCloud for Artists provides a platform that enables you to monetize and distribute your actual sound recordings. This service focuses on the master recordings rather than the compositions themselves. Because these two areas cover different aspects of your music rights, there is no conflict between them. You can effectively work with both to maximize your revenue streams and control over your music career. #### Does SoundCloud for Artists distribute podcasts?  We do not currently support podcast distribution. However, you can host your podcast on SoundCloud through an RSS Feed. Learn more here. #### Can I distribute a cover song?  Yes!  However, you must obtain a license from the original writers/publishers to do so.  We suggest using a company such asEasy Song Licensing to do this. #### Distribution Platforms SC4A can currently deliver your music to the following platforms: Adaptr, Amazon, AMI Entertainment, Anghami, Apple Music / iTunes, Audiomack, Ayoba, Beatport, Boomplay, Deezer, Claro Música, Facebook /Instagram, iHeartRadio, JOOX, KKBOX, MediaNet (Securus / JPay, GTL, ACX Music, UFC Ultimate Sound, Playlist aka Riff, Vybn, ODE Audio, Keefe, Turnkey, Broadtime, Monytize), Melon Plus, Mixcloud, NetEase, Pandora Plus, Peloton, Play Network, Pretzel, Qobuz, Resso, Saavn, Shazam, Sound Exchange, Spotify, Tencent, Tidal, TikTok, YouTube Music, 7digital (Triller, Snap, ROXI, Soundtrack Your Brand, 7digital.com, Grandpad, Musixmatch, TuneSat, SoundMouse) We’re also adding new platforms, and we’ll deliver your content for no additional cost. If you have new distribution platform suggestions, please let us know! Please note: Beatport delivery is only available through our legacy Repost Select plan currently. #### Delivery Timing It usually takes a few days for your release to be reviewed and delivered to platforms. Here are estimated delivery times for popular platforms: - Apple Music: 2-3 days (some releases may take 1-2 extra weeks if reviewed further) - Spotify: 2-3 business days - YouTube Music: 2-3 days - Amazon: 1-3 business days - Deezer, iHeartRadio: 3-7 business days - TikTok: 5-7 business days - Most other platforms: 1-3 weeks

To ensure your music goes live on a specific date, schedule your release at least 4 weeks in advance, as timelines vary by store. Early scheduling also lets you submit for editorial playlists and increases your chances of being featured in algorithm-based playlists like Spotify’s Discover Weekly and Release Radar. #### How do I get paid? When your music gets streamed, you get paid by the streaming platforms based on their own guidelines. For example, Spotify requires a certain number of streams for a track to be eligible for payment. Spotify also has different rates for music streaming vs. functional content (such as white noise). However, to learn more in-depth about how a stream generates revenue and how artists are paid, here’s a great article by industry expert Ari. Although most distribution platforms pay out monthly, payouts occur within 2 or 3 months after the stream. This lag occurs because they run processes to accurately attribute streams to your track. The distribution company then processes the streaming platform’s statements and pays the artist through a variety of payout methods. For more details on how you get paid on SoundCloud, click here.

Ready to share your music? Sign up for Artist Proand start distributing today!

How to Distribute with SoundCloud

Distributing your music should be as seamless as creating it. Once you’ve subscribed to Artist Pro, signed our Terms of Service, and completed your payout and tax information, you’re ready to send your tracks to the world. To get started, click Distribute below the waveform of your uploaded track. This will take you to SoundCloud for Artists, where you can finalize your release details. You can choose to publish your track publicly, set it to Private, or schedule your releaseif you’re an Artist Pro subscriber. In SoundCloud for Artists, click the Edit icon to add the necessary metadata for distribution. If you’re dropping an EP, album, or compilation, click Select Tracks to add more songs to the release. Every track requires: - Track title - Main artist - Composer (legal name) - Content rating and audio language - Songwriter info - ISRC (we can assign one for you if you don’t have one) - You’ll also set a Preview Start Time for platforms like TikTok and Instagram

If you’re using a licensed beat, a sample, or uploading a cover, ensure you include all required creators, like producers or original songwriters. Pro Tip: If you own 100% exclusive rights, you can enable YouTube Content ID. If your track includes samples or royalty-free elements, this wouldn’t be eligible, but be sure toupload your license documentation to avoid any delays in approval. This is where you define the look and timing of your release. - Release Name: For singles, this defaults to your track title. For multi-track releases, specify the album or EP name here. - Genre: Select your Primary Genre. Note that these categories may differ slightly from SoundCloud’s internal genre list. - Record Label: This field is required. You can use your artist name or a custom label name. Consistency helps fans find your catalog later. - Release Date: This must be in the future. We recommend setting your date 30–45 days ahead to allow for review and give you enough time to pitch to platforms like Spotify. - Artwork: Your imagery must be a .jpg or .png, 3000x3000px, and 300 dpi. Ensure your artwork meets all requirements put in place by our distribution partners, including:

Choose where your music lives. By default, we select all available platforms, but you can customize this list. Things to know: - Only content you own 100% of the exclusive rights to can be distributed to UGC Fingerprinting services (TikTok, Facebook/Instagram, and YouTube Content ID). - Some stores like Pandora, iHeart, and Peloton are curated. We deliver all approved releases, but it is ultimately up to those partners what they choose to carry.

Link your release to your existing Spotify and Apple Music profiles. Make sure your names match exactly—capitalization and spaces matter. If this is your first release, select Create New Profile. Pro Tip: Check SoundCloud to see if your artist name is already taken or similar to others. It’s much easier to choose a unique name now than to change it later. Split Payis available to Artist Pro subscribers. It allows you to assign a percentage of earnings to collaborators. To enable it, click the three dots on the right-hand side of your track. Enter your collaborator’s SoundCloud URL and their percentage. They don’t need a paid subscription to get paid; they just need to log in and provide their payout details. Double-check your details to ensure everything is accurate. When you’re ready, hit Submit. What happens next? Our team will review your release to ensure it meets partner guidelines. If your release is marked as Rejected, don’t sweat it. Usually, it just means we need a quick fix—like a metadata correction or proof of license—before we can move forward. Check our Distribution Best Practices to help ensure a smooth first-time approval.

Manage Your Artist Profiles on Partner Platforms

Once your music is live on streaming platforms, you can take control of your artist presence. Here is how to manage your profiles across Spotify, Apple Music, YouTube, and more. #### First Release: Claiming Your Profiles Your artist profiles on Spotify and Apple Music are created automatically on your release day. You cannot claim them beforehand. - How to Claim: Visit Spotify for Artists or Apple Music for Artists once your release is live. - Timing: It can take up to one week after your release date for these profiles to become searchable and available for claiming. - Pitching: Spotify requires an existing profile to pitch for editorial playlists. You will be able to pitch starting with your second release, once your artist profile has been established.

YouTube Official Artist Channels (OAC)

A YouTube Official Artist Channel (OAC) is a verified, unified channel for musicians, marked by a music note icon. It merges an artist’s personal channel and auto-generated “Topic” channel into one central hub, consolidating subscribers and organizing content to improve branding and search visibility.Learn more about OACs here. - How to Upgrade: Provide our AI Support Agent with links to your personal YouTube channel and your auto-generated “Topic” channel. This information will be escalated to a support specialist to verify eligibility and submit the request to YouTube. - Timeline: YouTube’s quality assurance process is extensive and currently takes 3+ months to complete. - Confirmation: You will be contacted by YouTube directly via email once your OAC has been successfully created.

Profile Customization

Want to change your bio, images, or lyrics? Here is who manages what: - Bio & Images: Most platforms (including Spotify/Apple) allow you to update these directly once you’ve claimed your profile. For legacy bio data, updates are often pulled from Allmusic.com. - Lyrics: If you’ve distributed to Facebook/Instagram via SC4A, your existing releases might already have lyrics available. If not, sign up as a Verified Artist on Musixmatch and use their New Release form to add lyrics for your next release.

Social Media Integration

This information will be escalated to a support specialist who can process this request. Log in to your Music Reports Publisher account.If you don’t have an account, you can sign up for one here. 2. Go to the Songdex® Marketplace on the left menu. 3. Find and select the Peloton Offer. 4.
