**All listed organizations serve as third-party resources and are not directly affiliated with SoundCloud.*

Reporting conflict of ownership

The only means we have of verifying the ownership of an account is the email address that was used to create the account. This means that the individual who controls the original email address used at sign-up is the owner of that account.

Our account ownership policy is designed to protect the security and privacy of our community, as well as satisfy our responsibilities as a service provider, in relation to applicable laws. #### How to proceed if you have a conflict of ownership  If there is a conflict regarding the ownership of an account that was once shared or set up on your behalf, we must follow our account ownership policy, which states that the owner of an account is the individual who controls the email address used at sign-up.    In such conflicts, the following options are available to you: 1. Gain access to the email address used to create the account; we can then restore this email to the account. 2. If this is not possible, you can report the account, or content hosted on the account, for violating our Terms of Use on the following grounds;

Impersonation and/or misrepresentation: If the account is misrepresenting its affiliation with you or is impersonating you, please let us know. If we find evidence of a Terms of Use violation, we will then be able to suspend the reported account. You can find out more about impersonation here. 3. Copyright Infringement: If the account is hosting content that you own the rights to, you can report this using our Copyright Infringement form. This will allow you to remove content that you own the rights to from SoundCloud. 4. Trademark Violation: If the account is infringing your trademark rights, you can let us know by emailing trademarks@soundcloud.com with proof of your registration. If we find evidence of trademark infringement, we can request that the account owner change their URL and/or Display Name.

A final option is to follow the due legal process to determine ownership of the account in question. If you can obtain a court order or settlement agreement in your favor (regarding the specific profile) we can pass access over to you. While we can appreciate that this process may seem complex, we hope that you can understand that our primary aim is to provide a service that respects both the privacy and security of our community members and their data. This means that we must follow our account ownership policy and related processes at all times.

Legal, Safety & Reporting: Content & Platform Safety

Content security

As a hosting platform, we cannot always guarantee what is uploaded to SoundCloud. However, that doesn’t mean we don’t care about you and your content. #### What would you like to learn more about?

Fake activity on your tracks

You may have noticed that there are websites out there offering an increase in account popularity in exchange for money. These services are in no way associated with SoundCloud, and go against our** **Terms of Use. 

If you are detected for ‘faking’ your popularity on SoundCloud by using these services, you will risk being permanently suspended from the platform.

Please be aware that many of these offerings are likely to be fraudulent or malicious, and we would like to remind you to stay safe online and remain vigilant aboutphishing.

Protecting your content on SoundCloud

Building a platform that helps creators of music and audio share their original content is at the heart of everything we do at SoundCloud. From the outset, we wanted to build a diverse, collaborative community of creators, where the rights of creators are respected. #### What would you like to learn more about?

Scams

We expect the community to be respectful of each other–this is why it is not okay to trick other users into doing something. We have rules in place that forbid scams and content which purposefully misleads others. As with all online platforms, we encourage you to be mindful when communicating with others in the community. In our experience, if something sounds too good to be true, it probably is. Read on to find out more about protecting yourself from scams. #### Misleading information As a platform built with creator needs in mind, we welcome the use of stage names or professional identities on SoundCloud. However, that doesn’t mean that you can post content that is intentionally misleading. As a rough guide, you mustn’t create profiles or post content that is intended to make people think you are someone else. Don’t use someone else’s name or trademark without their permission, or pretend to be associated with someone you aren’t, even if you feel that you are helping that person by doing so. This includes the use of misleading track titles or tags. #### Scams Protecting yourself online is important. While we do all we can to prevent unwanted attempts to access your personal information, there are some things to be aware of that can help you to protect yourself. Here are some tips to remember while using SoundCloud:

  1. Don’t give in to phishing attempts; never reveal any confidential information about yourself or your account details to other community members (via messages, comments or otherwise).

  2. If you are being offered a deal that sounds too good to be true, it probably is. You can find some examples of common scams here.

  3. Be wary of community members who ask for access to your content (e.g. unreleased demos, downloads of private tracks). You never know who is behind this request– it may not be who the profile claims to be.

Remember our key advice: always be extra cautious when interacting with individuals online.

Security

We take the security of our platform and community seriously. Read on to find out more about what you can do to protect your account, and what to do if something goes wrong. #### What would you like to learn more about?

Stream Rippers

SoundCloud uses the most widely supported streaming protocol to ensure your sounds can be played everywhere, by everyone, across the web. When someone hits play on a track, the technology behind this streaming protocol kicks in to ensure the track plays. By using a widely supported streaming technology, we can ensure your content is playable on all devices and browsers.

Websites can exploit inherent vulnerabilities in this streaming technology, allowing them to rip the stream and provide it for download elsewhere. This means they cannot download the original file you uploaded with us, but instead can only stream the audio (128 kbps). This is the downside of using a system that lets you be heard by everyone, everywhere.   There are other streaming protocols that are considered to be more secure, but sadly, they are not as widely supported. By switching the streaming protocol we use, your content would not be playable on certain browsers or devices, preventing people from playing your tracks.    While we are doing all we can to improve this situation, there are several measures you may want to consider to prevent unauthorized downloads of your content. While we cannot guarantee that this will stop these sites from accessing your content without your permission, it will put you in the best position possible to prevent people from downloading content without your consent: - Disable downloads on your tracks. You can learn how to do this here. - Disable app playback, so that your track will not be playable outside of the SoundCloud platform and our own apps (i.e., the official SoundCloud iOS and Android apps). You can learn how to do this here.

Unsafe links on SoundCloud

SoundCloud now defers any links to external sites through our deferral URL https://exit.sc. 

By doing this, we are able to check external sites against a database of blocklisted URLs that have been deemed potentially malicious, harmful, or spammy. If you click on a blocklisted URL, you will be warned with the following message:

We block certain sites to ensure the safety of our users and their accounts. We flag any site that is suspected of hosting content that goes against our Terms of Use, such as containing pornographic content, phishing scams, spam, or malicious software.    If you understand the risks of the site you are attempting to enter, you can continue to the site by clicking “More options”. 

You can report a harmful site to us, or let us know if a site you manage is being blocked, by reporting this activity here.

Legal, Safety & Reporting: Content, Community & Safety Standards

Abuse and harassment policies

We consider abuse to be any activity on SoundCloud where the intention is to deliberately demean, upset, or cause harm to another person. We think that criticism can be helpful if it is shared in a constructive way. Remember, just because someone says something that you disagree with, this does not necessarily mean they are acting in an abusive way. To us, there is a clear difference between an individual providing constructive feedback on content (e.g., “Your guitar is out of tune–if you fixed it, the song would be better”) vs. someone insulting another person (e.g., “You are bad at playing guitar because you are stupid”). 

If you ever find yourself in a situation where you feel uncomfortable or threatened by another SoundCloud member, make sure to speak with a friend or family member about what’s happening. If you receive violent threats and are concerned for your immediate safety, you should also get in touch with your local authorities (as well as letting us know) to ensure your safety. #### If you break the rules We have zero tolerance for abusive or threatening behavior within the community. We consider abuse to be any activity where the intent is to deliberately attack or demean someone else, to harm or upset them. Anyone found to be engaging in this type of activity risks the immediate, permanent termination of their account.

As with all policy violations, we will always send you written warnings should we find that you have broken the Terms of Use. In most cases, we operate a three-strikes rule, meaning that if we need to warn you more than twice, we will terminate your account. We also reserve the right to terminate accounts immediately for gross violations of the Terms of Use.

Community conflict policies

SoundCloud is an open, social platform, made up of a vibrant group of people with differing views, opinions, and cultural backgrounds. We support freedom of speech and the fundamental right for individuals to express themselves, and expect everyone else to do the same. With a diverse community, it can be expected that individuals will not always agree and that conflicts will happen. We encourage users to be respectful, even if they passionately disagree with each other. We also recognize that sometimes conflict becomes too personal, which can be very upsetting. Our policies recognize the difference between healthy conflict and outright abuse–we take allegations of abuse seriously and will always help in whatever way we can. #### Read more about our policies on:

Content policies

As an open platform, freedom of expression is important to us. However, there are certain types of content that have no place on SoundCloud. #### Prohibited Content on Our Platform To protect the community and maintain positivity, please don’t post: ##### Pornography: Remember that SoundCloud can be accessed by people as young as 13. Don’t post any content that is predominantly sexual in nature, or that could be perceived as an aid to sexual gratification. This includes, but is not limited to, images containing nudity and recordings or detailed descriptions of sexual acts. There are plenty of other places to find that content online. ##### Hate speech: You are welcome to share your opinions and beliefs on SoundCloud, even if they might be controversial or challenge the status quo. However, we will not tolerate content that promotes or encourages hatred, discrimination, or violence against others based on things like race, cultural identity or ethnic background, religious beliefs, disability, gender identity, or sexual orientation. ##### Violence; incitement & promotion: We want to uphold a positive atmosphere for the community–we do not tolerate any use of intimidation or threats of violence between users or against the wider public. Any threatening content will be removed when it is reported to our team. 

We will also remove any content that promotes or incites violence against others, e.g., we don’t accept graphic images of real or dramatized violence that have been uploaded to shock members of the community. ##### Extremism & illegal content: While we encourage everyone to share their opinions and beliefs, it is not acceptable to use SoundCloud to share illegal material or content related to extremist ideologies. We will remove all content and accounts that share this type of material when it is reported to our team for review. ##### Privacy violations: We believe that everyone has the right to privacy, no matter who they are. That’s why it is not ok to share personal details of another person (or entity) without their permission. This includes recordings of private conversations, photographs, unlisted phone numbers, and home or email addresses. #### If you break the rules If we receive notification from a rightsholder that any content uploaded to your account infringes their copyright, or if we believe that your activity violates any of our other guidelines, we will send you a written warning. If we have to send you more than two of these warnings, we will terminate your account. In the most extreme cases, we reserve the right to terminate your account immediately, without prior warning.

Policies on promotional services and advertising

SoundCloud aims to help creators to connect directly with their fans. We understand that promoting your work is important, and we encourage you to seek out fans and other like-minded individuals. In our experience, the most successful forms of promotion are built upon meaningful interactions between creators and their audience. That’s why the use of promotional services which sell social interactions is against the rules. Read on to find out more about our stance on these services, and what we do to combat fake activity. #### What would you like to learn our policies on?

Using or charing for Promotional Services

Any service that offers to sell social interactions or other types of promotional activities on SoundCloud is strictly prohibited. This includes services that charge users to repost content or upload material onto another user’s profile. We view charging for promotional activities as a form of unauthorized advertising, which directly violates our Terms of Use. Such practices undermine the integrity of the platform and are not tolerated. These types of services are often fraudulent or malicious in nature. They may attempt to deceive users or compromise their accounts. We strongly encourage you to exercise caution while online and remain vigilant against phishing attempts and other scams that could jeopardize your personal information or account security. If you artificially inflate your popularity on SoundCloud using banned services, you risk consequences, including permanent suspension and loss of your account and content. We prioritize authentic interactions to keep the community fair and trustworthy.

Legal, Safety & Reporting: Legal

Creators and the EU AI Act

Creators who are subject to the transparency requirements of the EU AI Act (“the Act”) under Article 50(4), are encouraged to disclose that their covered content is “AI-generated or manipulated” within their track description on SoundCloud. Please keep in mind that uploading any content that has been generated or manipulated with AI to SoundCloud must strictly comply with SoundCloud’s Community Guidelines and Terms of Use (our “platform policies”), including our platform policies on copyright, impersonation, harassment, misinformation, hateful or abusive content, and unlawful or harmful content. Creators are responsible for making sure that any AI tools used to generate or modify audio, lyrics, artwork, or other content respect the copyright and other legal rights of other artists and rightsholders, creators, and individuals. AI-generated or manipulated content must also not intentionally mislead listeners about its authenticity, origin, or the identity of the creator - impersonation and identity theft is strictly forbidden. This includes using AI tools, such as voice-cloning or likeness-generation tools, to imitate or represent another artist, creator, or individual in a way that is unauthorised, misleading, or otherwise violates SoundCloud’s platform policies. This guidance is intended to help creators to understand SoundCloud’s expectations around AI-generated and AI-manipulated content. Creators are responsible for understanding and complying with any legal obligations that may apply to them, including under the EU AI Act.

Defamation

Defamation (also referred to as slander or libel) is defined as accusing someone of an action they should not be held responsible for, with the outcome of damaging an individual’s reputation. Typically, defamatory content is presented as fact with or without evidence to back up assertions being made. 

SoundCloud does not tolerate defamation, whether made via spoken word (this is classed as slander), comments, messages, or any other written means (this is classed as libel). Activity deemed defamatory will be removed from the platform, and members defaming others will receive a warning or have their account terminated. #### If you break the rules We reserve the right to remove anything reported to us that is in breach of our Terms of Use or Community Guidelines (which you have agreed to adhere to by signing up to use SoundCloud), including any content that we deem to be otherwise unacceptable based on our reasonable discretion.

As such, we will remove content from your account if it has been reported to us, and is found to be defamatory. For this content to be reinstated, you would be required to provide supporting evidence to demonstrate the factual basis for the statements being made.

Law enforcement disclosure requests

In line with our Privacy Policy, we can only disclose requested information to a competent authority when we are obliged to do so by applicable law. If you are a law enforcement authority seeking information about SoundCloud users and accounts in the course of criminal investigations, please refer to our** **Law Enforcement Guidelines for details on submitting requests.

Legal

Our Terms of Use, together with our Privacy Policy, Cookies Policy and Community Guidelines constitute a legally binding agreement between you and SoundCloud in relation to your use of the platform. 

As well as forming the legal basis for your use of SoundCloud, these important documents will help you to understand how you can uphold the values and expectations we have for the community. This section of the Help Center will explain in more detail our policies on legal issues like trademark infringement, defamation and processing requests for user information. #### Please review the resources available below: Law Enforcement Guidelines - This guide is for law enforcement authorities seeking     information about SoundCloud users and accounts in the course of criminal investigations. It is also intended as a reference for SoundCloud users who are interested in finding out more about our policies and processes for handling law enforcement requests.

Terms of Use - This is the legal document that you agree to follow when you sign up for an account–think of it as the rules for using SoundCloud. Community Guidelines - This is where you can find out more about the expectations we have for everyone who uses SoundCloud. It is based on our Terms of Use, but uses less legal language, so it is easier to understand. 

Privacy Policy - This is where you can find out more about the specific data we collect, how we store it and what we use it for. 

Cookies Policy -  This is part of our Privacy Policy but focuses more specifically on our use of cookies and related technologies. We also share more information on how you can opt-out of specific services. 

Copyright Page - Find out more about copyright and our approach to protecting creators rights. #### What would you like more assistance with?

Reporting trademark infringement

As a platform built with the needs of creators in mind, we take protecting trademark rights seriously. 

If you would like content to be removed from SoundCloud that infringes your trademark rights, please contact our Trust & Safety team using our chatbot feature and provide us with the following details: 1. The full URL where the allegedly infringing material is located 2. Your full name, address, email, and telephone number 3. Your trademark registration number, and the countries in which your trademark is registered 4. A brief explanation of how the reported content infringes your trademark 5. The statement: “I have a good faith belief that use of the trademarks described above on SoundCloud is not authorized by the trademark owner or its agent, nor is such use otherwise permissible under law.” 6. The statement: “I represent that the information in this notification is true and correct and that I am authorized to act on behalf of the trademark owner.” 7. Scanned copy of your physical signature

Please note: by submitting a takedown notification, you consent to having your information revealed to parties involved in the case.

User data requests

SoundCloud collects unique personal data — email, sign-up, and last seen at IP, audio files, month, and year of birth— for each account on the platform. We do this so we can get to know our community members and better serve their needs.

In cases where legal authorities request data about our users, we require the requesting party to adhere to the guidelines set out in our Law Enforcement Guidelines. We will only release user data in cases where we are legally required to do so.

Legal, Safety & Reporting: Legal & Regulatory Transparency

European Union Digital Services Act (DSA) Resolution Options

This policy applies only to users covered by the European Union’s Digital Services Act (DSA). SoundCloud may take certain restrictive actions on your content or account if we believe you have violated the law, any of our Terms (including the Terms of Use** and Community Guidelines, Monetization Terms of Use), or may decide not to act on a report you submitted regarding potential illegal or Terms-violating content. When this happens, and you disagree with our decision, you may be able to refer your matter to an out-of-court dispute settlement body. You may wish to first dispute SoundCloud’s decision using our internal disputes process, resulting from the first decision you received via email. What is an out-of-court dispute settlement body under the DSA? Out-of-court dispute settlement bodies are independent bodies with the means and expertise to consider the issues brought to them. The DSA requires that each Member State certify out-of-court settlement bodies to handle eligible disputes. What types of complaints are eligible for out-of-court dispute settlement under the DSA?** Matters may be referred to a certified out-of-court dispute settlement body in the following circumstances: 1. The visibility of your content, your ability to monetize content, or your account has been restricted because SoundCloud determined that your content was illegal or violated one of our Terms. 2. You reported content that you believe violated the law or our Terms, and SoundCloud did not remove the content.

How will SoundCloud comply with this process? SoundCloud will work with the out-of-court settlement body where required by law. SoundCloud is not bound by any decisions made by these out-of-court settlement bodies. The exact process for seeking out-of-court settlement resolution has not yet been established, and the process may vary depending upon the Member State. We will update this site as information becomes available. Additional options may be available You may have the option to dispute SoundCloud’s decision through our internal disputes process. If you’ve received any communication from SoundCloud about the option to dispute, please check it for more information. For more information on our internal disputes process, please check our Moderation & Enforcement Policies. You also have the option to pursue your claims in court. If you have legal questions or wish to examine legal options that may be available to you, you may want to consult with your own legal counsel.

Updates to our Monetization Terms of Service - October 31, 2025

We recently updated our Monetization Terms of Service, effective October 31, 2025. These updates include new and clarified provisions related to SoundCloud’s distribution service fee, eligibility criteria, program termination process, and artificial streaming, among other areas. Below is a summary of the key changes: - Update to the distribution fee: SoundCloud’s distribution fee is now 0% (previously 20%) meaning artists keep 100% of their distribution royalties. - Expanded eligibility: Some users who were previously categorized as “Existing Report Artists” are now eligible to benefit from 0% distribution fee. - Third-party payment processing: SoundCloud may now pass along third party payment processing fees to users, rather than absorbing them (as it did previously when a distribution fee was applied). - Artist Subscription definition: Clarified which subscriptions are included in the definition of “Artist Subscription”. - Monetization eligibility: Clarified and updated which users and content are eligible for monetization. - Program termination notice: SoundCloud may now notify users of termination via email, in-app notification, or any reasonable means of communication (e.g., within the user’s SoundCloud profile). - Rejoining the program: Users who rejoin the monetization program within 30 days of termination will not be required to re-accept the Terms. - Artificial streaming: Reaffirmed that artificial streaming is not permitted on SoundCloud and that the company may reset stream counts for tracks affected by automated, artificial, or fraudulent activity.

Please note: the list above is a high-level summary of the primary updates and is not exhaustive. We encourage all users to thoroughly review the full Monetization Terms of Service for complete details here. In the event of any conflict between this summary and the Terms, The Terms will govern.

As we continue to build new social and recommendation features, we want to make sure our community understands how their actions shape their own experience and the experience of others on our platform. We encourage you to read the full Terms of Use and Privacy Policy. Following are some key updates to our Terms of Use (ToU) and Privacy Policy effective September 24, 2025 in the U.S., Canada, U.K., Ireland, Australia, New Zealand, with rollout to other markets following thereafter: - Discovery & Recommendation Features:

SoundCloud is more than just a listening platform – it’s a place to discover what’s next and connect through music. These updates clarify how profile information and on-platform activity (such as likes, comments, and follows) may help power new discovery and recommendation features that amplify connection. - Trust & Transparency: 

These updates don’t represent a shift in SoundCloud’s mission. They’re about giving you more clarity and control. We want you to understand how your activity on the platform may help improve both your own experience and the musical experiences of others. The updates also provide greater visibility and create the framework for upcoming features that showcase SoundCloud’s vibrant communities and celebrate the great taste of our users. Legal, Safety & Reporting: Platform Rules & Use Policies

Account Ownership Policies

The only means we have of verifying the ownership of an account is the email address that was used to create the account. This means that the individual who controls the original email address used at sign up, is the owner of that account.   Our account ownership policy is designed to protect the security and privacy of our community, as well as satisfying our responsibilities as a service provider, in relation to applicable laws. #### Deceased users Only verified, immediate family members or those authorized to act on behalf of the deceased’s estate can gain access to the account of that SoundCloud community member. After a number of  verification questions, we can - lock or delete the account, or transfer ownership, depending on your wishes. #### Minor users Protecting the privacy of our community members (particularly those who are minors) is a priority for us. 

Users must agree to our Terms of Use** on signup in order to have a valid SoundCloud account. These terms clearly state that you must be “either 18 years of age or more, or if you are under 18 years of age, you are 16 years of age or more if you reside in the European Union or 13 years of age or more if you reside in the United States or anywhere else”. ##### If you break the rules** If we receive reports that an account was set up by a minor without the permission of their parents, we will remove the reported account and send an email notification to the account owner. We will only restore these accounts if the account owner can provide us with evidence that they are over 18, or that they have parental permission.

Feature Use Policies

SoundCloud aims to help creators to connect directly with their fans. We understand that promoting your work is important, and we encourage you to seek out fans and other like-minded individuals. In our experience, the most successful forms of promotion are built upon meaningful interactions between creators and their audience. However, there is a fine line between developing these connections and oversharing with community members. #### You can be blocked from accessing specific feature(s) on-site if you are doing any of the following: - You’re posting similar comments or messages from your account (avoid copy and pasting, or sending comments or messages with the same links over and over) - You’re following a lot of accounts in a short time period - You’re following a lot of accounts you recently unfollowed - You’re liking or reposting a lot of tracks in one day (make sure you listen to any sound before liking or reposting it) - You’re liking or reposting a lot of tracks you recently removed from your likes or reposts - A number of community members have manually flagged your account, messages, or comments as spam

Warnings

We have on-site limits in place to encourage the growth of genuine, close-knit communities around creators’ tracks. These limits look for accounts that appear to be using a feature in a way other than intended and can block access to that feature.   Our anti-spam systems are automated and focus on detecting accounts that are performing the same activity in large numbers within a 24-hour period.    When you are being warned that you may end up in a block soon, you will see this message: When you see your first warning, you must acknowledge it by clicking “Yes, I understand” before you can carry on using the feature. Please note that if you continue to use the feature after agreeing that you understood the warning you received, you may be blocked. #### Blocks If you’ve previously received and accepted a warning, any time you hit this on-site limit again, you will be blocked from using that feature. You will receive a message similar to this one: If you are in a block, you will be unable to use the feature for a period of time. The length of this period depends on whether you have been in a block before. The more often you run up against the same limit, the longer that block will become, and it will tell you when the block will expire in the block warning.

Please note: no matter what subscription level you have, we cannot manually remove any blocks to ensure fairness for all our users.

Policy Resources

Our Terms of Use, together with our Privacy Policy, Cookies Policy, and Community Guidelines, constitute a legally binding agreement between you and SoundCloud in relation to your use of the platform. 

As well as forming the legal basis for your use of SoundCloud, these important documents will help you understand how to uphold the values and expectations we have for the community. This section of the Help Center will explain our policies in more detail on specific issues such as spam, hate speech, and abusive behavior. #### Please review the resources available below:  Terms of Use - This is the legal document that you agree to follow when you sign up for an account–think of it as the rules for using SoundCloud. 

Community Guidelines - This is where you can find out more about the expectations we have for everyone who uses SoundCloud. It is based on our Terms of Use but uses less legal language, making it easier to understand.

It is also intended as a reference for SoundCloud users interested in learning more about our policies and processes for handling law enforcement requests. #### What else would you like to learn about our policy on?

Sale of Accounts

You can’t sell or offer to sell any SoundCloud account or URL. The sale of accounts or URLs is prohibited in our Terms of Use, as outlined below:

“You must not sell or transfer, or offer to sell or transfer, any SoundCloud account to any third party without the prior written approval of SoundCloud.” #### If you break the rules If we receive reports that you have attempted to sell an account or URL, your account will be terminated immediately, without any prior notification.

SoundCloud Public APIs

We are offering access to our public APIs for you to develop cool new ideas to enjoy music even more! You can apply for access by talking to our AI agent and providing some information, such as your name and a description of your app, so our team can review your request and create credentials for you. #### Allowed usage of SoundCloud public APIs You can find all information about the Do’s and Don’ts in our API Terms of Use. Generally, our public APIs cannot be used for commercial use cases, but also some non-commercial applications that are frequently requested are not possible, for example: - Developing a Discord bot - Mixing music from SoundCloud with other content, e.g., for videos or within games - Downloading or storing of any content on SoundCloud

If you break the rules

If we have reason to believe that you are acting in breach of our API Terms of Use, or if we object to your use of the SoundCloud API for any other reason, we will revoke your access to the SoundCloud API by invalidating your client ID and client secret. Any attempt to circumvent this and obtain a new client ID and client secret is strictly prohibited. #### API development help and resources You can find everything you need to know on our developer website. Legal, Safety & Reporting: Privacy

Account privacy

We want to make sure you are in control of your account and it’s privacy when using SoundCloud and we have tools and settings in place to help with this. #### What can we help with?

California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA)

Go To:

What is the CCPA? What is SoundCloud doing to comply? What can I request regarding my data under the CCPA? How does SoundCloud process my data? How can I manage my data? How can I delete my data? #### What is the CCPA? The California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA) is a privacy and consumer protection regulation applicable to residents of California (US), which is enforceable as of January 1st, 2020. CCPA brings with it an array of new consumer data rights for residents of California and regulatory requirements aimed at giving these individuals more visibility into and control over how their personal data is used. #### What is SoundCloud doing to comply? As part of our efforts to ensure we’re compliant with the CCPA and implementing best practices for our users, we have updated our Privacy Policy to explain how we use your personal data and provide more detail about your ability to manage the information you share with us. We will also continue to evaluate and update our business practices as further regulatory guidance becomes available. #### What can I request regarding my data under the CCPA? Under the CCPA,  you can request the following, subject to certain exceptions and limitations: - Right to Know: You can request information about the types of personal data collected from you and the intended uses for this data. - Right of Access: You can request that we provide a copy of the personal data we hold about you in a portable format. - Right of Deletion: You can request deletion of certain personal data we hold about you. - Right to Opt-Out: You can opt out of the “sale” of PI. SoundCloud does not transfer or share data in exchange for money or otherwise sell data in the conventional sense. However, the sharing of personal information to third-party advertising partners to provide you with personalized advertising may constitute a “sale” for purposes of CCPA. - Right to Non-Discrimination: SoundCloud must refrain from discriminating against users for exercising their privacy/data rights under CCPA. SoundCloud can also not deny users goods/services,  offer a different level of service, charge users a different price, or impose penalties for exercising their right under CCPA.

If you’d like to submit a request regarding your personal data under the CCPA, please use our chatbot feature. #### How does SoundCloud process my data? Our** Privacy Policy explains in detail how SoundCloud processes your data and the controls available to you to manage that data. We recommend reading it and reaching out to us if you have any additional questions or feedback. #### How can I manage my data? To give you more control over how your data is used, there are options available to adjust your account settings, including Communications, Analytics, and Advertising settings. Please ensure you restart the app or refresh the browser for these to take effect. #### How can I delete my data?** If you wish to no longer have any information on SoundCloud, you can delete your SoundCloud account by signing in on a computer and going to Account Settings. Once you request this deletion, it will automatically be removed from public view, and within a short time period, SoundCloud will completely delete the account and will no longer hold any personally identifiable information about you.

General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR)

Go To:

What is the GDPR? What changes does it make to SoundCloud? What can I request regarding my data under the GDPR? How can I correct my account information? How do you process my data? What is a Data Processing Agreement? I use SoundCloud’s embedded players on my website. What do I need to know? How can I opt out of Cookies or revoke consent? #### What is the GDPR? The General Data Protection Regulation(GDPR) is a data privacy and protection regulation passed by the European Commission, which regulates the processing of personal information and is enforceable as of May 25th, 2018. GDPR brings with it an array of new individual rights and regulatory requirements aimed at giving individuals more visibility into and control over how their data is used. #### What changes does it make to SoundCloud? To ensure we’re compliant with the GDPR and implementing best practices for our users, we have updated our Terms of Use and Privacy Policy** to explain to SoundCloud users, like you, how we use your data and provide more detail about your ability to manage the information you share with us, and the new tools we’ve created to help you do that. To give you more control over how your data is used, we’ve implemented new account settings, including Communications, Analytics, and Advertising settings. Please ensure you restart the app or refresh the browser for these to take effect. #### What can I request regarding my data under the GDPR?** Under the GDPR, you can request the following: - Right of access: your right to receive confirmation of whether a company is processing your personal data, to access your personal data, and to receive a copy of it - Right to rectification: your right to have inaccurate or incomplete data rectified - Right to erasure (right to be forgotten): your right to have your personal data erased under certain conditions - Right to restrict processing: your right to restrict the processing of your personal data in certain circumstances - Right to object to processing: your right to object to the processing of your personal data under certain circumstances - Right to data portability: your right to receive a copy of your personal data in a commonly used, machine-readable format and to have that data transmitted to another party where technically feasible

If you’d like to submit a request regarding your personal data under the GDPR, please use our chatbot feature to file a ticket. #### How can I correct my account information? If there’s information contained in your account that is not correct, you have a few ways to update it. In your Account Settings,when signed in on a computer, you can update your birth month and year, gender, email address, and connected applications like Facebook and Google. From your Profile Edit Settings,** you can also change your real name, location, display name, or URL that is displayed publicly. #### How do you process my data? Our Privacy Policy explains in detail how SoundCloud processes your data and the controls available to you to manage that data. We recommend reading it and reaching out to us if you have any additional questions or feedback. #### What is a Data Processing Agreement? Under GDPR, data controllers are obligated to enter into a written “data processing agreement” with service providers (known as processors) engaged to process data on their behalf, to evidence that the processor will operate in compliance with GDPR. However, data processing agreements do not apply to the relationship between SoundCloud and its users, since users do not process data on behalf of SoundCloud. #### I use SoundCloud’s embedded players on my website. What do I need to know? If you’re using SoundCloud’s embed players on your own website, you need to let your users know that you are doing so and link to our Cookie Policy, so they can understand more. We suggest adding this to your legal pages, such as the Privacy Policy or Terms of Use. You need to do this as SoundCloud may collect usage data for analytics purposes, and it is therefore your responsibility to disclose this to visitors of any site where you embed the player. Please note you do not require a data processing agreement if using our embedded players. #### How can I opt out of Cookies or revoke consent? You can read about making changes and opting out of Cookies from our Cookies Policy.** Please see the section from “Your Choices and Controls” onwards. You can change any options with how SoundCloud uses (or therefore doesn’t use) your information, either within SoundCloud or with third parties, by changing yourAdvertising,Analytics,** andCommunications settings. You can also change what emails and notifications you receive from ushere. However, please read through our updatedPrivacy andCookies **Policies regarding what information we collect and store and why. Things such as your email address are needed to have an account with SoundCloud. If you wish to no longer have any information on SoundCloud, you can delete your SoundCloud account by signing in on a computer and going to Account Settings. Once you request this deletion, it will automatically be removed from public view, and within a short time period, SoundCloud will completely delete the account and will no longer hold any personally identifiable information about you.

Manage Privacy for Your SoundCloud Profile and Content

It’s not possible to make your account entirely private. The following will always be publicly available to anyone who visits your profile: - Your profile artwork, description, and website links - Your likes - Your re-posts - Comments you’ve made - Who you follow - Who follows you

However, you can make all your uploads and playlists private. This means no one can listen to your tracks without your explicit permission. You can read more about changing your track or playlist privacy settings here. #### Tips for Maintaining Privacy on SoundCloud To protect your privacy: 1. Regularly Update Privacy Settings:Check and adjust your privacy settings often to control interactions and profile visibility. 2. Manage Interactions:Since likes, reposts, comments, and follows are always public, be selective about your interactions if you want to maintain a lower profile. 3. Block Users:Block someone to stop them from following, messaging, or commenting on your tracks. To block, visit their profile, click the three dots, and select “Block.” 4. Control Messages:You can limit who can message you—either only your followers or anyone. Adjust this in your privacy settings under messaging options. 5. Controlling Search Visibility:You can’t hide your profile from search engines through SoundCloud settings, but you can request removal or updates via Google Search Console.

What strategies can users employ to maintain privacy for specific content on SoundCloud?

To maintain privacy for specific content: 1. Make Uploads and Playlists Private: You have the option to make all of your uploads and playlists private. When you set content to private, it will not be visible or accessible to others unless you explicitly permit them. 2. This is a useful strategy for sharing content with a select audience or keeping certain tracks and playlists hidden from public view. 3. Adjust Track and Playlist Privacy Settings:If you want to control who can listen to your tracks or playlists, consider changing the privacy settingsfor each upload. You can make a track or playlist private at any time, even after it has been uploaded. 4. Limit Public Information on Your Profile:Although your profile artwork, description, and website links are public, you can choose to limit the amount of personal information you share in these sections. Consider using general or artist-related information rather than personal details.

Managing SoundCloud Profile Visibility in Search Engine Results

If you want to reduce the chances of your SoundCloud profile appearing in Google search results: #### Change Your Display Name and Profile URL: - Consider changing your Display Name and Profile URL to a stage name or an alias. This strategy can help separate your identity from your SoundCloud presence, making it less likely for your account to be linked to your real name in search results.

Manage Your Images:

  • Sometimes, even after removing content from SoundCloud, it may still appear in Google search results due to cached pages.
  • To resolve this, click through the image in the search results to check if it’s still hosted on SoundCloud’s servers. If the URL starts withhttp://i1.sndcdn.com/ and the image appears, it’s still on their servers. If the image has been removed, you’ll see a page indicating that the content is no longer available.

Contact Google for Removal:

  • Since SoundCloud can’t control how Google stores or displays cached information, the most effective way to remove your profile or personal information is to contact Google directly. You can do this by filling out their public removal form and requesting that your information be removed from their search results.

Understand the Limits of Influence:

  • While SoundCloud cannot stop Google from indexing its content or control how long Google caches search results, removing personal information from your SoundCloud profile will eventually lead to it being updated in search engines as they refresh their data over time.

What are some alternative strategies to maintain privacy on SoundCloud?

  • Use a Stage Name or Alias: Consider using a pseudonym or stage name for your SoundCloud profile, which can help keep your real identity separate from your online persona.
  • Regularly Monitor Search Results: Keep an eye on search results for your name and profile to ensure that any unwanted information is no longer visible. If you find something that shouldn’t be there, take the necessary steps to remove it, either through SoundCloud or by contacting Google.

Privacy on SoundCloud

We believe that everyone has the right to privacy, no matter who they are. At SoundCloud, your privacy is important to us. 

We have a pretty simple approach to data protection and privacy, which can be summarized as follows: - You should have full control over your information - You should know exactly what we do with your information - You should never share personal details of another person (or entity) without their permission. This includes recordings, photographs, unlisted phone numbers, and home or email addresses.

Resources

Please refer to the resources below for more detailed information about how we collect, store, and use your data, as well as the policies we have in place to protect your privacy. 

Privacy Policy - This is where you can find out more about the specific data we collect, how we store it, and what we use it for. 

Cookie Policy - This is part of our Privacy Policy, but focuses more specifically on our use of cookies and related technologies. We also share more information on how you can opt out of specific services. 

Community Guidelines- This is where you can find out more about the expectations we have for everyone who uses SoundCloud. It is based on our Terms of Use, but uses less legal language, so it is easier to understand. #### Learn how to protect your privacy while using SoundCloud:

Privacy within the SoundCloud community

There are a few different ways to maintain privacy on SoundCloud. Learn more about these through:

Protecting your privacy

Privacy Matters

We believe everyone has the right to privacy—no matter who they are. Sharing someone’s personal details without their permission is not acceptable. #### What’s Not Allowed on SoundCloud #### Unauthorized Sharing of Confidential Information Never share another person’s (or entity’s) private information without their consent. This includes: - Photographs - Unlisted phone numbers - Home addresses - Email addresses

Unauthorized Distribution of Audio Recordings

Before sharing any recorded conversation, you must have: 1. Permission from everyone involved to record the conversation 2. Separate permission from everyone involved to share the recording

Uploading private conversations without consent from all participants is a violation of privacy. #### If Your Privacy Has Been Violated If you believe your privacy rights have been infringed, we strongly encourage you to report the incident. Reporting helps protect not only your rights, but also those of others who may be affected. If you believe that your rights have been infringed upon or violated in any way, we strongly encourage you to report the incident. Reporting such issues helps protect not only your own rights but also the rights of others who may be affected.

Stream Rippers

SoundCloud uses the most widely supported streaming protocol to ensure your sounds can be played everywhere, by everyone, across the web. When someone hits play on a track, the technology behind this streaming protocol kicks in to ensure the track plays. By using a widely supported streaming technology, we can ensure your content is playable on all devices and browsers.

Websites can exploit inherent vulnerabilities in this streaming technology, allowing them to rip the stream and provide it for download elsewhere. This means they cannot download the original file you uploaded with us, but instead can only stream the audio (128 kbps). This is the downside of using a system that lets you be heard by everyone, everywhere.   There are other streaming protocols that are considered to be more secure, but sadly, they are not as widely supported. By switching the streaming protocol we use, your content would not be playable on certain browsers or devices, preventing people from playing your tracks.    While we are doing all we can to improve this situation, there are several measures you may want to consider to prevent unauthorized downloads of your content. While we cannot guarantee that this will stop these sites from accessing your content without your permission, it will put you in the best position possible to prevent people from downloading content without your consent: - Disable downloads on your tracks. You can learn how to do this here. - Disable app playback, so that your track will not be playable outside of the SoundCloud platform and our own apps (i.e., the official SoundCloud iOS and Android apps). You can learn how to do this here.

Legal, Safety & Reporting: Report Abuse, Safety & Harmful Content

Reporting abuse or harassment

If you’re having trouble with another SoundCloud member, we don’t want you to feel like you are alone; we are here to help. First, we would advise** **blocking anyone you don’t want to interact with and avoiding going to their profile.

If this communication is part of a back-and-forth exchange between you and another person, we’d suggest removing yourself from the conflict first. Then, if this person continues to contact you, you can let us know, and we can see what we can do to help.

Due to the sensitive nature of these situations, we don’t accept reports from third parties because we want to help you personally, as quickly as we can. To do this best, we need to hear from you directly. If you are concerned about another person, please ask them to write to us.

Remember that we can only make decisions based on the information we have available to us. This means that we cannot accept reports of activity that happens externally from SoundCloud. #### Report Abuse or Harassment If you would like to report abuse or harassment, please provide our chatbot with the following details: 1. Your URL 2. The URL of the account you want to report 3. A brief explanation of the conflict 4. Links to the abusive content, e.g., track URLs

If the conflict is via comments or messages, please provide us with screenshots of this activity.

Reporting defamation

Defamation (also referred to as slander or libel) is defined as accusing someone of an action they should not be held responsible for, with the outcome of damaging an individual’s reputation. Typically, defamatory content is presented as fact, with or without evidence to back up the assertions. #### Reporting defamation For us to take action, there must be a clear link between the reported content and your personal identity. Please note that decisions will be based solely on the information available to us on our own platform. In cases where no sufficient association can be made between the reported content and your identity, the content will remain on SoundCloud.

Please note: we can only accept reports from those directly involved in these cases. We may require you to provide photo identification to verify your identity.

If you would like to report defamation, please provide us with the following details using our chatbot feature: 1. The URL of the content you want to report (please provide the exact timestamp where your name is mentioned) 2. A brief explanation of how the content is defamatory 3. Any further information to support your case

Reporting extremism and illegal content

At SoundCloud, it is not acceptable to use the platform to share illegal material or content related to extremist ideologies, including any content promoting, supporting, or inciting terrorism. 

We strictly prohibit the dissemination of terrorist content and are committed to its prompt removal from the platform. While we take into consideration UN, US, and EU lists of terrorist designated organizations, we also follow and enforce the details Pursuant to Article 3 of Regulation (EU) 2021/784 of the European Parliament and of the Council. We encourage you to report any content or behavior that may violate our policies against terrorism or other illegal and extremist content. Any user-reported content that is subsequently categorized as illegal following review is considered to be an urgent request and is removed as a priority. We ensure to carry out our review process as soon as possible and will remove all content and accounts that share this type of material when it is reported to our team. #### Reporting extremism and illegal content If you would like to report extremist or illegal content, please provide us with the following details: - The URL of the account you want to report - Links to the content to be reviewed, e.g., track URLs - A brief explanation of how the content violates our Terms of Use, Community Guidelines , or applicable law

It is also possible to report content under The Network Enforcement Act,where applicable.

Reporting hate speech

We will not tolerate content that promotes or encourages hatred, discrimination or violence against others based on things like race, cultural identity or ethnic background, religious beliefs, disability, gender identity, or sexual orientation. #### Reporting hate speech If you would like to report hate speech, please provide us with the following details using our chatbot feature: 1. The URL of the account you want to report 2. Links to the hateful content, e.g. track URLs 3. A brief explanation of how the content violates our Terms of Use or Community Guidelines

Reporting incitement or promotion of violence

We want to uphold a positive atmosphere for the community–we do not tolerate any use of intimidation or threats of violence between users or against the wider public. Any threatening content will be removed when it is reported to our team. 

We will also remove any content that promotes or incites violence against others, e.g., we don’t accept graphic images of real or dramatized violence that have been uploaded to shock members of the community. #### Reporting incitement and promotion of violence If you would like to report violent content, please provide us with the following details using our chatbot feature: 1. The URL of the account you want to report 2. Links to the content to be reviewed e.g., track URLs 3. A brief explanation of how the content violates our** Terms of Use **or Community Guidelines

Reporting pornographic content

Pornography is content that is predominantly sexual in nature, or that could be perceived as an aid to sexual gratification, and is not allowed on the SoundCloud platform. This includes, but is not limited to, images containing nudity and recordings or detailed descriptions of sexual acts. #### Reporting pornographic content If you would like to report pornographic content, please provide us with the following details through the contact button below this article: 1. The URL of the account you want to report 2. Links to the content to be reviewed, e.g., track URLs 3. A brief explanation of how the content violates our Terms of Use or Community Guidelines

Please note: we are currently seeing a series of pornographic spam accounts. These are fake accounts created to use SoundCloud profiles to redirect people to external websites, such as through their profile descriptions, messages, or comments. If you come across these types of accounts, please report them using our on-site Spam Report feature. This will help our team more quickly identify and remove this fake activity.

Reporting privacy violations

We believe that everyone has the right to privacy, no matter who they are. That’s why it is not ok to share personal details of another person (or entity), without their permission. This includes recordings of private conversations, photographs, unlisted phone numbers, and home or email addresses.

For content to be removed, you must be personally identifiable within the reported content, in addition to your voice being used. This means we must be able to link the recording and your personal identity (note that nicknames and aliases alone are not considered personally identifiable information). #### Reporting privacy violations Please note: we can only accept reports from those directly involved in these cases. We may require you to provide photo identification to verify your identity.

If you would like to report privacy violations, please provide us with the following details using our chatbot feature: 1. The URL of the account you want to report 2. Links to the content to be reviewed e.g., track URLs (please provide the exact timestamp where your voice can be heard/where your name is mentioned) 3. A brief explanation of how the content violates your privacy, e.g. is your full name used? Is any other confidential information shared?

Additionally, to help us moderate these cases, we will ask a series of questions to help us to verify your identity and determine your association with the content.

Legal, Safety & Reporting: Report Account & Profile Issues

Reporting a deceased community member

Due to legal restrictions, we can only pass access over to immediate family members, or those authorized to act on behalf of the estate. We require the following information in order to process these requests: - The Display Name or Profile URL of the deceased user’s account - Your email address - A copy of your photo ID (in order to confirm your identity) - A copy of the deceased user’s death certificate - A link to an online obituary (optional)

Please send us the above information via email to: legal@soundcloud.com and we will respond to you as soon as possible.

Reporting a minor on the platform

If we receive reports that an account was set up by a minor without the permission of their parents, we will remove the reported account and send an email notification to the account owner. We will only restore these accounts if the account owner can provide us with evidence that they are over 18, or that they have parental permission. #### To report a minor, please provide us with the following details: 1. The URL of the account you want to report 2. A brief explanation of your relationship to the account owner

Reporting a spam account

We’re continually working to fight against spam, but sometimes we can’t catch it all. With your help we’ll have a better chance! You can “Report” any account you suspect to be a fake, or spam account. This will also block that account from interacting with you, and remove previous comments, like or reposts made on your content. You can report from the account’s profile page, your notifications, or messages through the “Report” button, like this: (image: Screen_Recording_2017-01-30_at_12.42_PM.gif) If you see a spam comment on your own tracks you also have the option when deleting the comment to report it for spam. You will need to be signed in to delete and report comments. All reports will be reviewed by our team, and all accounts known to be spam will be removed. We appreciate your patience while we review all the accounts reported to us.

Reporting impersonation

If you have found an account that is using the same Display Name as you, please remember that it is unlikely that any name is unique. It may be that another user has the same name (or artist name) as you and has no intention of impersonating you.

We consider impersonation to be when an account is set up with the sole intention of pretending to be a genuine representation of another individual or group. This means that it would need to be clear when looking at an account that the intention is to convince others that the reported profile is in fact individual X or group Y. Therefore, when investigating reports of impersonation, we take the entirety of an account into consideration e.g. Profile URL, Display Name, profile description, artwork etc.

In our experience, using the same Display Name as another person does not always mean that the intention is to impersonate. That being said, if you come across an account that you feel is impersonating you, we can help. Before contacting us, please check if the account you are concerned about has been set up on your behalf. #### If you would like to report impersonation, please provide us with the following details: - Your URL (if you have an account with us) - The URL of the account you want to report - A brief explanation of how the account is impersonating you

If you are signed to a label or are using a distributor:

As part of the launch of SoundCloud Go, official representatives of artists (label, distributor or rightsholder) are able to create accounts on artists’ behalf. This means if the SoundCloud account has no image of you, contains the word “official” or “music” in the URL and has uploaded your content/ tracks please get in touch with your label, distributor or rightsholder directly for removal or management of the account.

Reporting tracks on the wrong profile

Sometimes tracks are uploaded to the wrong profile as part of our SoundCloud Go subscription service. This happens when labels and distributors send us content via the supply chain feed, but our system mistakenly attributes it to a profile, or is unable to find the correct profile to map the content to. #### How do I report tracks on my profile that belong to another artist? If you have found tracks on your profile that belong to another artist, please fill out this form . #### How do I report my tracks on the wrong profile? Please get in touch with your Rightsholder / Digital Distributor and request that the tracks be migrated or the profiles to be merged. SoundCloud requires written confirmation from the rightsholder for the content to be moved to another profile. If you’re unaware of your relationship to this rightsholder, then please contact your label who will be able to help. For more information, please refer to our article on Rightsholder content. If you’re looking to report copyright infringement or impersonation, please see: - Reporting infringing content on SoundCloud - Reporting impersonation

Legal, Safety & Reporting: Report Content Ownership & IP Issues

Reporting conflict of ownership

The only means we have of verifying the ownership of an account is the email address that was used to create the account. This means that the individual who controls the original email address used at sign-up is the owner of that account.

Our account ownership policy is designed to protect the security and privacy of our community, as well as satisfy our responsibilities as a service provider, in relation to applicable laws. #### How to proceed if you have a conflict of ownership  If there is a conflict regarding the ownership of an account that was once shared or set up on your behalf, we must follow our account ownership policy, which states that the owner of an account is the individual who controls the email address used at sign-up.    In such conflicts, the following options are available to you: 1. Gain access to the email address used to create the account; we can then restore this email to the account. 2. If this is not possible, you can report the account, or content hosted on the account, for violating our Terms of Use on the following grounds;

Impersonation and/or misrepresentation: If the account is misrepresenting its affiliation with you or is impersonating you, please let us know. If we find evidence of a Terms of Use violation, we will then be able to suspend the reported account. You can find out more about impersonation here. 3. Copyright Infringement: If the account is hosting content that you own the rights to, you can report this using our Copyright Infringement form. This will allow you to remove content that you own the rights to from SoundCloud. 4. Trademark Violation: If the account is infringing your trademark rights, you can let us know by emailing trademarks@soundcloud.com with proof of your registration. If we find evidence of trademark infringement, we can request that the account owner change their URL and/or Display Name.

A final option is to follow the due legal process to determine ownership of the account in question. If you can obtain a court order or settlement agreement in your favor (regarding the specific profile) we can pass access over to you. While we can appreciate that this process may seem complex, we hope that you can understand that our primary aim is to provide a service that respects both the privacy and security of our community members and their data. This means that we must follow our account ownership policy and related processes at all times.

Reporting trademark infringement

As a platform built with the needs of creators in mind, we take protecting trademark rights seriously. 

If you would like content to be removed from SoundCloud that infringes your trademark rights, please contact our Trust & Safety team using our chatbot feature and provide us with the following details: 1. The full URL where the allegedly infringing material is located 2. Your full name, address, email, and telephone number 3. Your trademark registration number, and the countries in which your trademark is registered 4. A brief explanation of how the reported content infringes your trademark 5. The statement: “I have a good faith belief that use of the trademarks described above on SoundCloud is not authorized by the trademark owner or its agent, nor is such use otherwise permissible under law.” 6. The statement: “I represent that the information in this notification is true and correct and that I am authorized to act on behalf of the trademark owner.” 7. Scanned copy of your physical signature

Please note: by submitting a takedown notification, you consent to having your information revealed to parties involved in the case.

Legal, Safety & Reporting: Report Fraud, Spam & Platform Manipulation

Reporting fake activity

At SoundCloud, we believe in building a strong community on the site, with deep connections to other users. To keep the community genuine, it is in breach of our Terms of Use to use any service or tool that promises to boost your account’s popularity (e.g., increasing your followers, likes, or plays). We work hard to fight against fake accounts and fake activity on our platform, regularly removing them when it is detected. #### Reporting fake activity on your account or tracks If you’ve noticed an unexpected, sudden increase in activity on your account, this can sometimes be explained by fake accounts on the platform. 

These accounts follow, play, like, and repost sounds across the community to appear human. Our Trust and Safety engineers work hard to detect fake accounts on the platform, but cannot always remove them before they have the chance to make actions on the site. 

Please let us know the following details through our chatbot feature: 1. Date you noticed this unusual increase in activity 2. An example of one of the accounts you suspect to be fake

We will use this information to review your account and, with the help of our Trust and Safety Team, remove any fake accounts that we find. Please bear in mind that this review may take some time to complete.

For now, we recommend that you Block and Report any account you suspect to be fake. You can do this using our block feature. Please note that you must be on a computer and using the latest version of SoundCloud to use this feature. #### Reporting fake activity on someone else’s account or tracks Please be assured that we share your concerns and frustrations with fake accounts and activity on SoundCloud. It could be that someone paid to boost the popularity of this account, or that it was mistakenly subject to fake activity intended for another account.

You can report any account you suspect to be fake to us by using the Block and Report function on-site (you must be using the latest version of SoundCloud to do this). We will then review all accounts reported to us and remove any accounts determined to be spam.

We work hard to combat fake activity on the platform. We hope these efforts reduce such occurrences where an account is trying to manipulate its own or another person’s popularity on the platform.

Reporting promotional services

SoundCloud aims to help creators to connect directly with their fans. We understand that promoting your work is important, and we encourage you to seek out fans and other like-minded individuals. In our experience, the most successful forms of promotion are built upon meaningful interactions between creators and their audience. That’s why the use of promotional services which sell social interactions is against the rules. #### Reporting charging for promotion Charging to promote the content of other accounts (e.g. charging others to upload and/or repost their content onto your account) is considered to be an unauthorized form of advertising, which is a violation of our Terms of Use and Community Guidelines. 

If you would like to report accounts charging for promotion, please provide us with the following details using our chatbot feature: - The URL of the account you want to report - A brief explanation of the services being offered - Any other information to support your case e.g. screenshots related to the service offerings

Reporting a sale of account

You can’t sell or offer to sell any SoundCloud account or URL. The sale of accounts or URLs is prohibited in our Terms, as outlined below:

“You must not sell or transfer, or offer to sell or transfer, any SoundCloud account to any third party without the prior written approval of SoundCloud.”

If you would like to report someone for attempting to sell an account, please provide us with the following details using our chatbot feature: - The URL of the account you want to report - A brief explanation of the situation - Any other information to support your case e.g. screenshots of messages or comments related to the attempted sale

Reporting scams

Protecting yourself online is important. While we do all we can to prevent unwanted attempts to access your personal information, there are some things to be aware of that can help you to protect yourself. Here are some tips to remember while using SoundCloud: 1. Don’t give in to phishing attempts; never reveal any confidential information about yourself or your account details to other community members (via messages, comments, or otherwise). 2. If you are being offered a deal that sounds too good to be true, it probably is. You can find some examples of common scams here. 3. Be wary of community members who ask for access to your content (e.g., unreleased demos, downloads of private tracks). You never know who is behind this request– it may not be who the profile claims to be.

Remember our key advice: always be extra cautious when interacting with individuals online. #### Reporting scams If you suspect that you have fallen victim to a scam, phishing attempt, or any other form of deception, please use our chatbot feature to make a report. We will do our best to help out if there is anything that we can do.

Reporting stream rippers

SoundCloud uses the most widely supported streaming protocol to ensure your sounds can be played everywhere, by everyone, across the web. When someone hits play on a track, the technology behind this streaming protocol is put into action to make sure your track can be played. By using a streaming technology that is widely supported, we can make sure that your content is playable on all devices and browsers.

Websites can exploit vulnerabilities that are inherent in this streaming technology, which allows them to rip the stream and provide it for download elsewhere. This means that they cannot download the original file you have uploaded with us, but instead the streamed audio (which is 128 kbps). This is the downside to using a system that allows you to be heard by everyone, everywhere. #### Reporting stream rippers If you believe a service is violating our Terms of Use** **by exploiting our streaming technology, you can contact us through our chatbot feature. We will do our best to help out if there is anything that we can do.

Legal, Safety & Reporting: Reporting Violations on SoundCloud

Reporting activity

We reserve the right to remove anything reported to us that is in breach of our Terms of Use or Community Guidelines (which all users agree to adhere to by signing up to use SoundCloud). #### What would you like to report?

Reporting an account

We support freedom of expression here at SoundCloud; even for individuals who might be expressing controversial opinions or beliefs. It’s important to remember that what is acceptable to one person, may be shocking to another. Just because you find something shocking or offensive does not mean that this content will be removed from SoundCloud.

For this reason, we advise if you do see or hear something that you don’t agree with, that you ignore it and if you can’t avoid the material because it is personal and directed towards you, or another specific individual, this might be considered as harassment. You can find out more about this here.

Use the Block feature in order to stop an account from following, or interacting with you. When blocking an account you will also be given the option to remove reposts and comments made by that person on your account. However, please keep in mind that all profiles are public and accounts you have blocked will still be able to view your profile and listen to your sounds. #### What would you like to report?

Reporting content

We support freedom of expression here at SoundCloud; even for individuals who might be expressing controversial opinions or beliefs. It’s important to remember that what is acceptable to one person, may be shocking to another. Just because you find something shocking or offensive does not mean that this content will be removed from SoundCloud.

For this reason, we advise if you do see or hear something that you don’t agree with, that you ignore it and if you can’t avoid the material because it is personal and directed towards you, or another specific individual, this might be considered as harassment. You can find out more about how to report harassment here. #### What would you like to report?

Reporting non consensual intimate imagery

Reporting Non-Consensual Intimate Imagery 

At SoundCloud, we are committed to providing a safe environment for creators and listeners. We strictly prohibit in our Community Guidelines the uploading, sharing, or distribution of non-consensual intimate imagery (NCII), including AI-generated explicit content (deepfakes). If you find content on SoundCloud that depicts you in a sexually explicit manner without your consent, you have the right to have it removed under our Community Guidelines. For our US users, there is a specific process in line with the US TAKE IT DOWN Act (TIDA). ##### How to Submit a TIDA Removal Request (US users) To submit an official TIDA removal request as a US user, please email SoundCloud at legal@soundcloud.com. Please copy and paste the template below into your email to legal@soundcloud.com. Please fill in the bracketed information. Subject: TIDA Removal Request - Non-Consensual Intimate Imagery I confirm that I am a US resident. 1. Location of the Content: > [Insert the exact SoundCloud URL(s) here] 2.
