Identification: I am the individual depicted in the content located at the URL(s) above. [Or: I am the authorized representative of the individual depicted in the content.] 3. Additional Context (Optional): [Provide any additional details that may help our Trust & Safety team locate or understand the context of the imagery, including how it is non-consensual] 4. Attestation: I attest that I have a good faith belief that the information and allegations contained in this report are accurate and complete, and that the distribution of the imagery identified in this report is non-consensual. 5. Electronic Signature: [Type Your Full Legal Name Here] SoundCloud requests that TIDA requests are sent as above. However from iOs or Android, SoundCloud will also honour TIDA requests from US users who report from the form as follows: 1. If an adult (under ‘it contains nudity or pornographic content’): 

“Non-consensual intimate image or recording of me” 2. “Non-consensual deepfake, AI image or recording of me”

If a minor (under ‘protection of minors’): 1. “Child sexual abuse material” 2. “AI, deepfake or non-photographic sexualised depiction of minors”

What Happens Next?

Once we receive a valid notice at legal@soundcloud.com, our Trust & Safety and Legal teams will acknowledge and prioritize your request. - Removal: Violating images will be removed from the platform within 48 hours of receiving a complete and valid notice. - Identical copies: Our Trust & Safety team will conduct searches for identical copies of the violating image and remove these. - Account Action: Users found to be uploading or distributing NCII or explicit deepfakes will be subject to platform enforcement in accordance with our Terms of Use.

Reporting on SoundCloud

We take our Terms of Use and Community Guidelines seriously, and expect everyone in the community to do the same. We hope that you will never need to report violations. But, in case you do come across something you think we need to take a look at, read on to find out more about reporting and our approach to moderation.  

We have a dedicated team of people who spend their time reviewing all reports objectively, using our Terms of Use, Community Guidelines, and internal policies when moderating reports. Remember that we can only make decisions based on the information we have available to us. This means that we cannot accept reports of activity that happens externally from SoundCloud. 

Please bear in mind that something that you find unacceptable may not be unacceptable to everyone. We try to maintain a fair and balanced approach and will remove any content that violates these rules or applicable law. Reporting content will not always result in that content being removed if it does not break the rules. Either way, we will always let you know the outcome of your report as soon as we can. #### What would you like to report?

Legal, Safety & Reporting: Sign In Security

How to Secure Your SoundCloud Account

Choose a strong, unique password

Never give out your password or account information

SoundCloud will NEVER:  - Ask you by email, messages, or comments to provide us with your password or sign-in credentials - Prompt you via email and email attachments, messages, or comments to log into a site outside of the SoundCloud.com domain, nor to download and install an application

Connect a secondary email to your account

In order to secure your account further, make sure to “Revoke All” in your settings “Connected applications” tab here to close all open sessions on logged in devices to enforce the new password. #### Enable 2FA for your SoundCloud account We offer 2FA for all SoundCloud users, more info in our help centre article here.

Sign In Notifications

Whenever someone signs in to SoundCloud from a device we haven’t seen before or an existing device we’ve not seen in awhile, the primary email address will receive a notification email to make you aware of this. The email will look like the one shown below: (image: Screenshot_2020-03-26_at_12.17.57.png) If you receive an email notification and can clearly identify the sign in as one that you have performed, you can ignore the notification email. Occasionally, it’s possible that the city associated with the IP address might be displayed in a slightly inaccurate manner. This is due to the way this data is fetched. In these cases, if the sign in is clearly shown to be from your IP address there would be no need for alarm and you can ignore the notification email. It’s also possible that the IP address or location might be missing from the notification too. Again, if you’re certain that the sign in is one that you have performed, you can ignore the notification email. However, If you receive a notification email where you have not performed a correlating sign in, this could indicate that someone else has gained access to your account. In this instance, you should follow the guidance given in this article  as soon as possible. As these notifications act as a security feature, we don’t currently have a way for you to disable these notifications.

Two Factor Authentication

Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) adds an extra layer of security to your SoundCloud account by requiring a code from an authenticator app when signing in. We recommend using Google Authenticator(on iOS or Android), LastPass, or Authy. #### Before you begin: 1. Make sure your email address is confirmed. This allows you to recover your account if needed. You can check this in your Settings on the website. 2. Download an authenticator app of your choice. 3. Add an email as a backup verification method (this option is not yet available to all users, it will be rolled out gradually).

Quick Navigation:

If you can’t access your 2FA codes If you lost your phone and backup codes If your 2FA code’s aren’t working #### To enable 2FA: 1. Go to SoundCloud on your browser and open your Settings. (2FA can only be managed on the website, but applies to both web and mobile.) 2. Open the Two-Factor Authentication tab. 3. Scan the QR code using your authenticator app, then enter the 6-digit code to confirm. 4. If you can’t scan the QR code, enter the setup key manually in your app and use the generated code. 5. Download and store your backup codes in a secure location. These can be used if you lose access to your device. 6. Once completed, 2FA will be active on your account.

Note: 2FA is not available via SMS. #### Adding an email as a backup verification method Please note: this option is not yet available to all users 1. During two-factor authentication setup, scan the QR code with your authenticator app. 2. After scanning, you’ll see the option “Add email as a backup verification method.” 3. Review the help text: “If you lose access to your app, we’ll send a code to your email.” 4. Turn on the toggle to enable email as a backup method. 5. Complete setup: both your authenticator app and email OTP will now be active.

What are email OTPs? - They are 6-digit codes that we send to your email - They can be used only once - Each code is valid for 5 minutes only - If you request a new code, all previous codes are automatically invalid

Please make sure that: - You always use the latest code (don’t try to use an old one) - Your code is not older than 5 minutes - if you have multiple accounts (or multiple emails) make sure you’re checking to correct email inbox - You check your spam folder if you’re sure your email is correct and you still haven’t received any code

If you can’t access your 2FA codes

1. Use a backup code

A backup code for an authenticator is a one-time use code you can use to log into your account if you can’t access your authenticator app (like when you lose your phone). When you set up 2FA, you receive backup codes that can be used instead of your authenticator app. We strongly suggest copying your 2FA backup codes when you set up 2FA. To use one: 1. Enter your username and password when logging in. 2. When prompted for a code, choose the option to use a backup code. 3. Enter one of your saved backup codes.

Please note: each backup code can only be used once. ##### Where can I find my backup codes? Backup codes can only be downloaded once during setup, so make sure they are stored securely. When you set up two-factor authentication (2FA), you were given a set of backup (recovery) codes. These are usually saved as a text (.txt) file on your device. To find them, look for a file you downloaded or saved during setup with this name: soundcloud-backup-codes.txt ##### Tips to help you find your file - Check the Downloads folder on your computer or your mobile device for soundcloud-backup-codes.txt - Think about which device you used to set up 2FA (phone, laptop, or desktop) and check there

2. Sign in using email OTP as a backup 

Please note: this option is not yet available to all users, it will be rolled out gradually 1. Enter your username and password on the sign-in page. 2. On the authenticator (TOTP) screen, select “Try another method.” 3. Choose Email OTP as your verification method. 4. Check your email for the one-time code. 5. Enter the code to complete sign-in and access your account.

3. Check Apple Keychain (iPhone)

If you’re using an iPhone, your 2FA code may be saved in your device: 1. Open Settings → Passwords 2. Search for “soundcloud.com” 3. Use the verification code if one appears

4. Restore from your authenticator app

Many authenticator apps support backups. If enabled, you can restore your codes on a new device. The steps vary depending on the app, so refer to your app’s documentation for instructions. Note: TOTP backup setup varies by app. Refer to the documentation for popular TOTP apps for guidance. - Google Authenticator - LastPass - Authy - Duo

5. Use your old phone

If you still have access to your old device: 1. Open your authenticator app 2. Find your SoundCloud code and use it to log in 3. You can then set up your new device using your app’s backup or transfer feature

Note: The Process to transfer codes from the old phone is different for different apps: - Google Authenticator - LastPass - Authy - Duo

If you lost your phone and backup codes

If you no longer have access to your authenticator app, backup codes, or old device: 1. Reinstall your authenticator app and attempt to restore from a backup. 2. If that doesn’t work, contact SoundCloud Support through the support bot. 3. You’ll need to verify your identity before access can be restored. Make sure you contact support using the email address linked to your account.

If your 2FA codes aren’t working

2FA codes are time-based and require your device’s clock to be accurate. If your codes aren’t working: 1. Check that your phone’s time is set to automatic. 2. If it’s already automatic, turn it off and back on to resync.

Incorrect time settings or time zone changes are the most common cause of invalid codes.

Legal, Safety & Reporting: Technical, Legal & Policy-Based Reports

Reporting a Security Vulnerability

Our Responsible Disclosure program is hosted on Bugcrowd. Please read our program brief carefully and sign up on Bugcrowd to report any security vulnerabilities you have found. #### Hall of Fame On behalf of our millions of users, we would like to give a shout-out to all security researchers who have helped us keep SoundCloud safe by reporting a security vulnerability to us responsibly - we really appreciate it! The current Hall of Fame can be seen on Bugcrowd: https://bugcrowd.com/engagements/soundcloud/hall_of_fames.

Reporting API Violations

If you find an application that you believe violates our API Terms of Use, please contact us through our AI agent, who will escalate your case to a support specialist. We will investigate any reports and take the necessary action.

Reporting Under The Network Enforcement Act/ Netzwerkdurchsetzungsgesetz (NetzDG)

The Network Enforcement Act** **is a German law that requires social networks to remove illegal content reported to them. To report content you believe should be restricted under the Network Enforcement Act, please file a ticket with our AI agent. They will escalate you to a support specialist who can assist you further.

My Account: Comments

Comments

SoundCloud is built on connection. Comments allow fans to give immediate feedback and creators to engage directly with their audience at specific moments in a track. #### How to leave a comment - Web: Click any free space in the area below the waveform to leave a comment at that exact timestamp. Type your message in the text box and press Enter. - Mentions: Tag another user by typing @** followed by their Profile URL (e.g., @artistname). They will receive a notification that you’ve mentioned them. - Replies:** Click the user’s avatar on the waveform or hit Reply next to their comment on the track page.

Managing your own comments

You can view every comment you’ve ever made by going to your profile and clicking “View all” in the comments section (or adding /comments to the end of your Profile URL). - To Delete: Click the trash can icon next to your comment. - Important: Deleted comments are removed permanently and cannot be restored.

Looking for more? See how to manage comments on Mobileor check our guide for managing comments as a creator on SoundCloud.

Comments on Mobile (iOS & Android)

The SoundCloud app lets you connect with the community anywhere. While the core features are the same as Web, the mobile experience is optimized for smaller screens. #### Leaving a comment 1. Open the full-screen player by tapping the mini-player at the bottom. 2. Tap the comment icon at the exact second you want to leave your feedback. 3. Type your message and tap the orange arrow to send.

Note: Unlike Web, mobile comments are not visible directly on the waveform; they are listed chronologically in the comment section. #### Reply to a comment 1. Open the full-screen player by tapping the mini-player at the bottom. 2. Tap “Reply” below the comment you’d like to respond to. 3. Type your message and tap the orange arrow to send.

Moderation & Reporting

If you encounter spam or need to remove a comment while on the go: - Report Spam: Long-press the comment and select “Report comment.” Once reported, our Trust & Safety team reviews and takes action against comments that violate our community guidelines. - Delete: Long-press the comment and select “Delete comment.” This removes it from all platforms immediately.

Link Restrictions

For security reasons, links within comments are not “clickable” on mobile devices. To follow a link in a comment, please access the track via a Web browser.

Manage Comments as a Creator

On SoundCloud, comments aren’t just feedback—they are real-time touchpoints with your community. Managing these interactions effectively helps you build a dedicated fanbase while keeping your profile a safe and professional space for your music. #### Engaging with Fans Responding to fans is the fastest way to turn a listener into a supporter. You can manage and reply to comments in two ways: - The Main Stream: Reply directly on your track’s waveform or on your track page. - Artist Studio (Artist Pro** Exclusive):** For those managing a busy catalog, the Artist Studio organizes all your track comments chronologically. This dedicated view allows you to track and respond to feedback across your entire discography from one central hub.

Moderation and Quiet Mode

As an artist, you have full control over the conversation on your tracks. If you want to limit distractions or maintain a specific aesthetic, you can use Quiet Mode (available withArtist Pro). Quiet Mode allows you to: - Choose if fans are allowed to comment on your tracks. - Toggle whether existing comments are visible to the public. - Choose if you’d like to keep your track stats (like play counts) private.

To enable this, head to your track’s Edit page and navigate to the Permissions tab. #### Deleting and Reporting Comments If a comment is off-brand, offensive, or spam, you can remove it permanently: 1. Go to the track page on the web. 2. Locate the comment below the waveform. 3. Hover over the comment and click the trash can icon. 4. Reporting: When deleting, you will also have the option to report the comment as spam. This helps our Trust & Safety team keep SoundCloud clean for everyone.

Note: Deleted comments are permanently removed and cannot be restored. #### Troubleshooting: Why are comments missing? If you can’t see comments you expect to find, check the following: - Quiet Mode: Double-check your Permissions tab to ensure Quiet Mode hasn’t hidden the comments from the waveform. - Replaced Audio: If you used the Replace Filefeature with a shorter version of your song, comments from the “original” longer ending will still exist in the comment list but will no longer appear as avatars on the waveform. - Fan Deletion: If you received a notification but the comment is gone, the listener likely deleted their comment before you could view it.

Looking for more social tips? Check out Commenting Basics or learn how to** **manage comments on mobile.

Troubleshoot: Can’t Comment or Reply

Why can’t I make or reply to a comment?

If you’re having trouble engaging with a track, it usually comes down to one of two things: Account Verification or Spam Limits. ##### 1. Confirm your Email You cannot comment until your email address is verified. - How to check: Go to your Account Settings. If you see “(Not confirmed)” next to your email, click Resend confirmation email and follow the link in your inbox.

2. Temporary Activity Blocks

Our spam detection may temporarily restrict your ability to comment if you post many similar messages quickly, as this violates our Community Guidelines. - The Rule: Avoid “copy-pasting” the same comment to multiple artists. Make your feedback unique to the track you’re listening to. - The Limit: We cannot manually lift these blocks—they are set to expire automatically. We recommend waiting 24 hours before trying again.

3. Quiet Mode

If you are trying to comment on an artist’s track and the text box is missing, the creator may have enabled Quiet Mode. This is an Artist Pro feature that allows creators to turn off commenting or hide existing comments to maintain a specific profile aesthetic. Still stuck? Check the SoundCloud Status Page to see if there is a site-wide issue affecting social features.

My Account: Direct Messages

Can’t send or reply to a message

There are a few reasons why you may not be able to make, or reply to a message. #### Email needs to be confirmed In order to send messages, your email must be confirmed to your account. Please check your Account Settings page to make sure your email is confirmed. If you need to send another confirmation email, you can do so from there. #### Recipient has chosen not to receive messages  If you can’t send or reply to a message and receive an error, it means that the user is either not accepting messages from people that they do not follow on SoundCloud. #### Recipient has blocked you  If you receive an error message, it may be because the user has blocked you from contacting them on SoundCloud. #### Your message is too long Please keep in mind that messages are limited to 1000 characters. #### You have been temporarily blocked from more actions Whenever a user sends a series of identical (or nearly identical) messages in a short period of time, this activity triggers our spam detection systems, at which point a user will receive a temporary block on using the messaging feature. These spam detection systems are completely automated, so we can’t control who receives a block and we can’t prevent it from happening to you. 

We block users from sending lots of identical messages in a row because this sort of behavior directly violates our Community Guidelines. 

We want to keep our messaging practices fair, genuine, and free of spam. In fact, we’re so serious about keeping your messaging inbox clear of spammy clutter, that the more a user is warned about shady messaging behavior, the longer their resulting blocks will be. 

We can’t remove these blocks sooner than they are set to expire and users with Artist Pro accounts don’t receive preferential treatment. 

The best way to avoid receiving this kind of block is to limit the amount of messages you send in a row and to keep each message as unique as possible.

Controlling who messages you

You can control who can message you in your Privacy Settings page. You can choose to either accept messages from anyone on SoundCloud, or only those who you follow. #### What are the consequences of limiting who can message you on SoundCloud? Limiting messages can have both positive and negative impacts: 1. Impact on Communication: What happens if you restrict messages to only the people you follow? When you limit messages to just the users you follow, you reduce the likelihood of receiving unwanted or spam messages. However, this also means you might miss out on opportunities to connect with new listeners, potential collaborators, or others who are interested in reaching out to you but whom you don’t follow. 2. Privacy Benefits: How does limiting messages enhance your privacy on SoundCloud? By restricting messages to followers only, you increase your privacy and control over interactions on SoundCloud. This setting can help protect you from unsolicited messages and ensure that only trusted users can contact you. 3. Ease of Management: How does managing message settings affect your experience? Adjusting your message settings allows you to tailor your communication experience on SoundCloud to your needs. Whether you want to be open to everyone or just maintain contact with a select group, this feature gives you the flexibility to decide who can reach out to you.

Direct Messages

Direct messaging on SoundCloud is where the community happens. Use DMs to collaborate with other artists, share your latest WIPs, or connect directly with your fans. #### How to Send or Reply to a Message - On Web: Click the envelope icon in the top-right navigation bar. Select a conversation to expand it. To start fresh, click “Write new” or visit an artist’s profile and click the envelope icon. - On Mobile (iOS & Android): Tap the envelope icon at the top right of your Home screen.

Pro-Tip: You can tag other creators in a message by typing @** followed by their Profile URL. #### Sharing Tracks and Playlists Sharing music via DM is the best way to get feedback or pitch a demo. - From the Waveform:** Click the Share button below any track or playlist and select the Message tab. Type in the recipient’s name or Profile URL. - Within a Chat: * Web: Click “Add track” to choose from your own uploads, or simply paste a SoundCloud URL to embed the waveform. Mobile: Tap the waveform icon next to the text box to select a track.

Mass Messaging and Spam

Can I message all my followers at once? We do not offer a mass-messaging tool. At SoundCloud, we value authentic 1:1 connections over broadcasts. No one likes a crowded inbox full of generic links. - The Alternative: If you want to reach everyone at once, share your track publicly. This ensures it lands in all of your followers’ Feeds where they can listen, repost, and share it with their own networks.

Managing Your Inbox

  • Deleting a Conversation: Click the trash can icon at the top of a chat to archive it. Note: Deleting a thread only removes it from your view; it will still be visible to the recipient. If either of you sends a new message, the full history will reappear.

Reporting Spam: When you delete a conversation, you’ll have the option to report it. Please do this for any unsolicited ads or bot activity—it helps our Trust & Safety team keep the community clean. Individual Messages: You cannot delete a single message within a thread once it’s been sent. Double-check your links and typos before hitting send! Need more control? Learn how to control who can message you, or use the Fans Tool to prioritize your most engaged listeners.

My Account: Email, Notifications & Communications

Manage Advertising Settings

To manage your advertising preferences, navigate to your Advertising Settings. On this page, you will have the ability to review and adjust your advertising settings according to your preferences. It is important to note that while you can control the types of ads you see, you will still be shown the same number of advertisements overall. However, if you choose to limit or adjust your preferences, the ads you receive may be less relevant to your interests. #### Web version If you are using the web version, you can click on the “Partners List” option. This section allows you to view your current advertising preferences in detail. From here, you have the option to allow or disable consent for all advertising partners, giving you greater control over how your data is used for advertising purposes. #### Mobile version If you are accessing your account through the mobile version, start by opening the Settings menu. Next, navigate to the Privacy section, where you can set and manage your advertising preferences. This process allows you to customize your experience and control how your information is used for targeted advertising while using the mobile app. #### What do users need to understand about GDPR compliance on SoundCloud? If you would like to learn more about the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and how it may affect your data and privacy rights, you can find additional information here. For comprehensive guidance on managing your SoundCloud account, including settings and privacy options, please visit this page here.

Manage Analytics Settings

How can users manage their analytics preferences on SoundCloud?

To manage your analytics preferences on SoundCloud, follow these steps: - Access the Analytics Settings Page: Go to your Analytics Settings on the SoundCloud website or mobile app. Here, you can adjust your preferences to help improve your experience on the platform. - Web and Mobile Versions: The settings can be accessed on both the web and mobile versions.

What do users need to understand about GDPR compliance on SoundCloud?

If you would like to learn more about the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and how it may affect your data and privacy rights, you can find additional information here. For comprehensive guidance on managing your SoundCloud account, including settings and privacy options, please visit this page here.

Manage Communications Settings

How can users manage their communication preferences on SoundCloud?

To manage your communication preferences on SoundCloud: - Access the “Communications” tab in your profile settings: Visit your Communications Settings on the SoundCloud website or mobile app. Here, you can select your preferences for receiving personalized news, tips, and offers from SoundCloud. - Web and Mobile Versions: You can update these settings on both the web and mobile versions of SoundCloud.

What should users understand about GDPR compliance on SoundCloud?

SoundCloud complies with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) to protect user data. For more detailed information about GDPR and how your data is managed, follow this link. For further information about how to manage your SoundCloud account, go here.

Manage Email & Push Notifications

Use your Notifications Settings page on SoundCloud to choose which updates you receive — including email notifications and push notifications on Android or iOS. Customize your preferences to stay informed about the activity that matters most to you. #### Notification Types: Activity Notifications: Artists may want to prioritize notifications that keep them informed about interactions with their content, such as: - New Follower: Receive updates when someone follows you. - Reposts: Get notified when someone reposts your track or playlist. - Likes and Comments: Stay updated when someone likes or comments on your tracks or playlists. - Messages: Be alerted when you receive a new message from fans or collaborators.

SoundCloud Updates: Both artists and fans can benefit from staying informed about platform updates, but artists might focus more on: - New SoundCloud Features: Keep up with the latest product releases and features. - Surveys and Feedback: Participate in feedback opportunities to shape future features. - Tips and Offers: Learn about new ways to discover artists or improve your SoundCloud experience. - SoundCloud Newsletter: Receive news and special offers from SoundCloud and its partners.

What additional tips can help users manage mobile push notifications and ensure they receive important updates?

To manage your mobile push notifications: Limit Notifications for Better Focus: SoundCloud limits activity notifications to one every 24 hours. This helps prevent notification overload, especially for active artists. Enable Push Notifications: If you’ve turned off push notifications in your mobile device’s settings, you’ll need to re-enable them to start receiving updates. Once enabled, return to your Notifications Settings to select which specific notifications you want on your mobile device. #### Not receiving email notifications?  If you’re not receiving notifications from us, first check your notifications settings here: https://soundcloud.com/settings/notifications. If you are still having trouble receiving email notifications, please check your spam folder. Adding “notifications@soundcloudmail.com” to your address book in your email settings will also help ensure our mail isn’t identified as spam. Please note it still may take a while for you to receive all mail consistently, as providers tend to leave notifications in blocking holds (often between one and six hours).”

My Account: Follower Basics

Follower basics

Following other people on SoundCloud

You can follow anyone on SoundCloud by clicking the ‘Follow’ button on the right hand side underneath their Profile Header image. By following another user, you will get their latest uploads in your Feed, so you can listen to the newest music or audio as it is released. Artists can share their music exclusively with their followers on SoundCloud, giving them early access to upcoming tracks, work-in-progress demos, or releases before anyone else. Non-followers can see that the track exists, but they will be prompted to follow the artist to unlock it. You can learn more about ‘Follower Exclusive’ over here.

You can review who you are following at anytime by going to Following in your Library page. #### Suggested Follows  SoundCloud App users on iOS and Android can find recommended people in their network to follow on the homepage. #### Your Followers Anytime you get a new follower on SoundCloud, you will be notified in your Notifications tab on web or on the SoundCloud app.  You can see everyone that follows you on your profile page under ‘Followers’ and if you have over 1,000 followers we will round the number. However, you can scroll over the rounded figure at any time to view the exact number of followers. #### Rounded follower count If you have over 1,000 followers we will round the number. However, you can scroll over the rounded figure at any time to view the exact number of followers. (image: Image_2015-11-02_at_11.31.51_AM.png)

How to Block and Unblock Users on SoundCloud

How can I block someone on SoundCloud?

  1. Visit the profile of the user you wish to block
  2. Click the three dots (…) in the top right corner
  3. Select the ‘Block’ option from the menu.

Manage Interactions: When you block a user, you will have the option to remove any reposts, likes, and comments they have made on your account. This ensures that their past interactions with your content are also removed. #### What are the consequences of blocking and unblocking users on SoundCloud? Blocking a user has several consequences: Will the blocked user know they’ve been blocked? The user does not receive a notification when they are blocked. Instead, they encounter an error message on the screen that reads, “Something went wrong when trying to perform this action.” What happens to the blocked user’s interactions with my account? You can choose to remove all their reposts, likes, and comments from your account when you block them. This cleans up any previous interactions they had with your content. How can I manage my list of blocked users? You can view and manage the users you have blocked by going to your Privacy Settings page. From here, you can unblock users if you choose. #### How can I unblock someone on SoundCloud? Unblock from Privacy Settings: You can view and manage the users you have blocked by going to your Privacy Settings page. From here, you can unblock users if you choose.Go to your Privacy Settings page, where you can see a list of all users you have blocked. You can unblock any user from this list. Unblock from the User’s Profile: Alternatively, you can visit the profile of the blocked user and select the option to unblock them directly from their profile page. #### What should I consider before unblocking someone? Re-Evaluate the Situation: Consider whether unblocking the user might lead to unwanted interactions or if the initial reason for blocking them is still relevant. Restoration of Interactions: Keep in mind that unblocking a user does not automatically restore their previous interactions (likes, comments, reposts) on your account.

My Account: Follower Issues

Can’t follow other users

If you are having problems following other users on SoundCloud, it may be for a few different reasons: #### You’ve hit the 2000 following limit The overall limit is 2000 and applies to all subscriptions. This is a measure designed to reduce stability issues related to following a large number of accounts (e.g., problems loading your Stream, following page, etc.). #### You’ve been put in a temporary block  There are currently limits on the number of follow actions you can make within 24 hours and on re-following the same accounts within a short period.

If you are repeatedly flagged for these kinds of activities it’s possible that your account will be temporarily blocked from following or unfollowing any more accounts. The duration of these blocks will increase in length each subsequent time you hit these limits.

Please understand that these limits are in place to address community complaints about accounts overusing features or using them in ways other than intended. #### 422 - Unprocessable entity error  If you’re having issues following or unfollowing users and you haven’t hit any of these limits, it’s possible you might be experiencing a known caching issue on the platform. Usually, if this is the case, you will see a message reading “422 - unprocessable entity” when attempting a follow-up action. ##### Here is how you can work around this until this is fixed: - Choose any other user profile and start following the user. - Briefly afterward, unfollow that user again to trigger the cache to be reset. - Now go back to the user profile that was giving you the error message. From there, you should be able to follow or unfollow as usual.

Follower count is stuck, and won’t increase

You receive notifications when people follow you, but not when users ‘unfollow’ you. This means in the same time that people follow you (which you’re notified for), other followers may have unfollowed you, which would lead your follower count not to increase by the amount that you were notified for. 

People can unfollow for a few reasons: - People choose to unfollow you. - People remove their accounts. - Batches of spam accounts that are in your followers have been removed from the platform.

Please note: Due to caching, the actual numbers displayed on follows won’t re-adjust until an action is made on your account. An action could be uploading a track, following someone new, or making any edits to your profile.

Follower count suddenly dropping

Every time you take an action on your SoundCloud account (such as signing in, uploading a track, or following an account), your cache is reset. This means that you may experience jumps in your follower counts when you do any of the above and your cache refreshes and recognizes new information.

Your follower count can drop for two reasons: - People are unfollowing you - Batches of spam accounts that are in your followers have been removed from the platform. In cases where you see a sudden drop, the latter is most likely to be the case.

Regularly, our Trust & Safety Team works to detect and remove spam accounts from the platform. On removing these accounts, any likes, reposts, or comments they’ve previously made will also be removed. This is why you may notice sudden drops in these activities from your account from time to time as well. 

The reason why spam accounts may interact with you is so that they can appear more human. These accounts will follow, like, repost, or comment on a wide variety of accounts in the community to appear more ‘real’.

Not receiving email notifications about new followers

We no longer send new follower email notifications. The reason we are doing this is to make sure that all emails are successfully delivered from SoundCloud’s email services. As many of these emails are not being opened when received or are being reported as spam, we risk our reputation as email providers being damaged. 

In the meantime, you will still be notified about new followers via push notifications via the SoundCloud Android app, as well as our on-site** **notifications on your SoundCloud profile. 

Please note: We do not currently offer push notifications on the iPhone or iPad apps.

My Account: Getting Started on SoundCloud

Anatomy of SoundCloud

Your** Feed keeps you up to date with the people you follow: their new tracks, playlists, and reposts appear here. Your own posts also show on your Feed and profile. Your ****Profile**** is your public page (soundcloud.com/[your URL]). This serves as a personal hub where all the tracks you upload and repost are displayed for others to discover and listen to. Home is your personalized hub featuring curated playlists like Weekly Wave, with new songs each week, and Daily Drops, offering daily updates. Discover trending hits and stay updated with the latest music. Your Library shows your Likes, Playlists, and the Tracks and Playlists of the people you follow. A Repost is a quick way to share your favorite tracks or playlists with friends and followers. Click the repost button below a track or playlist to add it to your profile and share it to your followers’ Feeds. Spotlight is an Artist and Artist Pro premium feature that lets you pin up to five tracks or playlists at the top of your profile. These appear under the “All” tab, making it easier for visitors to find and engage with your highlighted music. It helps artists showcase their style or recent projects more effectively. Embedded player lets you easily share tracks, playlists, or your full profile on your website or blog. It allows visitors to listen to your music without leaving your site. Your **Follower/Followinghelps you fill your Feed with audio you love by connecting with profiles you’re interested in. Your uploads and reposts will appear on the Feeds of your Followers. Likes let you save and quickly access your favorite tracks. Click the heart icon below a track’s waveform to save it. The heart turns orange, showing the track is added to your collection. This helps you build a personalized music library for easy listening anytime. Playlists are curated collections of music tracks, including your uploads or others’ songs. Like albums on Playlists let you organize music for workouts, relaxation, or sharing favorites, offering a seamless way to showcase your music.

Common Errors During Sign Up

What error message are you seeing? 

We couldn’t sign you up
Our robots think this signup/sign-in looks too much like spam

How do the anti-spam systems work, and what might trigger these flags? - Platforms like SoundCloud use anti-spam systems to detect and block suspicious activities. - They monitor IP addresses, flagging multiple account creations from the same IP. - Unusual browser behavior, such as rapid clicks or signups, may be flagged as automated. - Signups from regions with high spam rates can also be marked as suspicious. - While these systems help prevent abuse, legitimate users may get blocked. Switching networks, devices, or email addresses can sometimes help bypass these filters.

What can I do to resolve this issue? - Switch to another browser or use a different device. - Try signing up from a different network (e.g., a different Wi-Fi connection). - Use a different email address to create the account. - Disable VPN if using one.

When signing up, it says my email is already in use

Still need help? Reach out to us via our AI agent. They can create a ticket for you.

Creating an account on SoundCloud

Setting up an account is the first step to finding your sound and your scene. Whether you’re here to listen or ready to upload, getting started is simple. #### Sign up for free You can create an account using your email address, or connect via Google, Facebook, or Apple. A free account gives you unlimited listening and allows you to upload up to 120 minutes of your own audio. #### The basics When you create an account, you agree to our Community Guidelines and Terms of Use. These are the ground rules that keep SoundCloud a safe and creative space for everyone. #### Setting up your profile ##### Your profile is where your scene lives. To make it yours: - Choose a display name and profile URL: Make it easy for fans and collaborators to find you. - Add a profile picture and bio: Tell the community who you are and what you’re about.

If you’re an artist, you can take your profile further:
  • Spotlight your tracks: Pin your best work or latest releases to the top of your profile.
  • Add social links: Connect your fans to your merch, tour dates, and other socials.
  • Enable Fan Support: Give your audience a direct way to support your craft.

Building your community

SoundCloud is built on connection. Once you’re in, you can: - Engage: Like, repost, and comment on the tracks that move you. - Curate: Create playlists to organize your favorite finds or share new trends. - Connect: Use direct messages to talk shop with collaborators or reach out to other artists.

Ready to upload?

If you’re a creator, you can upload your first track as soon as your account is live. From there, you can explore SoundCloud for Artists to monetize your music, get advanced insights, and distribute your tracks to over 60 platforms. #### Level up Looking for more? Check out our subscriptions to find the right fit for your goals: - Artist Pro: Unlimited uploads, advanced discovery, and professional tools. - SoundCloud Go+: Ad-free listening and full access to our entire catalog.

Email requirements

It’s important to understand that the email address used to originally create a SoundCloud account will be used to indicate ownership of the account for the duration of it’s existence. Therefore it’s advisable to take extra care when selecting the email address you’re going to use when creating an account. #### If you’re signing up to SoundCloud with an email address, please note the following: - An email address can only be associated with one SoundCloud account at a time. It is not possible to manage multiple accounts from one email address. - The email address you use on your SoundCloud account is not made publicly visible to others on SoundCloud. - We use the email you enter to confirm your new SoundCloud account, we’ll send a confirmation email to do this. For this reason it’s important that you use an active email address that you have access to. - Please note that until the email address has been confirmed you will not be able to upload any content or images to the account.

Introduction to SoundCloud

Founded in 2007, SoundCloud is an artist-first platform powered by a global community of artists and listeners on the pulse of what’s new, now, and next in music culture. We empower independent artists with the tools, services, and resources they need to help them build and grow their careers. With 4x the catalog of every major streaming platform on SoundCloud, we are the largest audio discovery platform in the world. #### Who is SoundCloud for? ##### For Artists: Build Your Career on Your Terms Whether you’re just starting out or already growing your audience, SoundCloud gives you the tools to own your journey. Upload and share your tracks instantly. Promote your releases and connect directly with your fans. Earn money when you’re ready to monetize your music. Start for free, or upgrade to Artist Pro to unlock advanced insights, promotional tools, and exclusive features designed to help you level up. Explore our Artist Resource Center for tips, tools, and inspiration to keep your career moving forward. ##### For Listeners: Discover What’s Next SoundCloud isn’t just for streaming — it’s for exploring. Dive into a world of new sounds before they hit the mainstream. Discover fresh music and rising artists. Support creators you love with likes, comments, and reposts. Go+ subscribers can save unlimited tracks and playlists for ad-free, offline listening — so the music never stops. Learn how to optimize your listening experience and make SoundCloud your personal soundtrack to discovery.

Nina Protocol FAQs

We’re excited to welcome the Nina Protocol community into SoundCloud, so we can continue helping artists and fans connect and support each other. To see more details on how Nina Protocol users can start using SoundCloud, click here. #### Will Nina Protocol stay open? Sadly, no. We are huge admirers of Nina Protocol and the community that was built there. The Nina Protocol website will be closing as planned. However, we working together so that artists and users of Nina Protocol can migrate their content and networks to SoundCloud. We hope to continue building on our shared vision of a connected music network on SoundCloud. #### Who is eligible for the Artist Pro offer? The offer is available to Nina Protocol users who were active before the wind-down. The offer entitles you to SoundCloud Artist Pro through the end of the year. #### Where do I find my Artist Pro promo code? If you were an active Nina Protocol user before the wind-down, you should have received an email from Nina containing a unique Artist Pro promo code. Additionally, if you click on any of the ‘Claim Artist Pro’ links on the Nina website while logged in, you should get redirected to Artist Pro check-out with the code already applied. You will need to enter your payment details to claim your free months. You will not be charged at this time and are able to cancel before the end of your trial offer period. #### How do I redeem my Artist Pro offer? Your promo code can be redeemed for an Artist Pro plan via the SoundCloud checkout. You can also access this page via the link in your email from Nina Protocol, or via the link in the migration tool on ninaprotocol.com. #### Do I need an existing SoundCloud account? No. You can log into an existing account or create one during the SoundCloud migration process, or in the checkout flow. We recommend that you create, or sign in, to your SoundCloud account before using the migration tool or starting the checkout process. #### Does the offer apply to existing subscribers? The offer is valid for any user who does not have a current subscription. If you are already a SoundCloud Subscriber, and have an offer code, please reach out to our support team so we can look into this for you. #### What happens if an upload fails? The migration status identifies failed items. You can retry the migration for those releases or contact support if the problem persists. #### Why don’t I see all of my Nina Protocol releases? Only published releases associated with the logged-in Nina profile are shown. Refresh the page after logging in, or reach out to our support team if your catalog is incomplete. Please make sure you share your Nina Protocol account details so we can take a look. #### I made a mistake during the release migration process. How can I remedy it? As the migration progresses, releases become available on your SoundCloud profile. Select a specific track or playlist, and modify it directly by clicking on ‘Edit’. #### Will all of my content be automatically transferred to SoundCloud? No, your content will only be migrated over to SoundCloud with your consent. You can opt-in and seamlessly transfer your content over to SoundCloud on this page. #### What happens to the editorial content from Nina Protocol? We are actively exploring how we can preserve the rich editorial content from Nina Protocol and its community. More to come soon. #### Is SoundCloud still training AI on user content? Will songs uploaded to Nina now be subject to SoundCloud ToS? SoundCloud has never used artist content to train AI models, nor do we develop generative AI models or allow third parties to scrape or use SoundCloud content for AI training. As Nina joins SoundCloud, artists can choose to migrate their accounts to SoundCloud. If they do, their accounts will be subject to SoundCloud’s Terms of Service. Our approach to AI remains the same: we use AI to improve experiences like recommendations, search, content organization, and fraud detection not to train generative AI on artists’ music.

Verify your email

When you verify your email address, you help to significantly decrease the chances of unauthorized individuals gaining access to your account. This process acts as an additional layer of protection, ensuring that only you can manage and control your account settings and sensitive information. #### Confirmation emails are generally sent out instantly when you sign up. If you haven’t received one yet, please try the following: - Check your spam folder to make sure it didn’t end up there by accident - Add hello@soundcloud.com to your address book in your email settings. It may be that your email provider has bounced our email confirmation - Try to sign in and if prompted, click ‘resend email’. You may need to go to the Email Settings to resend the email - Try signing up with another method like Apple/Google

The magic link in the email does not work.

The link may have timed out. Sign in and click ‘resend email’. Go to the Email Settings to resend the email. #### I confirmed my email, but I still can’t use SoundCloud properly. If you confirmed your email, but are still being notified on-site that this action hasn’t been made, don’t worry. This is due to caching, and your profile not recognizing the new information. Please sign out and back into your account to refresh your profile.

My Account: Login Issues

Backup Login with One-Time Password (OTP)

If you got an email about this new feature but don’t see it when logging in, don’t worry! It’s not available to all users yet but will be soon. A One-Time Password (OTP) is a temporary code we send to your email to help verify it’s really you when logging in. If you currently have Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) enabled, you may now be able to use a code sent to your email as a backup way to sign in instead of your authenticator app. This helps you get back into your account faster if you lose access to your authenticator app. Availability depends on your account and regional availability. #### Important Things to Know Some accounts now have email OTP enabled as a backup verification method to 2FA. If you are not automatically opted-in you can enable it in your Account Settings. Email OTP is helpful if: - You got a new phone and lost access to your authenticator app - Your authenticator app was deleted or reset - You can’t generate a verification code

Using OTP as a backup makes signing in more flexible, but it’s important to enable additional security measures where possible. Use a strong password and keep your email account secure. #### How to log in using an OTP If you can’t access your authenticator app, you can try logging in with an email code: 1. Go to the SoundCloud login page 2. Enter your username/email and password 3. On the verification screen, click “Try another method” 4. Select “Send code to email” 5. Check your email inbox for the one-time passcode 6. Enter the code on the login screen 7. You’ll be logged in to your account

If you don’t have access to your authenticator app and email OTP isn’t enabled on your account, you’ll need to contact support via our AI Agent for help recovering access.

Blocked from Signing In or Signing Up

Sometimes you may see a “Our robots think you’re spam” or “Our robots think you’re a robot” error message when trying to log in or sign up. 

We have a number of systems in place to stop spammers from signing up or logging in. It looks like there was something about your sign up or login attempt which triggered these systems and prevented you from accessing SoundCloud. 

To regain access to your account or to create an account, try these troubleshooting tips: - Reload/refresh the page - Use a different browser - Access through a different computer or device - Reset your router - Use a different internet connection - Make sure your OS and SSL certificates are up to date - Disable temporarily your VPN, ad-blocker or privacy extension

If you’re still trying to create an account, we’d recommend you try using a different email address, as it’s possible there’s an issue with your email address or domain.

Still need help? Contact us via our AI agent. They will connect you to a support specialist for further assistance. 

My Account Is Frozen and I Can’t Sign In

Accounts may be frozen for various reasons, such as policy violations, fraud or security concerns requiring resolution. Before contacting support, users should check their emails and SoundCloud messages folder for any notifications related to the issue or review their account activity to identify potential reasons for the freeze. SoundCloud will always inform users via email in these cases. #### What should users expect from support? If your account is frozen, please reach out to our AI agent. They can create a ticket for you, and a support specialist will be in touch. They will assist you in resolving the issue and guide you through the necessary steps to regain access to your account.

Signed In to the Wrong Account?

If you have signed in, but aren’t in your usual account - don’t worry. Your regular profile likely still exists. Try searching for it here, or type the Profile URL into your browser’s search bar. #### Did you sign in with Facebook? If you signed in through Facebook and created a new account, it may be that your regular profile isn’t attached to Facebook . Please do the following:

Delete the new profile you have created through your Account Settings page.

Sign into your regular profile using your email, or full Profile URL (ex: https://soundcloud.com/alex).

If you have created a new account on a mobile device, we do not have account deletion available through the app at this time. Please sign out of the new account on the app, and into your normal profile. You can delete your duplicate account at any time by signing in via Facebook or Google+ through a computer browser. #### Did you sign in with your email address? If you signed in through your email and created a new account, this means that your regular profile isn’t attached to the email you think it is. Please do the following: 1. Delete the new profile you have created through your Account Settings page 2. Send a password reset link by inputting your Profile URL here. This will send a password recovery link to the primary email address that is registered to the SoundCloud account. 3. Search each of your email accounts for messages that come from no-reply@soundcloudmail.com. The email that receives a password reset link is the one attached to your regular profile.

Signing in on a mobile device

If you have created a new account on a mobile device, we do not have account deletion available through the app at this time. Please sign out of the new account on the app, and sign into your normal profile through the steps above. You can delete your duplicate account at any time by logging in with your email through a computer browser.

Switching from Facebook Login to Email Sign-In

If you originally signed up with Facebook but:

  • You no longer want to sign in through the app, or
  • You deleted your Facebook account linked to SoundCloud

You can still access your SoundCloud account by setting a new password. Request a password reset link here using your profile URL or the email linked to your Facebook account. The reset email will be sent to your Facebook-associated email. If you don’t see it, check your spam folder. After resetting your password, you can log in with your email and password instead of Facebook.

To fully disconnect Facebook, log in and do so here. #### I don’t know the email address attached to my Facebook account. If you still have access to your Facebook account, you can view your attached email by going to your Facebook settings .

Troubleshoot Sign-In Issues on Android

  1. Try turning off your internet connection and switching it back on again. (If you’re using data, you may also want to switch to Wi-Fi.
  2. Try pulling down the screen to refresh, which hopefully updates the app.
  3. If you’re still having problems, try clearing your cache by heading to ‘basic settings’ in the app and selecting ‘Clear application cache.’
  4. You may also want to force-stop the app by going to your application manager and clicking ‘Force Stop.’ Then try reopening the app to see if that resolves the issue.
  5. Finally, you could try deleting and reinstalling the app. This sometimes helps resolve issues.

If none of these steps work, please contact us via our AI agent, and they will connect you to a support specialist for further assistance. 

Troubleshoot Sign-In Issues on iOS

  1. Try turning off your internet connection and switching it back on again. (If you’re using data, you may also want to switch to Wi-Fi.
  2. Try pulling down the screen to refresh, which hopefully updates the app.
  3. If you’re still having problems, try clearing your cache by heading to ‘basic settings’ in the app and selecting ‘Clear application cache.’
  4. You may also want to force-stop the app by going to your application manager and clicking ‘Force Stop.’ Then try reopening the app to see if that resolves the issue.
  5. Finally, you could try deleting and reinstalling the app. This sometimes helps resolve issues.

If none of these steps work, please contact us via our AI agent, and they will connect you to a support specialist for further assistance.

Unable to Sign In to Your Account

If you’re having trouble accessing your account, use these steps to identify the issue and regain access. #### Quick Navigation: I forgot my password I forgot my sign-in email I can’t access my email address “Our robots think you’re spam” error Troubleshoot the mobile app #### I forgot my password You can reset your password from any device. 1. Go to the Forgot password page on the web or select Forgot your password? on the mobile app sign-in screen. 2. Enter the email address linked to your account. 3. Check your inbox for a reset link. If you don’t see it, check your spam or junk folder.

I forgot my sign-in email

If you don’t remember which email you used, you can sign in using your profile URL. 1. Open soundcloud.com and search for your profile name. 2. Select your profile to open your page. 3. Copy the part of the URL after soundcloud.com/ (e.g., soundcloud.com/fontainesdublin). 4. Use that profile URL in the email field along with your password to sign in.

I can’t access my email address

If you’ve lost access to the email account linked to your SoundCloud profile, follow these steps to regain entry. ##### Try a linked social account If you previously connected a social profile, you can bypass the email requirement entirely. Select the Continue with Facebook, Google, or Apple icons on the sign-in page to see if an active connection exists. ##### Check for an active session Check all your devices (tablets, old phones, or work computers). If you are still signed in anywhere, go to your Settings immediately to update your email address to one you can currently access. ##### Recover your email via your provider Try to regain access through your email host’s recovery tools: - Google: gmail.com - Microsoft: hotmail.com / msn.com / live.com / windowslive.com / outlook.com - Yahoo: yahoo.com / ymail.com / rocketmail.com - Apple: mac.com / me.com / icloud.com - Telecom/ISP:att.net/ sbcglobal.net / comcast.net/ cox.net / btinternet.com / btopenworld.com - Other: aol.com / aim.com / mail.com / inbox.com

“Our robots think you’re spam” error

If you see a spam or “robot” error, our anti-spam systems may have flagged your connection. This is often resolved with these quick steps: - Refresh the page or try a different web browser. - Disable any active VPNs, ad-blockers, or privacy extensions. - Try a different internet connection (e.g., switch from Wi-Fi to mobile data).

Troubleshoot the mobile app

If you are entering the correct details but the app won’t let you in: 1. Check for updates: Ensure you are running the latest version of the SoundCloud app. 2. Clear cache: On Android, go to Basic settings in the app and select Clear application cache. 3. Reinstall: If the issue persists, delete and reinstall the app. This often resolves minor technical blocks.

Why Am I Being Signed Out Repeatedly

Common issues for frequent sign-outs include browser caching problems, extensions or plug-ins causing interference, using a VPN, and specific device-related issues. #### What steps can users take if they encounter frequent sign-out issues? We suggest trying the following steps: - Clearing the browser’s cache - Disabling any extensions or plug-ins - Try a different browser - Disable your VPN connection - App users: check the app stores for any new updates, and download the latest version - Log out and re-authenticate two-factor authentication (2FA)

Are you using a Sony Xperia device?

We are currently experiencing sign-in issues on Sony Xperia devices. Until we have a proper solution for this problem in place, please try updating the SoundCloud app to the latest version and try signing in again. There are two known workarounds for this issue: 1. Do a full factory reset while not using an SD card 2. Log into a different account (does not always work) 3. Once we have a proper fix for this problem in place, we will post an update on our status blog.

Why Am I Seeing Repeated CAPTCHA Requests When Signing In?

A CAPTCHA is an added security measure that asks you to complete a short written ‘test’ to confirm that you are not a robot. We introduced this as a security measure to protect our users’ accounts from potential security breaches. 

If you are regularly signing in and out of your account on the same day, we’re probably going to ask you to fill this out for us. To avoid getting it so often, we suggest keeping yourself signed in to your account. #### I need to sign into multiple accounts! If you care for multiple accounts on SoundCloud, we recommend using incognito windows or multiple browsers for each profile. This helps reduce the captcha requests.

My Account: Manage My Account

How can I connect my SoundCloud account with my Facebook, Google or Apple account?

SoundCloud now offers you multiple convenient ways to sign into your account. In addition to your usual login credentials, you have the option to access your SoundCloud account using your personal Facebook profile, your Google account, or your Apple account. This enhancement provides you with greater flexibility and security, ensuring that you have alternative methods available to access your account. #### Connecting your Facebook, Google or Apple account To connect your SoundCloud account to Facebook, Google or Apple: 1. Go to your Account Settings 2. Scroll down until you see “Sign in with other social networks” 3. Click on the Facebook*, Google, and/or Apple** button to connect your accounts 4. Sign in using any of the social channels you’ve connected

*SoundCloud can only connect directly to Facebook personal profiles, not Facebook Pages. Apple users must enable Multi-Factor Authentication. #### Disconnecting your Facebook, Google or Apple account  You can disconnect Facebook/Google/Apple from being associated with your SoundCloud account by clicking the Disconnect account** button within your Account Settings. By doing this, you will no longer be able to sign in to your account through Facebook, Google or Apple. Disconnecting means you won’t be able to sign in to SoundCloud with that platform (Facebook, Google, or Apple). Make sure you have another login option, like an email and password, to keep access to your account.

How can I delete my account?

SoundCloud Web

If you’re logged into your SoundCloud account of web, this is how you can delete it: 1. Go to your Account Settings 2. Click the ‘delete account’ button at the bottom of the page. #### Android & iOS Apps You can delete your account while you’re signed in by going to your account on the setting screen, and tapping the ‘delete account’ button.

You can reach your account setting and deletion option by following those steps: 1. Go to your avatar from the library screen 2. Go to* ‘Settings’ 3. Then go to ‘Account’ 4. Click’Delete account’* 5. Confirm the account deletion To delete your account, you must be signed in to your account, so if you are experiencing trouble signing in, please visit Help Accessing Your Accountfor more help first. #### Deletion policy Protecting our users and their data is our first priority. For this reason, we need to fully delete data whenever we are requested to do so by a signed in user. Please bear in mind that, if you delete your account, all data associated with your account–including the sounds that you have uploaded and the usage data associated with those sounds–will be deleted and may not be recoverable.

As SoundCloud is based in Germany, we have a duty to comply with German data protection laws. If our Trust & Safety Team is contacted with a request to manually delete an account, we will always establish that we are being contacted by the account’s verified owner before assisting with the deletion request. In other words; our deletion policy upholds a user’s right to always remove their own account data, while protecting against account fraud and the deletion of data without an account owner’s consent. #### Google search results We don’t have control over the deleted account link showing up in Google’s search results. If you have deleted your account, Google should catch up and recognize this soon. However, as they cache search results for faster loading times, they may keep your information in their search results if enough people have clicked on it in the past. To fully remove your profile/information, you will need to contact Google directly by filling in this public removal form. #### I tried to delete my account, but it isn’t going away. If you deleted your account, it will be put into a deletion queue. If you try to sign back in and get an error message saying that you are frozen, this means that your deletion attempt has timed out, and the account was not deleted properly. If this happens, please reach out to us via our AI agent to have a ticket created for you. A support agent will be in touch shortly after.

Managing Email Addresses in Your SoundCloud Account

Quick Navigation:

How Do I change my primary email address? How do I add a new email address to my account? What should I do if I don’t receive the confirmation email? How do I remove an email address from my account? Lost access to the email address associated with your account? #### How Do I Change My Primary Email Address? 1. Go to your Settings Page. 2. Select the Primary Email: If you have more than one email associated with your account, simply click the ‘Make primary’ button next to the email you want to set as your primary address. 3. Verify your identity with a One Time Password for added security. When changing your primary email address, you’ll need to verify your identity with a 6-digit code sent to your current email. 4. Enter this code to confirm the change. This step ensures only you can update your primary email. If you don’t receive the code, check your spam folder or request a new one.

How Do I Add a New Email Address to My Account?

  1. Go to your Settings Page.
  2. Add the Email: Enter the new email address in the ‘Add an email address’ field.
  3. Confirm the New Email: A confirmation email will be sent to the new address. Check your inbox and click the confirmation link to complete the process.

What should I do if I don’t receive the confirmation email?

  • Check Your Spam/Junk Folder: Sometimes, the confirmation email might be filtered into your spam or junk folder, so check there first.
  • Resend the Confirmation Email: If you still don’t see the email, go back to your SoundCloud settings and resend the confirmation. You can send a password reset email from your settings page.
  • Verify Email Address Accuracy: Ensure that the email address you entered is correct. A typo could prevent the email from being delivered.

How Do I Remove an Email Address from my account?

  1. Go to your Settings Page.
  2. Remove the Email: Click “Remove address”, and then confirm the changes by clicking “Delete”

Note: If you only have one email associated with your account, you won’t be able to remove it. You must add another email address before you can delete the existing one. #### Lost access to the email address associated with your account? Learn how to recover an email address or reach out to our chatbot and provide as much detail as possible. We’ll do our best to help but, if we can’t verify your ownership, we can’t grant access. Send us the following to regain access to your account: - Email address linked to the account - Account creation date - Last sign-in date - Last IP address used (search “what is my IP” to find yours) - Names or upload dates of any private tracks - Names of deleted tracks, if any - A new email to attach (must not be linked to another SoundCloud account)

Managing Multiple SoundCloud Accounts

What alternative strategies can users employ for managing multiple SoundCloud accounts, and what are the implications of deleting one?

It is not possible to merge two SoundCloud accounts into a single account. However, if you need to consolidate your content: - Alternative Strategy: If you have multiple accounts, consider keeping them separate for different purposes (e.g., one for personal projects and another for collaborations). This allows you to maintain distinct profiles and content without losing important data like stats and comments. - Account Deletion and Re-uploading Content: You can delete one of your accounts and re-upload the tracks from the deleted account to the active account you wish to keep. However, keep in mind that the stats, comments, and interactions associated with the tracks on the deleted account will not carry over. This means any engagement, such as followers’ comments and play counts, will be lost.

How does deleting a SoundCloud account affect followers and interactions, and what should users consider before proceeding?

Deleting one of your SoundCloud accounts will result in: - Loss of Followers and Interactions: When you delete an account, you lose all the followers, likes, comments, and other interactions tied to that account. Re-uploading the tracks to a new account will not restore this data, which could impact your overall presence and engagement on the platform. - Impact on Brand Consistency: If your accounts are part of a broader brand or project, consider how deleting one might affect your brand’s consistency and reach. In some cases, it might be more beneficial to maintain both accounts rather than consolidate them to avoid losing valuable engagement data.

Merging accounts

It is not possible to merge two SoundCloud accounts into a single account. However, you can always delete one of your accounts and upload any tracks from the deleted account to the active account you wish to keep. The only drawback of doing this is that the stats and comments from the tracks you re-upload will not carry over.

Sharing access to an account

We understand that the SoundCloud community is built on collaboration, and that you may want to share access and account responsibilities with band members, managers, or others who help you manage your sounds. However, we don’t advise sharing access to an account, even with those you trust. By sharing access, you will leave yourself at risk of changes being made, or your account being deleted without your consent.

Before making the decision to share an account or not, remember; we consider the owner of the email address used at sign-up is considered to be the account owner. Therefore, if you do go ahead with creating a shared account, we would advise that you use an email address which you all have access to, so that you can all access the account. Learn moreabout our policy and process for conflict of ownership.

Sign out of your account

On Web

To sign out of your account, click the three dots in the top navigation header, then select ‘Sign out’. You will then be directed to a screen that confirms that you have signed out successfully. #### On Android To sign out of your account from the Android app: 1. Start by heading to your Profile page. You can get there by tapping the Library icon in the bottom right corner of the screen. 2. Once you’re on your Profile page, scroll to the bottom and tap Sign Out. 3. After selecting this option, you’ll see a pop-up message that says: “Signing out removes all downloaded tracks.”  This message is specifically relevant for Go or Go+ users, meaning that any music you’ve saved for offline listening will be removed from your device.

If you sign back into the same account later, your music and library will still be there—but you’ll need to manually re-download any albums or playlists you want available offline. #### On iOS To sign out of your account from the iOS app: 1. Go to your Profile page by tapping the Library icon in the bottom right corner. 2. From there, tap your avatar in the top right corner (next to the casting button). This will take you into your account settings. 3. Tap the Account option (located below the Autoplay toggle), where you’ll find the Sign Out button. Once you select Sign Out, you’ll be asked to confirm your choice.

After confirming, you’ll be signed out of your account, and all downloaded tracks will be removed from your device.

My Account: Passwords & Account Recovery

How to Reset Your Password

If you would like to reset your password, simply click the ‘Send password reset link’ button in your Account Settings. The password reset link will be sent to all email addresses connected to your account. #### Tips for Creating a Secure Password: - Use a Strong Password: Create a password that is difficult to guess by including a mix of uppercase and lowercase letters, numbers, and special characters. Avoid using easily guessable information like names or common words. - Unique Passwords for Each Service: Do not reuse passwords across multiple services. Each account should have its own unique password to prevent a breach in one service from compromising your accounts on other platforms. - Consider a Password Manager: Using a password manager can help you create and store strong, unique passwords for all your accounts without the need to remember each one individually.

For more information on securing your SoundCloud account, please see our help center article here.

How to Troubleshoot Missing Password Reset Emails

If you don’t receive a password reset email after requesting it, try these steps: 1. Check your Spam or Junk folder. 2. Look for an email from SoundCloud with a subject like “Request to change SoundCloud password”. 3. Wait at least five minutes for the email to arrive. 4. Check any other email accounts you may have used.

If you’ve taken the above steps and still can’t log in, please see this help center article.

What to Do If Someone Else Created Your Account

If the account was set up on your behalf, you’ll need to get the person who created the account to add your email address to it. If there is a conflict regarding the ownership of an account which was once shared or set up on your behalf, we must follow our account ownership policy which states that the owner of an account is the individual who controls the email address used at sign up. #### In such conflicts, the following options are available to you: 1. Gain access to the email used to create the account, and we can restore it. 2. If this is not possible, you can report the account, or content hosted on the account, for violating our Terms of Use on the following grounds;

Impersonation and/or misrepresentation: If the account is misrepresenting its affiliation with you or is impersonating you, please let us know. If we find evidence of a Terms of Use violation, we will then be able to suspend the reported account. You can find out more about impersonation and how to report it here. 3. Copyright Infringement: If the account is hosting content which you own the rights to, you can report this using our Copyright infringement form. This will allow you to remove content which you own the rights to from SoundCloud. 4. Trademark Violation: If the account is infringing your trademark rights, you can let us know by emailing trademarks@soundcloud.com with proof of your registration. If we find evidence of trademark infringement, we can request for the account owner to change their URL and/or Display Name.

A final option is to follow due legal process to determine ownership of the account in question. If you can obtain a court order or settlement agreement in your favor (regarding this profile specifically) within 90 days of the reported account’s suspension, this will then be treated as a legal request, meaning that we can revert the suspension and pass access over to you. Please contact us at legal@soundcloud.com, providing detailed documentation from your legal representative. While we can appreciate that this process may seem complex, we hope that you can understand that our primary aim is to provide a service which respects both the privacy and security of our community members and their data. This means that we must follow our account ownership policy and related processes at all times.

What to Do If You Receive an Unrequested Password Reset Email

If you receive a password reset email that you didn’t request, the safest course of action is to ignore it. This could be a phishing attempt. Remember, no one can reset your SoundCloud password without access to your email account. If you’re unsure whether the email is legitimate, do not click on any links or provide any information. Instead, manually navigate to the SoundCloud website and check your account settings.

As a security precaution, we recommend that you reset your SoundCloud password. You may also want to reset your email password for extra protection. Additionally, please be sure two-factor authentication (2FA) is enabled on your account. This adds an extra layer of protection, making it much harder for unauthorized users to gain access.

What to Do If You’re Logged Out of a Shared Account
