SoundCloud Fans & Listeners: Filters & Personalization

Dark mode

Apps

Dark mode is the default mode for our iOS and Android apps. #### Web You can change between dark and light mode in your settings page.

Mood & Genre Filters

Now you can instantly filter your tracks based on what you’re feeling in the moment. Navigate to your Liked tracks from the Library, just pick your mood or genre and your entire collection will be filtered by AI, serving you up a perfect playlist to match it. - Depending on the types of tracks you have liked, you will see different mood and genre filters. - You can easily tap on any filter which will then create a playlist for that mood/genre (e.g. playful, dancy or electronic). - You can play or shuffle (using the buttons above the filters) the tracks in their genre as if it were a playlist. - There’s 64 Moods & Genres available at the moment, with more to come. - If you are a new user, the filters will only appear once you have 10 or more tracks liked.

Please note:  this feature is currently available to Go and Go+ subscribers on iOS and Android. (image: Screenshot 2024-09-06 at 15.02.41.png)

SoundCloud Fans & Listeners: Library, Likes & Social Features

Add & manage captions on reposts

Add a caption to a repost

To add a caption, click the repost button, enter your text in the caption field, and select Repost to publish. Please note: - You must have a verified email address to add captions. - Captions are limited to 140 characters, including spaces.

Captions will appear in your followers’ Stream alongside your repost, not on your profile page. #### Edit or remove a caption To update or remove a caption, locate your repost in your Stream and click the repost button again. From there, you can edit the text or clear it entirely. Please note: Tracks can only be reposted once. Editing a caption will not repost the track again or resurface it in your followers’ Streams. #### Visibility and blocking Your followers can see captions in their Stream. If you block a user: - They cannot see your reposts or captions - They cannot repost your tracks

To report a caption, open the More menu on the repost and select Report. You can choose whether to report the track or the caption.

Artists Shortcuts for Fans

Shortcuts to your favorite artists so you can immediately get their latest drops as soon as they are posted, directly on your home page. (image: Stories_Listener_Web_HelpCenter_2.gif) #### How do I get updates? Follow at least two of your favorite artists. #### How often will I get an update? You’ll get an update every time the creators you follow posts and reposts. #### Does the track automatically play or do I need to click it on?  The track preview will autoplay once you click on the artists’ avatar. #### How can I play the full track? By clicking on the story, you can listen to the full track in the player. #### What else can I do in the story?  You can like the track, repost it, and add it to a playlist. #### How do I get to the next update? The next update will autoplay, and you can also click the right arrow/clickthrough to preview all other updates. #### What happens after I click on an update? The orange unread indicator will go away to indicate that it was read.   #### Can I mute updates? You cannot mute updates from artists you are following. #### I no longer have the module Your updates expire after 7 days, and if you do not have new updates, the module will go away until new updates are available, so make sure you follow all of your favorite artists to improve the likelihood of consistent updates. #### Are you a creator?  Learn how to set up your own Artist Shortcuts here.

Follow & unfollow other users

An important aspect of SoundCloud is the community we have, and following other members is a great way to find new music and audio to listen to. When you follow another user, their new tracks, playlists, and reposts will be displayed in your** Stream **as soon as they’re posted or uploaded. This makes it easy to stay up to date with your favorite artists and labels. The person you follow doesn’t have to follow you back for you to see their public updates.

You can find who you are following by going to your Library page to the Following tab. #### How to follow To follow someone, you just need to navigate to their profile page and click the orange Follow button.

Additionally, you’ll see suggested accounts to follow on the right side of your Feed and Discover sections under ‘Who to follow’.

Please note: We have on-site limits to promote genuine, close-knit communities around creators’ tracks. These limits detect accounts misusing features like following, liking, reposting, and messaging, and may restrict access. #### How to unfollow To stop following someone, simply click the ‘Following’ icon that appears to be an orange ’Follow’ button again. The person will not be notified of your decision.

Liked By

Liked By makes it easier to discover music that’s resonating with your community on SoundCloud. When someone you follow—like a friend, fellow listener, or artist—likes a track, you’ll see their profile picture next to that track across the platform, for example, in playlists you’re listening to. #### How it works Whenever a track has been liked by someone you follow, their profile image will appear next to it. See which tracks are on your community’s radar. Look for Liked By in: - Playlists (yours and others) - Search results - Track lists on artist pages - Your Home feed - Liked tracks - Your uploads - And more

Liked By playlists & track list

Follow friends or artists to see a list of liked tracks and playlists compiling their likes on home. The more people you follow, the more opportunities you have to check out what your favorite people and artists are liking. You are automatically opted in to these playlists and can opt out at any time in your Settings. #### Why are you seeing them Liked By indicators are part of how SoundCloud helps to connect you with the people and artists you care about: - Expand your music taste beyond your current favorites - Help your followers discover new music every time you drop a like - Build community and encourage social connections on SoundCloud - Highlight active listeners in your musical community

These small signals make a big impact, helping you feel the presence of your community as you listen. #### Want to see more Liked By** activity?** To see more Liked By, follow people whose music taste you trust—friends, creators, or artists you’re into. The more people you follow, the more Liked By activity you’ll see across the platform. You can also interact with tracks by liking them yourself, which helps your followers discover what you’re enjoying.

Move Your Music to SoundCloud

Music collections are personal: your library took years to compile, and playlists can be time capsules of our past selves. Moving to a new music platform can feel like moving into a new home. To make it easy we’re introducing a new feature, available to SoundCloud free and subscribed users, in the mobile app, that will allow you to move your music to SoundCloud. #### How do I move my music from other platforms? Move Your Music allows you to import your playlists and likes from other music platforms, including: - Spotify - Apple Music - Deezer - Tidal - Amazon Music - Resso

This new functionality simplifies the process of replicating your music collection on SoundCloud, so you can get up and running without having to manually rebuild your playlists. #### What Can I Move? Move Your Music allows you to move - Your liked songs - Your playlists (even ones you follow / liked but did not create yourself, like editorial playlists on other platforms)

Why Are We Offering This?

Because no one who has been collecting music for years should have to re-build their music library from scratch. The effort to transfer likes and playlists from other platforms can be time-consuming and complicated. By offering the Move Your Music feature, we aim to make it easier for you to migrate your existing music collections and start enjoying SoundCloud right away. #### How Does It Work? 1. Ensure you’re logged in to your SoundCloud account on the latest version of the SoundCloud app 2. Go to the Settings page and click “Import my music”. 3. Select the platform you’d like to transfer from (Spotify, Apple Music, etc.) 4. Follow the prompts to connect your other account to SoundCloud and choose which playlists or likes you want to transfer 5. Once your library is imported, it will appear in your SoundCloud library, and you can start listening immediately. Note: Certain songs may not be available based on the subscription you have.

Which Platforms Are Supported?

Currently, the Move Your Music feature supports imports from: - Spotify - Apple Music - Deezer - Tidal - Amazon Music - Resso

Please note: imported likes are now reversible on Android and iOS. Just go to Settings > Import my Music >* Manage imported likes.*

React to Tracks

Reactions are a new way to show your love for tracks on SoundCloud — artists love to see signs that listeners are vibing with the music they release on SoundCloud, and fans love to see excitement in the community as they listen to the same track in real time. #### How Do I Use Them? - Add a Reaction: Open the full-screen player, find the interaction bar, and tap your favorite reaction emoji. It’ll stick to that specific moment in the track for everyone to see. - See & Remove Reactions: Go to the Comments view to see reactions from others. If you change your mind, you can remove your own reactions here, too.

Can I add more than one Reaction to a track?

Yes! Go wild. Reactions are attached to a specific timestamp in the song. You are able to add multiple of all types, if that is how you feel. We do have some common-sense limits to stop it from getting too wild, but we doubt you’ll notice. #### Can I pick different emojis? Right now, you can only use our default set of reactions. We are exploring options to let you or the artist choose from a wider set of emojis in the future, so stay tuned for that. #### Is it possible to turn them off? Of course. Both fans and artists have control: - For Fans: We have extended the “Show Comments on Player” controls to also show or hide reactions.  iOS: Go to Settings > Social > Show Comments & Reactions on Player. - Android: Go to Settings > Basic Settings > Show Comments & Reactions on Player.

Got some feedback on Track Reactions? It’s a new feature, and we would love to hear it. product.support+reactions@soundcloud.com. Please keep in mind that it is not always possible for us to reply to all emails sent to this address. This address is specifically for capturing user feedback and is not monitored for general customer support tickets.

Repost Tracks & Playlists

Reposts are the fastest way to post songs to your Profile page and to share your favorite discoveries on SoundCloud with your friends and followers.

Click the repost button below any track or playlist to add it to the top of your profile, and share it to the Feed of your followers. To remove a reposted item from your profile, click on its ‘repost’ button again. It’s only possible to see one post or a repost of a specific track in your Following Feed. Initially, all tracks are “posted” by a creator in the feed; however, if someone that you follow reposts the track, the repost will be shown at the top of your feed and erase any post of the same track from another user if it’s further down in your feed. You cannot repost your own track or add reposts to your Spotlight. #### Removing reposts: To remove your repost, please click the orange repost icon again and click “Delete repost”. Please note: We enforce on-site limits to foster genuine, close-knit communities around creators’ tracks. These limits target accounts misusing features like following, liking, reposting, and messaging, and may restrict access to those features. See feature policies here.

Save songs from TikTok to SoundCloud

Love a sound or song on TikTok? Now you can instantly save it to SoundCloud so it can live alongside your entire music library. #### How Does It Work? 1. Log in to TikTokMake sure you’re logged in to TikTok and have the latest version of the app installed. Note: Make sure you have SoundCloud installed on your device. 2. There are two ways to enable this feature: Go to “Settings and Privacy”, “Music”, then “Save to music app”. Select SoundCloud as your default music app. 3. Note: If you’re already connected to another streaming service, you’ll follow the same steps, then confirm “Switch” to SoundCloud as your default app.

  • You’ll be asked to log in to your SoundCloud account via the TikTok app and grant access. Click “Connect and Continue.” If Two-Factor Authentication is enabled, enter the 2FA code from your authentication app.

  • Once your SoundCloud account is connected, tap “Add to SoundCloud” on the sound details page to add the track to your library and listen anytime in your Liked Tracks.

Feature Availability

TikTok’s Add to Music App feature is available in 184 countries. SoundCloud’s full music catalog is reserved for subscribers in the territories where Go and Go+ are available. Content availability on SoundCloud through the Add to Music App will depend on your territory and listening subscription status. For U.S. users, make sure you’re on at least version 38.0.0 to take advantage of this feature.

Search Your Likes

It is now easier than ever to find music that you have previously liked on SoundCloud. Did you find a track that you really like and want to hear more of? Head to your Likes page and use the search function provided. #### On Web  Head to your Likes and use the Search feature in the top right-hand corner. #### Android and iOS Use the Search bar at the top to find music that you have already liked.

Your Library & Feed

Your SoundCloud library and feed are your gateways to staying connected with the music, playlists, and creators you love. Managing these features ensures that you always have easy access to your favorite tracks, updates from artists you follow, and a personalized soundtrack, whether you’re using the SoundCloud app or website. #### Understanding Your Library Your SoundCloud library is your personal collection of liked tracks, playlists, albums, and followed artists. Use the library to organize your listening experience and revisit your favorite moments quickly. Access your library from the app’s bottom menu or on the website’s main navigation bar. With a SoundCloud Go subscription, you can listen to your entire Library offline on iOS and Android, perfect for enjoying music without internet access. #### How to Manage Your Library 1. Open SoundCloud on your app or browser and sign in. 2. Tap or click the Library icon to access your liked tracks, playlists, and followed artists. 3. To remove a track or playlist, tap the “heart” again to unlike, or select options to unfollow or delete. 4. Organize playlists by creating, editing, or rearranging tracks as needed.

Keeping Your Feed Fresh

Your feed shows updates from artists you follow, new releases, reposts, and relevant recommendations. To tailor your feed, actively follow or unfollow artists and engage with content you enjoy. The more you interact, the better SoundCloud personalizes your listening experience.

Your Likes & Playlists

Like any track or playlist, to find it easily later, and let its creator or curator know their work is appreciated. Click the Heart icon below any tracks or playlist to add it to your Likes. The heart will turn from grey to orange. You can unlike a track or playlist by clicking the heart again to turn it back to grey. Please note: It is not possible to like private tracks or playlists. It’s also not possible to like the tracks that you’ve uploaded to your account. You can shuffle and listen to your Likes here, or visit this page via your Library.

We enforce on-site limits to promote genuine, close-knit communities around creators’ tracks. These limits detect accounts misusing features like following, liking, reposting, and messaging, and may block access. Read our feature-use policies here. #### Why can’t I like a track? There is a daily limit for the number of like actions that you can make within 24 hours. If you are repeatedly flagged for this activity, you will be blocked from liking or unliking any track(s) or playlist(s) for a period of time. As we wish to prevent this activity in the future, each block you receive will increase in length. If you’re trying to like tracks in order to save them for offline listening, please note that you can always add these to a playlist instead of liking them, and you won’t run into any limits.

Cast to devices

Take your listening experience beyond your phone – cast your SoundCloud tracks directly to nearby devices, whether it’s a smart speaker, headphones, or your smart TV. Cast to devices is compatible with devices that support Bluetooth, AirPlay, or Chromecast casting functionality. #### How to cast To start casting, make sure you’re on the latest version of the SoundCloud app for iOS and for AirPlay and Chromecast, be sure your phone and device are on the same wifi network. Then: 1. Select the track you want to play 2. Tap the cast icon 3. Choose a nearby device from the list (TVs, smart speakers, headphones, and more) 4. Once connected, your audio will start playing on the selected device 5. You’ll be able to control playback from your phone

Troubleshooting Tips

If you don’t see your device listed, make sure: 1. It’s powered on and connected to the same Wi-Fi network (for AirPlay and Chromecast) 2. You’re running the latest version of the SoundCloud app 3. Your iOS device’s Bluetooth and Wi-Fi are turned on 4. Try restarting your device or the SoundCloud app if the issue persists

You can listen to your favorite SoundCloud tracks with Siri. To get started, just say “Hey Siri, play SoundCloud.” and confirm that Siri is allowed to access your data on SoundCloud. To play SoundCloud’s curated playlists: - “Hey Siri, play the playlist The Day Ones on SoundCloud.” - “Hey Siri, play the playlist Fresh Pressed on SoundCloud.”

You can also control the playback or a track with: - “Hey Siri, pause.” - “Hey Siri, resume.” - “Hey Siri, next track.” - “Hey Siri, turn up the volume.”

You can use Siri with SoundCloud when your phone is connected via bluetooth to speakers or to your car entertainment. Please make sure that you have turned on the setting “Talk to Siri”” from your iOS devices accessibility settings.

SoundCloud Fans & Listeners: Listening & App Troubleshooting

Can’t find a track anymore

There are several reasons why a track you may have previously played on SoundCloud might not be playable any longer. These reasons include: Track deletion or removal: The track has been deleted by its owner or removed from the platform for copyright infringement. Privacy Settings: The track has been made private by its owner. If it were a private track already, then the secret token may have been changed by the user. Over upload limit: The user who uploaded the track may have gone over their upload limit, or their subscription may have lapsed, causing any tracks over the Basic plan’s limit to be hidden from listeners. Account suspension or deletion: The uploader’s account may have been deleted by its owner or removed for breaching our terms and conditions in relation to spam, copyrights, abuse, etc. Blocked in your region: It may be that the original uploader does not have the necessary rights to make a track available in your territory. As a consequence, the track might not be available in your region. Incorrect URL: The URL may have been misspelled or may have included an extra character.

Common Streaming Issues

Streaming music seamlessly is at the heart of the SoundCloud experience. However, playback or streaming errors can occur due to network, device, or app-related issues. Whether you’re an artist previewing your latest track or a fan enjoying your favorite playlist, this guide will help you diagnose and fix common SoundCloud streaming problems on web and mobile. #### Common Causes of Streaming Issues - Unstable or slow internet connection - Outdated app or browser versions - Corrupted app cache or data - Device-specific software bugs

Quick Troubleshooting Steps

  1. Check your internet connection. Switch between WiFi and mobile data or restart your router if needed.
  2. Update the SoundCloud app or your web browser to the latest version.
  3. Clear cache/data from your SoundCloud app settings (Android/iOS) or clear browser cache on web.
  4. Restart your device to refresh its network and memory.

On Android or iOS apps

Pull down on the screen until you see a spinning wheel to refresh the page, and see if that helps. If not, check to make sure that you are on a stable wifi or date connection. If you are still experiencing trouble, please delete and reinstall the app and see if that helps. #### On Web If you are having trouble when streaming, first make sure that you are using a browser version that SoundCloud supports. The lowest browser versions SoundCloud supports are: - Chrome 57 or newer - Firefox 50 or newer - Edge 18 or newer - Safari 10.1 or newer

If you are using a lower browser version, please upgrade it. #### My browser version is up to date. What do I do? Please try loading the page after following these steps: 1. Check our** Status Blog **to make sure that there are no interruptions on site that could cause you difficulties loading pages 2. Check to see if the page loads in another browser, i.e., Firefox, Chrome, Edge 3. If applicable, try disabling anti-virus and any firewalls your browser may have installed

When to Contact SoundCloud Support

  • Persistent errors after trying all troubleshooting steps
  • Streaming issues for only certain tracks or albums
  • Suspected account-related restrictions or technical bugs

Hiding or removing other users’ tracks

Depending on the track’s platform location, you might be able to remove it. Where does the track appear? #### Your Feed If you want to stop seeing tracks or reposts from certain users in your** **Feed, you just need to unfollow them. This will remove all current tracks, reposts, and playlists from your Feed and prevent new uploads from appearing.

There isn’t a way to remove individual tracks from the Feed. #### Your Library To stop seeing certain tracks or playlists on your Library page, you need to unlike them. You can unlike by clicking the ‘Liked’ button to be ‘Like’. #### Your playlist If you created a playlist and added tracks to it, you can also remove those tracks. Read more about how to do this here. #### Recommended tracks There’s no way to remove recommended tracks from your individual track’s page if it is public. If your track is private, no recommended tracks will play afterward.

I’m Not Getting Notifications from Artists I Follow

If you’re not receiving notifications from the artists you follow, try the following: 1. Make Sure Your App is Updated to the Latest Version 2. Check Your Device Settings: Ensure that notifications are enabled for the SoundCloud app on your phone. Go to your device’s settings and make sure SoundCloud is allowed to send notifications. 3. Verify Your Follow Status: Go to the profiles of your favorite artists to confirm that you’re still following them. 4. Adjust Notification Preferences: Visit the artist’s profile page. 5. Click on the bell icon. 6. Select “All New Releases” to receive notifications for the new tracks they release. 7. Choose “Personalized” to get notifications based on your interaction with the artist.

I’m Getting Too Many New Release Notifications

Feeling overwhelmed by notifications? You can manage and customize them to better suit your preferences: 1. Modify Notification Settings for Specific Artists: Make sure your app is updated to the latest version 2. Go to the profile page of the artists you follow. 3. Click on the bell icon. 4. Switch from “All New Releases” to “Personalized”. This setting will prioritize notifications based on your engagement with the artist and the content you interact with the most. 5. Turn Off Notifications or Unfollow: If you prefer not to receive notifications from a particular artist, you can choose to receive “No Notifications” from them. 6. Alternatively, you can unfollow the artist entirely if their notifications are no longer relevant to you.

I’m Getting Too Few Notifications

If you’re not getting enough notifications, here’s what you can do: 1. Make Sure Your App is Updated to the Latest Version 2. Check Your Device Settings: Ensure that notifications are enabled for the SoundCloud app on your phone. Verify this in your device’s settings. 3. Verify Your Follow Status: Make sure you’re following your favorite artists by checking their SoundCloud profiles. 4. Adjust Notification Preferences: Go to the artist’s profile page. 5. Click on the bell icon. 6. Select “All New Releases” to be notified of the new tracks they release. 7. Choose “Personalized” to receive notifications tailored to your interactions with the artist.

Listen and discover troubleshooting

Sorry that you are having trouble with your listening experience on SoundCloud. #### What kind of problems are you having? I can’t find a track anymore

Regional availability

Some SoundCloud Content Partners have the ability to select which territories they wish to have their content available in, depending on licensing rights. If a SoundCloud user does not have the licensing rights to release a track globally, they may only make it available in the countries where they hold those rights. As a result, the track may not be available in certain regions.

Unable to play tracks

If you are unable to play a certain track it might be that this SoundCloud member does not have the licensing rights to release a track everywhere, they may only make it available within the countries where they have the rights to do so. As a consequence the track might not be available in certain regions. #### On Android or iOS apps Pull down on the screen until you see a spinning wheel to refresh the page, and see if that helps. If not, check to make sure that you are on a stable wifi or 3G/4G/5G connection. If you are still experiencing trouble, please delete and reinstall the app and see if that helps. #### On Web If you are unable to play any tracks on SoundCloud, please follow the steps below: 1. Try refreshing the page. In most cases, playback hiccups are only temporary. 2. Check our Status Blog for news and updates on any service interruptions that may be occurring. 3. Clear your browser’s cache and cookies, and then restart it. 4. Check to make sure you have the latest version of your browser installed. 5. Disable any extensions or ad-blocking plugins that could be blocking SoundCloud from working properly and add soundcloud.com to the exceptions list in the plug-in settings of your browser. 6. Try a different browser (such as Firefox, or Chrome) to see if it is a local issue on your browser.

SoundCloud Fans & Listeners: Offline Listening & Downloads

Downloading tracks

On Web, you can download tracks once you have signed in to your SoundCloud account by clicking on the download file button beneath the waveform. You can enable, or disable downloads for your listeners through your track’s Permissions tab. Enabling downloads means that your listener can have a copy of your original file format that you have uploaded to SoundCloud. Please note: Not all tracks are downloadable. If you don’t see a download file button, it means the user who uploaded it did not intend for it to be downloadable. Additionally, only individual tracks can be downloaded and playlists as a whole are not available. Saving content on mobile devices

It is not possible to download a track from a mobile device. However, users with a SoundCloud Go or Go+ subscription can save content for offline listening on a mobile device.

Manage Offline Listening on SoundCloud Go

SoundCloud Go is now available in multiple countries. Check to see if SoundCloud Go has launched in your country. We will be rolling out to more countries in the near future. To keep up to date on where SoundCloud Go is being released next, check out our blog for more updates.   

The best way to ensure individual tracks are saved offline with a SoundCloud Go subscription is to add them to a playlist you’ve created or to your Likes. 

From there, save your playlist, Likes, or entire Library offline. Once you’ve added the track to your playlist or Likes, refresh your app by pulling down on the screen to ensure that the newly added track is saved for offline listening. #### How do I save content for offline listening? With a SoundCloud Go subscription, you can save your Likes, playlists, and your entire Library for offline listening on your mobile device. Here’s how: #### Saving Likes for Offline Listening: - Go to your Library and then to your Likes - Click the download button - You’ll see the progress of how many tracks are left to save in the orange progress bar at the bottom of your screen on iOS or in the pull-down menu on Android.

Saving Playlists for Offline Listening:

  • Go to your Library and to the playlist you want to save
  • Click the download button (the small arrow next to the heart)
  • You’ll see the progress of how many tracks are left to save in the orange progress bar on the bottom of your screen on iOS or in the pull-down menu on Android.

Automatically Save Your Library for Offline Listening:

  • Go to your Settings page, then go to Downloads
  • Turn on “Download automatically” to save your entire Library of Likes and playlists for offline listening.

Saving Over Wi-Fi Connections:

  • If you want to save data, you can set tracks and playlists to save offline only when connected to Wi-Fi.
  • Go to your settings page and toggle the button next to “Only download via Wi-Fi”

How do I remove content from offline listening?

  • Removing Likes: To remove all your Likes from offline listening, click the orange download arrow on your Likes page to turn it gray.
  • Removing Playlists: To remove a playlist from offline listening, click the orange save offline arrow on the playlist, turning it gray.

Removing Your Entire Library:

  • Go to the Storage tab on your app’s Settings page.
  • Click ’Remove all downloads. This will remove all currently saved tracks and playlists and prevent new Likes or playlists from being automatically saved.

Removing Individual Tracks:

  • Currently, there is no way to remove an individual track from offline listening without removing it entirely from your Likes or playlist.

Removing Playlists:

  • Go to the playlist and click the three dots to see the option to remove the playlist from downloads.

I’m having problems with offline listening content. What can I do?

If you encounter issues with offline listening, follow this troubleshooting guide: ##### Recently Added Tracks Not Showing Up: - Check your Offline Listening Settings page. - If you have enabled “Only save via Wi-Fi” and are trying to save over a 3G/4G/5G or LTE connection, either connect to Wi-Fi or disable the “Only save via Wi-Fi” setting.

Tracks and Playlists Disappeared:
  • Offline content is temporarily stored in your mobile device’s SoundCloud app.
  • If you uninstall the app or sign out, you will lose all offline content. Before doing so, consider if you’re prepared to re-save your Library for offline listening after reinstalling or signing back in.
General Offline Listening Issues:
  • Ensure you are connected to a stable Wi-Fi network if you’ve set your app to only save content via Wi-Fi.
  • Restart the app and try refreshing your Library or playlist by pulling down the screen.
Track not available for Offline Listening:
  • SoundCloud ensures that the rights holder has the ability to control how and in what countries they want their tracks to be available to listeners.
  • If a track is not available for offline listening in a playlist or your Library with your SoundCloud Go subscription, this is because the rights holder of the track has chosen to disable the ability to listen to the track offline.

  

Trouble with offline listening

SoundCloud Go is now available in multiple countries. To keep up to date on where SoundCloud Go is being released next, check out our blog for more updates. If recently added tracks are not showing up in your saved Library, Likes, or playlists offline, first check your Offline Listening Settings page. If you have enabled saving offline only over a Wi-Fi connection and are trying to save over a 3G/4G/5G or LTE connection, either connect to Wi-Fi or disable the ‘Only save via Wi-Fi’ setting. The tracks and playlists you have saved for offline listening are temporarily locally stored in your mobile device’s SoundCloud app. This means that if you have uninstalled the SoundCloud app, or have signed out and back in, you will lose what you have chosen for offline listening in your Library or playlists. Please consider whether you are prepared to re-save your Library for offline listening before uninstalling or signing out of the app. #### Why isn’t a track available for offline listening? SoundCloud ensures that the rights holder has the ability to control how and in what countries they want their tracks to be available to listeners. 

If a track is not available for offline listening in a playlist or your Library with your** **SoundCloud Go subscription, this is because the rights holder of the track has chosen to disable the ability to listen to the track offline.

SoundCloud Fans & Listeners: Playback Controls & Audio Experience

Ads on SoundCloud

Every time you see or hear an ad, artists get paid. Occasional advertising on our platform allow us to continue to support artists and keep SoundCloud free for listeners.

If you would like to remove ads from your listening experience, you can purchase SoundCloud Go through our website or Android app for a lower price, or through the Apple App Store with additional transactional fees attached. #### Ads on embedded players If an embedded track has an audio ad at the beginning, the owner of the track is part of the revenue sharing level of our creator partner program and has enabled ads on their content.

Only the artist or partner and SoundCloud will share in the revenue generated. The external website and the person embedding the track will not share in any revenue. #### Advertising on SoundCloud Want to learn more about advertising on SoundCloud? Read further here.

Audio Streaming Formats

What Audio Streaming Formats Does SoundCloud Provide?

SoundCloud is home to the largest community of artists and fans in the world, and we want to make streaming available for everyone. Below, you can find information on what formats SoundCloud streams, how we use different qualities for different situations, and specific information for creators. #### Available Formats Our standard streaming format is Advanced Audio Coding (AAC). Based on the quality of the uploaded source file, we transcode tracks into as many as three AAC qualities: - High Quality (256k or higher): Transcoded to 256k, 160k, and 96k - Medium Quality (160k to 255k): Transcoded to 160k and 96k - Standard Quality (Under 160k): Transcoded to 96k only Note: Legacy tracks currently streaming as MP3s are being actively migrated to AAC. #### Why Does SoundCloud Create “Low Quality” 96k Transcodings? Many people in the world have limited mobile data plans or slower internet connections. Providing a 96k transcoding allows people to stream content that might otherwise be too expensive or require a lot of buffering time before playback. We think that users should be able to stream at a lower quality instead of being cut off by slow or expensive internet connections. Free listeners can stream 96k and 160k, Go+ listeners also get access to 256k transcodings. #### Information for Creators: For more information about the best formats to upload your tracks to take full advantage of these transcodings, see our help page on High Quality Streaming.

High Quality Streaming

SoundCloud is home to the largest community of artists and fans in the world, and we want you to hear every detail. High Quality (HQ) streaming allows you to listen to your favorite tracks in a superior audio format. #### What is HQ Streaming? High-quality streaming is an exclusive feature for SoundCloud Go+ subscribers. While standard tracks are streamed at 128kbps MP3, HQ tracks are encoded in 256kbps AAC—the equivalent of a 320kbps MP3. Which tracks are available in HQ? Any track uploaded in a lossless format (.wav, .flac, .alac, or .aiff) or a high-bitrate lossy format is eligible for HQ streaming. We are constantly working with our creators to ensure as much content as possible is available in this superior format. #### How to Enable HQ Streaming HQ streaming is not turned on by default to help save your data. Here is how to activate it: - On Web: Go to your Settings page under the Streaming tab and select High quality audio. - On iOS: Go to your Library, tap the three dots (…) in the top right, select Settings > Streaming Quality, and tap High Quality audio. - On Android: Tap the More symbol (bottom right), select Settings > Streaming Quality, and tap High Quality audio.

Information for Creators

To ensure your fans hear your music in HQ, you must upload your files in a lossless format: - Recommended: .WAV, .FLAC, .AIFF, or .ALAC. - Bitrate: 16-bit / 44.1 kHz or higher. - Pro-Tip: If you upload an MP3, we cannot “up-convert” it to HQ. Always start with the highest quality source file possible. You can find more information on preparing your tracks for HQ here.

Offline & Mobile Data

  • Offline Listening: As a Go+ subscriber, your offline downloads will automatically match your streaming quality settings. If you have “High Quality” enabled, your offline tracks will download in HQ.
  • Data Usage: High-quality audio uses more data than standard streaming. If you are on a limited data plan, we recommend enabling HQ only when connected to Wi-Fi.

Not a Go+ Subscriber? Unlock High Quality streaming, ad-free listening, and full track access.

Next up - Play Queue

With the Next Up feature, you can add the tracks you like to your listening queue. #### How does it work? Next up adds functionality to the player in your web browser, Android and iOS app: - See what’s coming up next - Reorder items in the queue (and remove them) - Add to the queue from elsewhere around soundcloud.com - Full set of shuffle & repeat modes (beyond existing repeat-one toggle)

On Web On both Android and iOS, you can control and see what songs you’ve added to your queue. You can also reorder songs to your liking or remove songs from your queue. On Android            On iOS  We’ve moved the repeat button on iOS into your queue so you can access it all from the same screen! #### Autoplay Station and Continuous Play Once your track or playlist finishes, you’ll continue your listening experience with the next track or playlist on your Feed or profile. If you are listening to a track or playlist on their individual page, a recommended track will start playing afterwards. If you have been adding tracks to your Next Up queue, you can disable Station Autoplay to prevent additional related tracks from being added to the queue.

Shuffling and Repeating tracks

Shuffling tracks

You can listen to your own or another user’s Likes or playlists on shuffle on Web, or through our Android and iOS apps. 

For Likes, simply go to the your Likes then click the ‘shuffle’ button displayed in the top right so it displays orange. For Playlists, the same button is displayed below the playlist’s artwork. #### Repeating tracks You can listen to any track on repeat. Simply go to the player on the bottom of your screen and click on the arrow icon: Clicking on the icon and turning it orange will activate ‘repeat’. The song will repeat until you uncheck the icon. You can also press ‘SHIFT + L’ on your computer’s keyboard to turn the repeat button on. On mobile, you can repeat tracks and playlists via the Next Up feature. Artist subscribers have access to: - 3-hour limit on upload time - Amplify** ****2 tracks per month - 3 track replacements** per month (keeping your stats) - 1 spotlighted track  - 2 distributed and monetized tracks per month - 1 mastering** credit** per month

As an Artist subscriber, you’ll automatically receive monthly credits for these features, which reset every 30 days. These credits are redeemed automatically when you spotlight your tracks or distribute, monetize, master, or replace them. Learn More & Subscribe Today. #### What’s included in an Artist Pro subscription? If you’re an established artist ready to level up, Artist Pro gives you the tools to do it. Artist Invoices and Billing

Manage your subscription details, download invoices, and update your billing information directly from your account settings. #### Access your invoices Invoices are only available through a web browser; they cannot be accessed via the SoundCloud mobile app. 1. Using a computer, log in to your account. 2. Select the three dots in the top-right corner of the browser. 3. Select Subscription. 4. Scroll until you see Purchase History.

Update billing information

You can update your billing address and invoice details for future payments. Please note that past invoices cannot be amended. 1. Go to your Subscription settings. 2. Select Edit. 3. Select Manage plan to update your billing address or VAT information.

VAT and B2B exemptions (UK and EU)

Users in the UK or the EU can include a VAT number to claim business exemptions at checkout or by updating their settings. - During sign-up: Select the Add billing or VAT box. VAT numbers are verified in real-time, and any B2B exemptions will be applied at the final checkout screen. - For existing plans: Update your VAT number in your subscription settings. PayPal subscribers

If you paid via PayPal, your billing address is managed through your PayPal account, not SoundCloud. To change your billing address or other invoice details: 1. Cancel your current plan at soundcloud.com/you/subscriptions. 2. Wait for the plan to expire. 3. Once expired, visit the Checkout page to resubscribe. 4. During the new sign-up, select Add billing address to enter your updated information.

Nothing is deleted from your account. Your tracks, stats, and comments will be hidden but saved, and will be fully restored when you resubscribe.

What happens when I cancel my Artist subscription?

What happens if I downgrade from Artist Pro to a Basic plan?

When you downgrade from Artist Pro to Artist or Basic, your oldest uploads that exceed the subscription limit (180 minutes for Artist and 120 minutes for Basic) will be hidden from listeners. Subscriptions & Billing: Subscription Overview

Cancel your subscription

You have 30 days to renew your subscription to keep your content distributed and monetized.  If your content has already been taken down, it should be reinstated within 7 days of a successful subscription renewal. Sales Tax & VAT

Understanding how taxes affect your subscription helps you stay on top of your billing. Depending on where you’re located, taxes may be included in your subscription price or added at checkout. #### Are taxes included in my SoundCloud subscription? Whether taxes are included depends on your local laws: - EU, Switzerland, Norway, Australia, and New Zealand: VAT is already included in the advertised price. - United States: Some state and local governments require us to collect sales tax on top of the advertised price. You’ll see this reflected at the point of sale, which is why your receipt might show a slightly different total than the base rate.

You can always review exactly what you’re being charged by checking your receipts: 1. Sign in to your Subscriptions page. 2. Scroll down to Purchase history. 3. Select the order to view the receipt.

How do I make my account tax-exempt?

If you’re a non-profit or an eligible company, our support team can help you set up tax-exempt status. You’ll need to send a request with your exemption certificate and SoundCloud account details so we can verify your status. Once approved, future billings will be tax-exempt. To get started, click the chat bubble in the bottom-right corner to talk with our AI agent. #### Why am I being charged taxes if I have a valid VAT number in the EU? SoundCloud includes VAT on all subscriptions in the EU, but some users may be eligible for exemptions. Under the EU reverse charge mechanism, we can remove VAT from your invoice if you verify your VAT number during checkout. If you’re eligible, make sure to click “add VAT” and “billing information” during the sign-up process. Your number will be verified in real time, and the deduction will appear on the final checkout screen. Note: Users in the UK and Germany are not eligible for VAT-free purchases, as we are locally registered entities in these countries and must apply VAT as required. #### How do I change my VAT number and update my billing address? - Credit Card users: You can update your VAT and billing info on your subscription page. - PayPal users: Update your info directly within your PayPal account. Alternatively, you can cancel your subscription and resubscribe with your new details once the current period expires.

Will my future bills reflect the lower taxes in my new location?

Taxes are based on the location where you originally signed up. If you move to a new state or country, you’ll still be charged based on your original location. To update your tax calculation to reflect your new home, you’ll need to cancel your upcoming renewal and sign up again with your current address. Local taxes will then be applied based on the country and ZIP code you enter during checkout. #### Why didn’t you charge me tax before? If you’re seeing tax for the first time, it’s because we are now required by law to add sales tax to purchases in your area. This change is applied to accounts automatically, and rates may change based on local jurisdiction laws. #### How do you decide how much tax to charge me? Tax rates are determined by the laws in your region. SoundCloud determines your location based on the country and ZIP code you provided when you first purchased your subscription. If you’ve moved and need to update your payment details, please reach out to us via our AI agent. #### What happens if sales tax becomes required for my location? If laws change and we are required to add sales tax for your area, the change will be applied to your account automatically. You don’t need to take any action to keep using SoundCloud. #### I never agreed to that price. Can I get a refund? Because state or local governments determine when to subject purchases to additional sales tax, we do not offer refunds for changes in tax laws in your jurisdiction.

Billing & Payments

We offer two billing cycles to fit your needs: - Monthly: Pay as you go, cancel anytime. - Yearly: Pay once for the year at a lower overall cost.

The yearly plan is our best value. While it may be shown as a “per month” price on the pricing page to show you the savings, the full yearly amount is charged at checkout. Both monthly and yearly plans automatically renew. You can view your current plan and opt out of any automatic renewals by visiting your Subscriptions page and clicking on the Edit icon. Keeping your billing info current ensures your music and your listening stay uninterrupted. If you pay by credit or debit card: 1. Log in to SoundCloud on the web or open the app. 2. Go to your Subscriptions page. 3. Click Edit, then select Manage your billing. 4. Enter your new details and save your changes.

If you use PayPal or want to switch to it: To update your PayPal info—or to switch from a card to PayPal—you’ll need to let your current plan expire and then start a fresh one. Because of how PayPal works, these changes are handled as a new subscription. 1. Cancel your current plan at soundcloud.com/you/subscriptions. 2. Wait for your current plan to reach its expiration date. 3. Once it expires, visit your Subscriptions page and choose your desired plan. 4. Enter your updated details and select your preferred payment method.

Note for Artist Pro creators: If your plan expires before you renew, don’t sweat it. Your tracks stay exactly where they are—nothing is deleted. If you go over the free upload limit, your older tracks will simply be hidden from the public, but you can still see them on your Tracks page. They’ll reappear as soon as your new plan is active. Note on already canceled plans: If you have already canceled any upcoming billing, the option to edit your info won’t be available. You’ll simply need to purchase a new plan after your current subscription expires. #### Manage Your Subscription There isn’t a way to change the date your monthly payment is taken at the moment. If it’s more convenient to have payment taken on another date, please opt out of automatic renewals in your account’s Subscriptions page or via Apple by clicking on the Edit icon. Your subscription will continue for the remainder of the 30-day period, and then you will be downgraded to the Basic plan. You can then choose to subscribe again through your Subscriptions page. It is not possible to pause a subscription. However, you can opt out of automatic renewals by going to your account Subscriptions page** and clicking on the Edit** icon. Follow the prompt “Don’t want to renew your plan?” to confirm that you would like to stop your recurring payment. When you cancel your subscription, please note that previous pricing will not apply to your new purchase. #### Still have questions? What happens if I downgrade from Artist Pro to a Basic plan? Vinyl Distribution: Building Your Vinyl Distribution Release

Artwork guidelines for vinyl distribution

Your vinyl artwork must be square, 2000x2000px minimum (though we recommend 3000x3000px), RGB color space, and 300dpi. You’ll also need to make sure your file type is a PNG or JPEG that’s under 300MB. Make sure you’re uploading high-quality images fully owned by you. Ensure there is no offensive imagery, doesn’t violate copyright laws (think: no logos, characters, or photos of anyone you don’t own 100% of the rights to), and isn’t a scaled-up version of a smaller image. You’ll upload a file for the front cover of your record, but we’ll generate the back with your track details and other metadata, the spine, and the sticker on the record itself.

Can I recreate my digital distribution release on vinyl?

While you may want to distribute your next album or project on both digital platforms like Spotify, Apple Music, YouTube Music, and more, there will be some key differences to keep in mind when you build a release for physical distribution on vinyl. Some things to keep in mind: 1. Your track list may need to change. There is a limit to both the number of tracks and the length of your album when distributing on vinyl. 2. Audio guidelines will be different. As you can imagine, printing your music on vinyl may sound different than how it may sound on a digital streaming platform. When we’re reviewing your vinyl release, we may need to request different audio files to ensure the sound will work on vinyl. 3. Your artwork may need to change. If you’re using a smaller artwork file that might work great on digital platforms, keep in mind that it might look blurry or distorted once it’s in a larger format.

As with any type of distribution, it’s imperative that you provide us with accurate information about any licenses you’ve purchased for your music, even if it’s just a small sample or drum beat. When in doubt, disclose to us if you’ve used anything you didn’t personally play on an instrument or write with no other tools. You’ll be able to upload documentation when creating your release.

Licensing Information for Vinyl Distribution

We won’t be able to approve any content you’re not sharing proper documentation for. You must own and/or control all content, or have the necessary rights for physical (vinyl) distribution. It’s extremely important that if you’ve used anything you didn’t create entirely, whether that be a beat, a stem, or any small piece of content you’ve licensed, you need to upload licensing agreements for everything. Make sure you’re uploading documentation for them - it’ll make your review process simpler if you start by uploading everything you can. We also want to make sure all the right people are getting paid when you’re distributing on vinyl. We’ll ask you for all of your contributors’ publishing information, including their full names, which MRO and PRO they’re registered with, as well as any registration numbers you have. You want to get this right, so if you know this information, make sure to include it.

Music publishing for vinyl release

Music publishing refers to the legal rights granted to songwriters and other composition rightsholders. Royalties must be paid whenever these rights are exploited. Basic copyright law protects songwriters by giving them exclusive rights to grant or deny the reproduction, distribution, or performance of their original songs. When original music is written, and such songs are registered with collection societies, songwriters will be paid performance and mechanical royalties for the use of their music, which includes digital streaming, television, radio, live concerts, physical products, and more. Therefore, including accurate songwriter information with your vinyl release will ensure songwriters are paid. #### Why is publishing information needed for my vinyl release? When you’re building your vinyl release, you’ll edit the details for each track you add. One of the questions we’ll ask is if you own the publishing rights to your track. For each of the songwriters, you’ll want to include the name and registration number for both the Mechanical Rights Organization (MRO) and the Performing Rights Organization (PRO). This ensures that the right people get credited and paid. #### What is a Mechanical Rights Organization (MRO)? A Mechanical Rights Organization (MRO) is responsible for the administration of mechanical licenses, and they collect and pay out mechanical royalties to songwriters and publishers when songs are reproduced, including physical products, digital streaming, downloads, or television. #### What is a Performing Rights Organization (PRO)? A Performing Rights Organization (PRO) is responsible for collecting income on behalf of songwriters and music publishers when a song is publicly broadcast or performed. Public performances include digital streaming, plays on television or radio, in clubs and restaurants, on websites, or on other broadcasting systems.

Preparing Audio Files to Distribute on Vinyl

Our vinyl partner, elasticStage will transfer your content onto vinyl as faithfully as possible, preserving the sound of your uploaded files without making creative or unnecessary changes. Vinyl, as a format, has physical limitations that are not present for CD or streaming formats and therefore, some considerations should be taken into account when preparing your music for vinyl. While we do not offer a dedicated vinyl mastering service, here are some tips to get the most out of your record: #### Track Layout The physical limitations of vinyl are most audible towards the centre of the disc, typically experienced as loss of treble and an increase in distortion. Some commonly used practices to mitigate this include: - Placing songs with more treble at the beginning of a side, and quieter tracks towards the end of a side. - Applying a de-esser to reduce excessive high frequencies, for example, reducing sibilance and aggressive cymbals.

Playback Compatibility

Different turntables and playback cartridges can have different characteristics. Some common practices to optimize playback compatibility include: - Filtering out content above and below the human audible spectrum. - Converting bass content to mono. - Avoiding long periods of negative phase correlation. - Avoiding sudden changes in amplitude such as clicks and pops, for example noises from bad edit points or dropouts.

Loudness

All vinyl products are limited by space constraints, leading to a trade-off between duration, bass and loudness. We have a default maximum playback level at which we produce our vinyl, but in order to work within these constraints the playback level will decrease if more space is needed. Longer or bass-heavy content takes up more space per side, while quiet or shorter content takes up less space. At present, we maintain the loudness level relationship between all tracks per side to preserve the intended listening experience. Once you have everything set up, we strongly recommend purchasing a personal copy of your vinyl, especially if you’re new to producing content for this format. If you encounter any issues, we recommend reviewing this FAQ to ensure you’ve made the relevant audio adjustments.

Requirements for vinyl vs digital distribution

Vinyl comes with a few key differences you’ll want to account for when building your release: #### Track/Release Duration:  Distributing for physical media means that there are stricter rules on the duration of your release. Each release will have two sides (A and B), which can include up to 8 tracks per side, each side no longer than 22:00 minutes of music. #### Audio Guidelines:  Because your approved release would be printed on vinyl, there are a few more audio considerations to keep in mind. We’ve created this article for additional guidelines that will help you prepare your tracks. #### Content Ownership/Proper Licensing We won’t be able to approve any content you’re not sharing proper documentation for. You must own and/or control all content, or have the necessary rights for physical distribution. It’s extremely important that if you’ve used anything you didn’t create entirely, whether that be a beat, a stem, or any small piece of content you’ve licensed, you need to upload licensing agreements for everything. Make sure you’re uploading documentation for them - it’ll make your review process simpler if you start by uploading everything you can. #### Publishing Information We want to make sure all the right people are getting paid when you’re distributing on vinyl. We’ll ask you for all of your contributors’ publishing information, including their full names, which MRO and PRO they’re registered with, as well as any registration numbers you have. You want to get this right, so if you know this information, make sure to include it. #### Artwork Guidelines Vinyl distribution has similar guidelines when it comes to artwork. We recommend your file be 3000x3000px, though we can accept files with a minimum of 2000x2000px. Your file must also be in the RGB color space, 300dpi, and less than 300 MB. Your artwork should not include any offensive imagery or contain text that doesn’t match the metadata you’ve already entered in your release details. Similar to the music you may have added to your release, you must outright own or have proper licensing for artwork you didn’t create yourself. The spine and back cover on your vinyl will be autogenerated for you. You’ll see a preview of these autogenerated elements when you’re uploading your cover artwork.

What is an ISWC and how do I find it?

An International Standard Musical Work Code (ISWC) is the global standard for identifying unique musical works. Different from an ISRC, an ISWC relates to the specific composition, or written lyrics, rather than the recording.

What is an MRO or a PRO?

A Mechanical Rights Organization (MRO) is responsible for the administration of mechanical licenses, and they collect and payout mechanical royalties to songwriters and publishers when songs are reproduced and this includes physical products, digital streaming, downloads or television. A Performing Rights Organization (PRO) is responsible for collecting income on behalf of songwriters and music publishers when a song is publicly broadcast or performed. Public performances include digital streaming, plays on television or radio, in clubs and restaurants, on websites, or on other broadcasting systems.

What should I enter in the “P-Line” and “C-Line” fields?

In copyright law, the P Line is specific to musical works (the P stands for “phonogram”) and is represented by ℗. The purpose of this symbol is to indicate that legal rights are held for a sound recording and to identify the owner of those rights. You may have seen this printed on an LP sleeve or CD booklet accompanied by the year that the work was first released and the name of the owner of the sound recording. For digital music the P Line is included within the metadata associated with an audio file. The © symbol, or C Line, is used in relation to the underlying musical composition and lyrics and also to indicate copyright in a range of creative works other than sound recordings. In the context of music it is used to denote rights protection for the cover art or written material included within an album, like liner notes. Because the P Line and C Line refer to different rights you will always see them written separately, even when the owner of the rights is the same.

Vinyl Distribution: Managing Approved Vinyl Distribution Releases

How can I take down a release that’s live on vinyl?

If you’d like to take down a release on vinyl, reach out to our support bot and include the release name and EAN for your vinyl release. We’ll confirm with you once the takedown has been processed. Keep in mind that taking down a vinyl release does not automatically mean a digital version of the release will also be taken down. Find more information on editing or taking down your digital release here.

How do I make changes to a live vinyl release?

At this time, if you need to make any changes to your release, you’d need to contact us to request the release be taken down - once the release is taken down, you can recreate the release and make any necessary changes. Reach out to our support bot and include the release name and EAN of your vinyl release and we’ll let you know once the takedown has processed. Keep in mind that any orders that are already in progress would still be sent and would not include any of your edits.

Vinyl Pricing and Shipping

When your vinyl release is approved, you or your fans can purchase any quantity of your 12” Vinyl. Each vinyl will be $39.40 USD, but exact pricing will depend on your shipping country, which you can set at the bottom of any release page on elasticStage: (image: Screenshot 2025-09-22 at 4.21.45 PM.png) Before you buy any records on elasticStage, you’ll see the date by which elasticStage will aim to ship them. Shipping fees will be calculated at checkout and will depend on your location for exact pricing. For any order-related issues or questions, please reachout to elasticStage directly, as they’ll be processing the orders directly. You can find details about elasticStage’s pricing and royalty splits here.

Vinyl Distribution: Reviewing Your Vinyl Distribution Release

What happens on my Release Date for vinyl distribution?

Once you receive confirmation from us that your vinyl release is approved, you’ll find a link in your email, and on your Artist Studio page to your record on elasticStage. Keep in mind that the link won’t show anything until your release date. On your release date, send that link to any and everyone to have your fans purchase your vinyl record. For more information on ordering and shipping through our partner, elasticStage, check out their Help Center here.

What happens when my vinyl distribution release is in review?

Once you’ve submitted your vinyl release to us, our review team will take a look at everything and request any edits or clarifications from you. Keep in mind that this might take a bit of time, so whenever you can, please make sure you’re submitting your release well in advance of your release date. Requesting more information from you is very common and ensures that all of your information is accurate, and we have all of the information we need to ensure you are the rightful owner or licensee of the content.

Miscellaneous

How do I take part in vinyl distribution with SoundCloud?

SoundCloud now offers on-demand vinyl distribution, allowing you to turn your digital releases into physical records with zero upfront costs and no minimum order quantities. We handle the manufacturing, storefront, and global shipping—you focus on the music. #### Quick Navigation - How to Get Started - How On-Demand Works - Technical Specs & Assets - Earnings & Payouts

How to Get Started

To begin your vinyl journey, follow these steps in your SoundCloud for Artists dashboard: 1. Navigate to your Artist Studio. 2. Click the Vinyl Distribution tab in the navigation bar. 3. Select “Create New Release” and follow the prompts to select your tracks and design your sleeve.

How On-Demand Works

Unlike traditional vinyl pressing, which requires ordering hundreds of copies upfront, our service is On-Demand. - The Storefront: We create a dedicated sales page for your record. - No Inventory: We only press a record when a fan buys one. This means no boxes of unsold vinyl in your garage and no financial risk to you. - Fulfillment: We handle the high-quality pressing and ship the record directly to your fan’s door, anywhere in the world.

Technical Specs & Assets

Vinyl requires different assets than digital distribution. To pass the review process, ensure your materials meet these requirements: - Audio: High-quality WAV files are required. We recommend 24-bit/44.1kHz or higher for the best analog translation. - Artwork: You will need a high-resolution 12-inch jacket design. Our builder provides templates to ensure your spine text and bleeds are aligned correctly. - Track Length: Remember that a standard 12” vinyl typically holds about 18–22 minutes of music per side. If your album is longer, you may need to split it into two vinyl releases.

Earnings & Payouts

You earn a profit on every record sold. - Base Pricing: Each 12” vinyl costs $39.40 USD. Prices may vary slightly by currency and shipping location. For details on on-demand pricing, see our guide here. - Shipping & Delivery: Shipping fees are calculated at checkout based on the fan’s location. Before a purchase is finalized on elasticStage, you or your fans will see an estimated shipping date. - Tracking: All vinyl sales are tracked in your Earnings dashboard alongside your digital royalties. - Payouts: Profits from vinyl sales follow the same payout rules and minimums as your digital earnings. Learn more about getting paid here.

Ready to press? Head over to the Vinyl Distribution dashboard to start your draft. If you have questions about a specific order, please contact our AI Agent with your order number.

How do I upload content that contains work created by someone else?

You almost always need permission to share content that has been created by someone else.  This is true for any content created by someone else, including DJ sets, remixes, and mashups. Please bear in mind that purchasing a track or downloading it from another source does not grant the rights to publish the track, either in an original or edited way, without explicit permission. Additionally, an unreleased track is not free to use.  It is the creation of a piece of music–not its release–that creates copyright protection.  Unreleased music is still protected by copyright.  We have a zero tolerance policy when it comes to the unauthorized publications of unreleased music on SoundCloud and your account will be permanently terminated if reported for a leak. We will be required to take down the content if it is reported to us for infringement in order to be in compliance with copyright law. If you have obtained the proper permission from the rightsholder to use the content, please be sure to have this permission documented and available in case an issue occurs.  If the content you are using was released on a label, then this permission usually must come from the label who is typically the rightsholder for the master recording.  Permission from the artist themselves will usually be insufficient. If your properly licensed content is blocked when uploading, or you believe your use falls under fair use or a copyright exception, we encourage you to file a dispute to let us know the details of your situation. Is this also true for covers and remade beats? Yes, you must obtain permission from the original creators if you would like to use their composition.  While you may be performing all elements of the track or using a remade beat, the songwriter(s) still have copyright protection over the composition and therefore the composition must be properly licensed. Can I use a “free” or “non-profit” beat that I found somewhere? There are “free,” “non-profit,” and “free for profit” beats that can be found in various places online.  This type of content is difficult for use on SoundCloud for a variety of reasons. First, the source of the beat may not be the rightsholder. For example, the track may be an instrumental from a popular track with the vocals removed and put online as a “free” beat. We have no way to confirm if the uploader has permission from the original creator to use the instrumental themselves or the ability to grant permissions to other creators for use of the beat. The “free” instrumental might also be a remade instrumental, but we cannot confirm if they have properly licensed the composition, as needed when performing a cover, and secured the rights to grant such permission to others. Second, the beat may be mislabeled. The creator may have labeled the instrumental as “free” or “non-profit” but expects that the work would be leased/licensed. Given the difficulty of confirming ownership for an instrumental found somewhere online without documentation from the rightsholder, we cannot accept as a defense to your blocked content that the work used was “free” or “non-profit.” If you would like to use one of these types of works, we recommend getting in touch with the original creator to request permission and obtaining documentation of this permission. What about works in the public domain? The term “public domain” refers to creative works that are no longer subject to copyright protection. Most often, works enter the public domain because their copyright term has expired.  A work in the public domain can be used by anyone without obtaining further permission.  A work is not public domain simply because it has been released publicly. Copyright protection typically expires 70 years after the author’s death, so works must be quite old before they enter the public domain. The most common example of a public domain work is a piece of classical music.  Keep in mind, though, that while the compositions in those cases may have passed into the public domain and can be recorded or performed publicly without a license, there may still be copyright protection on contemporary recordings of the work.  For example, Für Elise by Beethoven is no longer subject to copyright, but the recording of a modern symphony’s performance of Für Elise likely is subject to copyright. As a result, your upload may be blocked for being similar to the copyright-protected recording.  When uploading your personal recordings of works in the public domain, please file a dispute if the content is blocked to let us know the details of your issue. Disclaimer: We do not give legal advice. The above information is provided for informational purposes only.  Consult a qualified attorney in your area for more information about copyright and your work.
